paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: What additional non-perturbative information about boundary and defect conformal field theories can supersymmetry provide, including through techniques such as supersymmetric localization?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{CFT}_d$ be a $d$-dimensional conformal field theory and let $\mathcal{D}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a conformal boundary or a conformal defect of dimension $p<d$ that preserves the subgroup $SO(p+1,1)\times SO(d-p)$ of the conformal group. The defect data of $(\mathrm{CFT}_d,\mathcal{D})$ consist of:
\begin{itemize}
\item the bulk one-point functions $\langle \mathcal{O}_\Delta(x)\rangle_\mathcal{D} = a_\mathcal{O}/|x_\perp|^\Delta$ for bulk primaries $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$,
\item the spectrum $\{\widehat{\Delta}_i\}$ of defect primary operators and their bulk-to-defect coupling coefficients $b_{\mathcal{O}\,\widehat{\mathcal{O}}}$,
\item the defect conformal anomaly coefficients (e.g.\ for $p=2$ the central charges $b$ and $d_1,d_2$, and for $p=4$ the anomalies $a_\mathcal{D}$, $c_\mathcal{D}$, $d_{1,2}$),
\item the defect free energy / $g$-function and its monotonicity along defect RG flows.
\end{itemize}

Now suppose in addition that the bulk theory and the defect together preserve some amount of supersymmetry, so that supersymmetric-localization techniques apply (in particular, that the path integral on a suitable curved background such as $S^d$, $S^p\times \mathbb{H}^{d-p}$, or $\mathbb{HS}^d$ in the presence of $\mathcal{D}$ can be reduced to a finite-dimensional matrix integral).

Determine which of the non-perturbative defect data above can be computed exactly using supersymmetric localization in the presence of the defect $\mathcal{D}$. Concretely, formulate and answer the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For which classes of supersymmetric defects (e.g.\ BPS Wilson/'t Hooft lines, surface operators, BPS boundaries and interfaces of class $D5$/$NS5$ type, codimension-two monodromy defects) does localization on $S^d$ produce a closed-form matrix model whose observables compute defect one-point functions $a_\mathcal{O}$ of BPS bulk primaries?
\item Which defect anomaly coefficients (such as the $b$-anomaly of $2d$ defects in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories, or the $4d$ defect anomalies in $6d$ $(2,0)$ theories) can be extracted from the localized partition function or its derivatives, and through which precise formulas?
\item Can the defect free energy (or $g$-function) and the corresponding monotonicity ($b$-theorem, defect $a$-theorem) be proven non-perturbatively for supersymmetric defects via localization?
\item Can localization, possibly combined with integrability or the conformal bootstrap, determine non-protected defect CFT data such as anomalous dimensions of non-BPS defect primaries and bulk-to-defect OPE coefficients at finite coupling?
\end{enumerate}
category_tag: Boundary and defect conformal field theory
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: supersymmetric localization yields exact matrix-model expressions for one-point functions of BPS operators in the presence of D5-type interfaces in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, exact bulk-defect OPE data for the 1/2-BPS Wilson line (in combination with the Quantum Spectral Curve), and exact results for protected correlators in 3d $\mathcal{N}\ge 4$ defect setups. Defect $b$- and $a$-anomalies have been computed via localization in several supersymmetric examples, and a general defect $a$-theorem framework using $a$-maximization has been developed. However, a complete non-perturbative determination of all defect CFT data (including non-BPS spectra and general anomaly monotonicity theorems) via localization remains open; the broad question is therefore only partially resolved.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: How do the double-trace interfaces described holographically fuse with one another, and can that fusion process be analyzed systematically using the mixed-boundary-value and harmonic-analysis tools proposed in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a holographic setup in which two conformal field theories CFT_+ and CFT_- are related by deformation by a double-trace scalar operator, and are joined along a codimension-one conformal interface (a "double-trace interface") realized in the bulk by imposing mixed Dirichlet–Neumann boundary conditions for a scalar field on the two sides of an asymptotically AdS geometry. Such interfaces can be analyzed by (i) solving the resulting mixed boundary-value problem for the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, and (ii) applying harmonic analysis on warped-product bulk geometries (so that the wave equation separates) to compute interface two-point functions and the operator spectrum localized on the interface.

Two parallel codimension-one interfaces of this type can be brought together and "fused" into a single effective interface. Develop a systematic framework, using the mixed boundary-value-problem and harmonic-analysis tools above, to describe the fusion of two such double-trace interfaces. Specifically:

1. Define the fusion of two parallel double-trace interfaces I_{a} and I_{b} (associated with double-trace deformation parameters a and b respectively) as the limit in which their separation tends to zero, and characterize the resulting interface I_{a*b} via its bulk boundary conditions and its action on bulk propagators and on the spectrum of interface operators.
2. Derive a closed-form fusion rule expressing the parameter (or boundary condition data) of I_{a*b} in terms of those of I_a and I_b, and verify associativity of the resulting fusion product.
3. Determine how the interface two-point functions and the spectrum of operators living on the fused interface are obtained from those of the constituent interfaces through the harmonic-analysis decomposition.
status_search_result: A search shows continued activity on double-trace interfaces and mixed boundary conditions in AdS/CFT (e.g., the originating "Double Trace Interfaces" work and later developments on mixed boundary conditions and double-trace-like deformations in celestial/wedge holography), but no source explicitly presents a complete, systematic fusion analysis of double-trace interfaces using the proposed mixed boundary-value and harmonic-analysis methods. The status of the specific fusion program therefore appears unresolved based on the available evidence.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: What are the explicit correction terms, beyond the leading linear-in-temperature contribution, to the low-temperature specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger-liquid environment, and do their exponents indeed match the exponents inferred earlier from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a side-coupled quantum-dot model defined as follows. A one-dimensional interacting electron system in the Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid universality class, characterized by a Luttinger parameter K (with K=1 being the noninteracting point and K≠1 corresponding to repulsive or attractive electron–electron interactions), is coupled by a tunneling amplitude t to a single localized level (the quantum dot) of energy ε_d, where the dot is attached at a single point of the lead but does not interrupt the lead (side-coupled geometry). Let the partition function and free energy F(T) be defined for this Hamiltonian at temperature T, and let the specific heat per unit length of the lead, with the bulk Luttinger-liquid contribution subtracted, be denoted C_d(T) = -T ∂²F_d/∂T², where F_d is the impurity contribution to the free energy.

It is known that, in the low-temperature regime T → 0, C_d(T) admits an asymptotic expansion whose leading term is linear in T, i.e. C_d(T) ≃ γ T + (subleading corrections). A renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation n_d(T) at low temperatures yields a set of anomalous power-law exponents {α_i(K)} (functions of the Luttinger parameter K) that govern the subleading temperature dependence of n_d(T) about its zero-temperature value.

Determine explicitly the subleading correction terms to C_d(T) beyond the leading γT contribution as T → 0, expressing them as a sum of power-law terms T^{β_j(K)} with explicit coefficients depending on K, t, and ε_d. In particular, decide whether the set of exponents {β_j(K)} appearing in the specific heat coincides with the set of exponents {α_i(K)} obtained from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation.
category_tag: Luttinger liquids and quantum impurity models
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published work explicitly computing the subleading low-temperature corrections to the specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger liquid and matching their exponents against those obtained from the RG analysis of the dot occupation. Existing literature on related models (embedded dots, Kondo impurities in Luttinger liquids) discusses the leading Fermi-liquid–like linear-in-T behavior and notes anomalous power-law subleading exponents controlled by the Luttinger parameter K, but does not appear to provide the explicit calculation requested. The status therefore appears to be open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can one develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of sine-Gordon scattering off a non-integrable boundary, despite the fact that the boundary interaction excites many additional modes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon field theory on the half-line x ≤ 0, with field φ(x,t) governed by the bulk equation
   ∂_t^2 φ − ∂_x^2 φ + sin φ = 0,
together with the one-parameter family of Robin boundary conditions at x = 0,
   ∂_x φ(0,t) = M sin(φ(0,t)/2),
where M ∈ ℝ is a real parameter. For generic M this boundary condition breaks the integrability of the bulk theory, and the scattering of an incoming antikink (or kink) off the boundary excites not only the soliton's translational zero mode but also a host of additional degrees of freedom (boundary-localized modes, breathers, and continuum radiation), so that the outgoing state may consist of various combinations of an antikink, a kink, and one or more breathers depending on the incident velocity and on M.

Problem. Develop an effective collective-coordinate description of antikink/kink scattering off this non-integrable boundary that quantitatively captures the observed reflection, transmission into breathers, and resonance windows. Concretely, exhibit a finite-dimensional reduction of the field dynamics — specifying a moduli ansatz φ(x,t) ≈ Φ(x; q_1(t), …, q_n(t)) and the resulting effective Lagrangian L_eff(q, q̇) — whose solutions reproduce, with controlled accuracy, the scattering outcomes of the full PDE for a wide range of M and incident velocities, including the resonant energy exchange between the soliton translational mode and the modes excited at the boundary.
status_search_result: Boundary scattering of sine-Gordon solitons under non-integrable Robin boundary conditions has been studied numerically (e.g., showing intricate resonance structures and breather production), and collective-coordinate methods have been successful in related impurity and deformed sine-Gordon problems. However, no published collective-coordinate reduction is reported to give an effective and quantitatively accurate description of sine-Gordon scattering off the non-integrable Robin boundary, due to the many additional modes excited there. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model in 1+1 dimensions, defined on the half-line $x \le 0$ by the bulk Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bulk}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t \phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x \phi)^2 + \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\bigl(\cos(\beta\phi) - 1\bigr),$$
where $\phi(t,x)$ is a real scalar field, $m>0$ is a mass parameter, and $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ is the coupling. At the boundary $x=0$, impose a boundary potential
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bdy}} = -V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi(t,0)),$$
where $V_{\text{bdy}}$ is chosen so that the resulting boundary condition does not preserve the infinite tower of higher-spin local conserved charges of the bulk theory (i.e., the boundary condition is non-integrable, lying outside the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family $V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi) = M\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi-\phi_0)\bigr)$).

The problems are:

(a) Provide a precise quantum-field-theoretic description of this half-line sine-Gordon model with non-integrable boundary potential: specify the Hilbert space, the renormalized Hamiltonian, the spectrum of asymptotic particle states (solitons, antisolitons, breathers, and possible boundary bound states), and the appropriate notion of reflection amplitude when bulk-integrability-preserving boundary Yang–Baxter relations fail.

(b) Determine to what extent techniques developed for quantum integrability on the half-line — such as the boundary bootstrap, reflection matrices satisfying the boundary Yang–Baxter equation, the truncated conformal space approach, and form-factor perturbation theory — can be adapted to quantitatively describe the breakdown of integrability induced by such non-integrable boundary terms, including the computation of corrections to reflection amplitudes, decay widths of formerly stable boundary bound states, and the modification of finite-size spectra.
status_search_result: Existing literature treats integrable boundary conditions of the sine-Gordon model (Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov, boundary bootstrap, half-line reflection matrices) and develops form-factor perturbation theory for non-integrable bulk perturbations, plus an asymptotic Lagrangian framework for general non-integrable boundary QFT. However, no comprehensive QFT description of sine-Gordon with a generic non-integrable boundary, nor a complete adaptation of integrability techniques to quantify the breaking, has been established; the question remains open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?
self_contained_problem:
Consider two-dimensional conformal field theories defined on surfaces with boundary. Two specific fermionic/superconformal theories of interest are:

(i) the free Majorana fermion CFT (central charge c = 1/2), and

(ii) the third unitary N = 1 super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, i.e. the unitary superconformal minimal model with central charge c = c(m) for m = 5 in the family
   c(m) = 3/2 · (1 − 8/(m(m+2))),
which is the supersymmetric analogue of a unitary Virasoro minimal model and contains fields organised under the N = 1 super-Virasoro algebra.

For each of these theories, conformal (and, where relevant, superconformal-preserving) boundary conditions can be specified by boundary states |B⟩ in the closed-string Hilbert space satisfying gluing conditions of Cardy/Ishibashi type, together with an integrality (Cardy) condition on the open-string spectrum.

Problem. Derive the complete set of (elementary) conformal boundary conditions, together with their boundary states and the corresponding annulus/open-string partition functions, for the free Majorana fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, by either:

(a) a direct first-principles construction (for example, solving the Cardy/Ishibashi gluing and integrality conditions intrinsically in the fermionic/superconformal category of representations), or

(b) an adaptation of the classifying-algebra and TFT-with-defects methodology used to construct boundary conditions for bosonic rational CFTs from a modular tensor category and a special symmetric Frobenius algebra, suitably extended to the fermionic/super setting.

Produce in either approach an explicit list of boundary states, verify the Cardy condition, and exhibit the boundary structure constants.
category_tag: Boundary conditions in superconformal field theory
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Runkel and collaborators (notably "Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras", JHEP 06 (2020) 025) develops fermionic classifying algebras for boundaries, defects and interfaces and applies the framework to the fermionic Ising model (free Majorana fermion) and the fermionic tri-critical Ising model (first unitary N=1 super-minimal model). This addresses the methodology for the free fermion and lower super-minimal models, but a complete first-principles or classifying-algebra derivation specifically for SVIR3 does not appear to be explicitly carried out in the literature found. The problem therefore appears partially solved.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can one find a closed tree-level formula for one-point functions of the closely related SO(5)-symmetric D3-D7 defect conformal field theory when the full scalar SO(6) sector is considered, beyond the already understood chiral-primary case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the four-dimensional defect conformal field theory obtained from N=4 super Yang–Mills theory with gauge group SU(N) by introducing a codimension-one defect dual to the probe D3–D7 brane intersection that preserves an SO(5) R-symmetry subgroup of SO(6). On one side of the defect, three of the six real scalars Φ_i (i=1,…,6) of N=4 SYM acquire classical, position-dependent vacuum expectation values built from a fuzzy-four-sphere construction with k units of background flux, while the remaining three scalars vanish classically; on the other side all scalars vanish.

Tree-level one-point functions of single-trace scalar operators of the form
   O(x) = tr( Φ_{i_1} Φ_{i_2} ⋯ Φ_{i_L} )(x)
in this background can be computed as overlaps between an SO(6) integrable spin-chain Bethe eigenstate of length L and a matrix product state |MPS_k⟩ encoding the classical defect solution.

Problem. Find a closed-form expression, valid for arbitrary chain length L, arbitrary set of magnon rapidities {u_j} solving the SO(6) Bethe equations, and arbitrary flux parameter k, for the overlap
   ⟨MPS_k | {u_j} ⟩ / ⟨{u_j} | {u_j}⟩^{1/2},
i.e. for the tree-level one-point functions of all scalar operators in the full SO(6) sector of the SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 defect CFT, going beyond the chiral-primary (BPS) case for which a closed formula is already known.
category_tag: Defect CFT one-point functions and integrability
status_search_result: For the D3–D5 defect CFT a closed determinant formula for tree-level scalar one-point functions in the full SO(6) sector is known. For the SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 system, partial results are available: closed expressions have been obtained for chiral primaries and for restricted SO(6) eigenstates (e.g. operators in specific subsectors), and the relevant matrix product state has been shown to satisfy integrability criteria, but a fully closed tree-level overlap formula valid for all SO(6) Bethe eigenstates and all flux parameters k does not appear to have been established in the literature.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: How should one incorporate finite-string-tension corrections, i.e. 1/λ corrections, into the large-N, large-'t Hooft-coupling analysis of four-point correlators in AdS5 × S5 supergravity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider type IIB string theory on the AdS_5 × S^5 background with N units of self-dual five-form flux, dual to four-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory with gauge group SU(N) and 't Hooft coupling λ = g_YM^2 N. In the planar limit N → ∞ with λ fixed, four-point correlation functions of single-trace half-BPS superprimary operators (e.g., the stress-tensor multiplet superprimary O_2 of dimension 2) admit a strong-coupling expansion

⟨O O O O⟩ = G_sugra + λ^{-3/2} G_{R^4} + λ^{-5/2} G_{D^4 R^4} + λ^{-3} G_{D^6 R^4} + ⋯,

where G_sugra is the tree-level type IIB supergravity contribution on AdS_5 × S^5 and the subleading terms encode finite-string-tension (α'/L^2 ∼ λ^{-1/2}) higher-derivative stringy corrections.

Develop a systematic procedure to compute the 1/λ corrections G_{R^4}, G_{D^4 R^4}, G_{D^6 R^4}, … to four-point correlators of half-BPS operators at leading order in 1/N. Concretely: determine, in Mellin space or position space, the precise form of the holographic four-point amplitudes induced by the higher-derivative interactions (R^4 and its descendants) on AdS_5 × S^5, fix all coefficients consistently with superconformal Ward identities, crossing symmetry, and the flat-space α'-expansion of the type IIB four-graviton S-matrix, and identify the resulting anomalous dimensions and OPE coefficients of double-trace operators exchanged in the OPE.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on incorporating 1/λ corrections to four-point correlators in AdS_5 × S^5. The leading R^4, D^4 R^4, and D^6 R^4 corrections to the stress-tensor multiplet four-point function have been computed in Mellin space using a combination of crossing symmetry, the flat-space limit, and supersymmetric localization constraints (Chester, Pufu, Yin and others). Higher-order α' corrections, full Kaluza–Klein generalizations, and a complete all-orders systematic procedure remain active areas of research, so the broader program is partially solved rather than completely settled.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can the bootstrap analysis of conformal field theories on real projective space be extended to holographic or otherwise strongly coupled theories such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory, and if so does it agree with the corresponding holographic predictions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a conformal field theory (CFT) defined on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$, obtained as the quotient of $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or $S^d$) by the antipodal involution $x \mapsto -x/|x|^2$. On such an unorientable background, one-point functions of bulk primary operators $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$ are not forced to vanish; conformal symmetry fixes them to take the form
$$\langle \mathcal{O}_\Delta(x)\rangle_{\mathbb{RP}^d} = \frac{A_{\mathcal{O}}}{(1+|x|^2)^{\Delta}},$$
and two-point functions of bulk primaries depend nontrivially on a cross-ratio invariant under the antipodal map. The "projective-space bootstrap" consists of constraints obtained by expanding such two-point functions in two distinct OPE channels (the bulk OPE and the image-point/crosscap channel) and demanding consistency, yielding equations that determine the coefficients $A_{\mathcal{O}}$ in terms of the bulk CFT data.

Problem. Extend this projective-space bootstrap program to strongly coupled or holographic conformal field theories — in particular to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory placed on $\mathbb{RP}^4$, and to two-dimensional Liouville theory placed on $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Compute the crosscap one-point coefficients $A_{\mathcal{O}}$ (for example, for $\tfrac{1}{2}$-BPS operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM) and the corresponding two-point functions, and determine whether the resulting bootstrap predictions agree with the holographic computations obtained from the appropriate gravitational dual (e.g. type IIB supergravity on $AdS_5\times S^5$ with an orientifold-like involution dual to $\mathbb{RP}^4$).
category_tag: conformal bootstrap on real projective space
status_search_result: Subsequent work has carried out this program for $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM on $\mathbb{RP}^4$: a holographic dual was constructed in 5d $\mathcal{N}=8$ gauged supergravity and uplifted to a 1/2-BPS type IIB solution (Wang, 2022, JHEP 2023), and bootstrap-based computations of two-point functions of 1/2-BPS operators at strong coupling were performed and found consistent with the holographic predictions (PRL 133, 201602, 2024). The Liouville-on-$\mathbb{RP}^2$ side does not appear to be fully addressed in the same comparative way, so the broader question is partially resolved.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A quasi Riemann surface is a structure Q (in the sense of Friedan) that abstracts the properties of spaces of integral 0-currents on a Riemann surface: it carries a commutative associative addition with cancellation, a distinguished asymptotic cone of "effective" elements, a complete weak metric, and additional structure (integral j-currents for j = 0, 1, 2, 3) sufficient to define a Jacobian J(Q), namely the complex torus built from the homology in the middle dimension of Q.

For an ordinary 2-dimensional conformal space (Riemann surface) Σ, let D^int_0(Σ) denote the space of integral 0-currents on Σ (formal integer linear combinations of points, i.e. integral 0-cycles, with the topology and metric induced from currents). The space D^int_0(Σ) is a quasi Riemann surface, and its Jacobian coincides with the classical Jacobian variety of Σ.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic, as a quasi Riemann surface, to D^int_0(Σ) for some 2-dimensional conformal space Σ whose Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q). If the statement holds, give an explicit construction of Σ from Q together with the isomorphism Q ≅ D^int_0(Σ).
status_search_result: The conjecture is due to Friedan in his "Quasi Riemann surfaces" papers (2017). Friedan himself characterizes the conjecture as speculative with no supporting evidence at the time of writing. No subsequent literature appears to establish or refute it, so it remains open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let M be a 2n-dimensional smooth manifold and let Q → M be a fiber bundle over M whose fiber at each point is a "quasi Riemann surface": a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface on which one can define a conformal-field-theory-like structure, namely an assignment to each point ξ of the total space Q of a field operator Φ(ξ) acting on a fixed Hilbert space, with operator product expansions and correlation functions analogous to those of a 2d CFT. A "defect" ξ ⊂ Q is a submanifold of Q; one says ξ is tiny (or pointlike) if its image in M under the bundle projection is concentrated near a single point of M, so that from the point of view of M the defect looks like an insertion at a point.

For each tiny defect ξ, define an ordinary local field on M by restricting/integrating the fields Φ(·) over ξ, producing an operator-valued distribution φ_ξ(x) on M (x ∈ M).

Question. Do the local fields {φ_ξ} obtained in this way, as ξ ranges over tiny defects, satisfy the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for a local quantum field theory on the 2n-dimensional manifold M, and if so, do they define genuinely new examples of local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions (i.e., theories not equivalent to previously known local QFTs in dimension 2n)?
status_search_result: The construction of CFT-like structures on quasi Riemann surfaces and their restriction to pointlike defects to yield local fields on a 2n-dimensional ambient manifold is a recent proposal; available references describe the construction but do not establish that the resulting restricted fields constitute new bona fide local QFTs in 2n dimensions. No proof or disproof of this claim was located, so the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
original_question: In the statistical model of nuclear reactions, partial gamma decay widths for isolated neutron resonances are usually assumed to follow a Porter-Thomas distribution (PTD), and total gamma decay widths are then obtained by summing a very large number of such partial widths over many gamma decay channels. The paper asks whether replacing the PTD assumption for the partial gamma widths with a different distribution could produce a predicted distribution of total gamma decay widths for neutron resonances in the compound nucleus 96Mo that agrees better with the experimentally observed distribution, which is much broader and centered at larger values than the standard statistical-model prediction.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a compound nucleus formed at neutron-resonance energies. In the standard statistical model, each isolated resonance λ has partial gamma decay widths Γ_{λc} into many gamma decay channels c = 1, …, N (with N very large), and the total gamma decay width is Γ_λ = Σ_{c=1}^N Γ_{λc}. Under the usual hypothesis the partial widths Γ_{λc} are independent random variables, each distributed according to a Porter–Thomas distribution (i.e. Γ_{λc}/⟨Γ_{λc}⟩ is distributed as a chi-squared variable with one degree of freedom). Summing N such independent partial widths yields, for large N, a predicted distribution P_PT(Γ) of total gamma widths that is sharply peaked about its mean.

For the compound nucleus ^{96}Mo, the experimentally observed distribution of total gamma decay widths over many neutron resonances is found to be much broader than P_PT(Γ) and to be centered at substantially larger values of Γ than the statistical-model mean.

Question: Does there exist an alternative probability distribution f(x) on [0, ∞) (with finite mean), used in place of the Porter–Thomas distribution for each normalized partial gamma width Γ_{λc}/⟨Γ_{λc}⟩, such that, when N independent partial widths drawn from f are summed to form the total width Γ_λ, the resulting predicted distribution of total gamma widths reproduces the empirically observed broader distribution, located at larger values of Γ, of total gamma decay widths of neutron resonances in ^{96}Mo? If so, exhibit such an f; if not, prove that no choice of f (subject to standard finiteness assumptions) can reconcile the statistical-model prediction with the observed distribution.
status_search_result: The internal analysis associated with this question indicates that replacing the Porter–Thomas distribution with a modified distribution for the partial gamma channels does not remove the discrepancy with the ^{96}Mo data, suggesting a negative answer within the framework considered. However, no fully general impossibility proof covering all alternative distributions appears to be established, and the broader puzzle of the ^{96}Mo total gamma-width distribution remains an active topic in nuclear-reaction statistics.

paper_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
context_brief: Strong low-lying gamma channels and neutron-width PTD
original_question: A possible way to reconcile the statistical model with the experimental total gamma decay-width data is that a comparatively small number of gamma transitions to low-lying final states are much more strongly coupled than the rest. Such channels would need to be intense enough to shift the simulated total gamma decay widths toward the experimental values and few enough in number to evade the central-limit-theorem narrowing that normally makes the predicted distribution too narrow. The open question is whether a comparatively small number of such strongly coupled gamma decay channels could also change the Porter-Thomas distribution behavior of the reduced neutron widths.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a compound-nucleus resonance described by a statistical model with the following ingredients:

(i) A set of N reduced partial neutron width amplitudes {γ_n^(i)} (i = 1,…,N) attached to N resonances of fixed spin and parity at excitation energies near the neutron separation threshold. In the standard Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) random-matrix description, these amplitudes are independent zero-mean Gaussian random variables, so that the reduced neutron widths Γ_n^(i) ∝ (γ_n^(i))^2 are distributed according to the Porter–Thomas distribution

   P(x) dx = (1/√(2π x)) exp(−x/2) dx,   x = Γ_n^(i)/⟨Γ_n⟩,

i.e. a chi-squared distribution with one degree of freedom.

(ii) A set of gamma decay channels c = 1,…,M from each resonance to lower-lying final states, with partial gamma widths Γ_{γ,c}^(i) and total gamma width Γ_γ^(i) = Σ_c Γ_{γ,c}^(i). In the standard picture the partial-width amplitudes γ_{γ,c}^(i) are also independent zero-mean Gaussian random variables, so each Γ_{γ,c}^(i) is Porter–Thomas distributed and, by the central limit theorem, the total widths Γ_γ^(i) have a relative variance that scales as 1/M_eff and is therefore strongly peaked about its mean for large effective channel number M_eff.

Hypothesis. Suppose now that a small subset S ⊂ {1,…,M} of gamma decay channels (with |S| ≪ M, e.g. transitions to a few low-lying final states) is anomalously strongly coupled, in the sense that the variances ⟨(γ_{γ,c}^(i))^2⟩ for c ∈ S are much larger than the variances for c ∉ S. Assume |S| is small enough that the central-limit-theorem narrowing of the distribution of Γ_γ^(i) is evaded (so the distribution of total gamma widths is broadened toward experimental values), yet large enough in coupling strength to shift the average Γ_γ^(i) toward the experimentally observed values.

Within a unified random-matrix / shell-model statistical framework where neutron and gamma channels are treated on the same footing (e.g. via a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian H_eff = H_GOE − (i/2) Σ_c V_c V_c^T with channel-coupling vectors V_c), the strong gamma channels in S contribute rank-|S| anti-Hermitian terms that break orthogonal invariance and mix the resonances.

Question. Does the presence of such a small number |S| of strongly coupled gamma decay channels — sufficient to broaden the distribution of total gamma decay widths Γ_γ^(i) and shift its mean toward experiment — necessarily induce a measurable deviation of the distribution of normalized reduced neutron widths Γ_n^(i)/⟨Γ_n⟩ from the Porter–Thomas (chi-squared, one degree of freedom) distribution? Quantify the deviation, for instance by computing the effective number of degrees of freedom ν in a fit to a chi-squared distribution of ν degrees of freedom, as a function of |S| and of the coupling strengths of the strong gamma channels.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has shown that channel coupling can in principle modify the Porter–Thomas distribution: rank-one and few-channel anti-Hermitian perturbations to a GOE Hamiltonian provably alter the chi-squared(1) law for partial widths, and realistic estimates of nonstatistical gamma decay yield significant modifications of the PTD for neutron widths. Experimental evidence in 150Nd indicates branching-ratio statistics inconsistent with ν=1, supporting deviations. However, a definitive quantitative answer linking a small set of strong low-lying gamma transitions to a specific, observed change in the neutron-width PTD across nuclei has not been established, so the question is best regarded as partially addressed but not fully resolved.

paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
context_brief: Direct three-α decay of the Hoyle state
original_question: Can a direct three-α decay branch of the carbon-12 Hoyle state be experimentally observed, despite current searches only limiting the branch relative to the 8Be + α two-body decay channel to about 10^-4 without success, and can such an observation give a clearer signal of the Hoyle state's internal α structure?
self_contained_problem:
The Hoyle state is the second 0⁺ excited state of the ¹²C nucleus, located near the 3α breakup threshold and known to decay predominantly through the sequential channel ¹²C* → ⁸Be(g.s.) + α → 3α. A direct three-body breakup channel ¹²C* → 3α (in which the three α particles are emitted simultaneously, not via an intermediate ⁸Be ground state) is also kinematically allowed and is regarded as a sensitive probe of an underlying α-cluster (in particular, dilute α-condensate-like) structure of the Hoyle state.

Let Γ_{3α,direct} denote the partial width for the direct three-α decay of the Hoyle state and let Γ denote its total width (equivalently, let Γ_{8Be+α} be the partial width of the sequential channel). Define the direct branching ratio
    B_direct = Γ_{3α,direct} / Γ   (or, equivalently, Γ_{3α,direct} / Γ_{8Be+α} to leading order).

Existing experimental searches have, at the time of formulation, established only upper bounds B_direct ≲ 10⁻⁴ relative to the sequential ⁸Be + α channel, with no positive observation.

Problem. Determine whether a nonzero direct three-α decay branch of the Hoyle state can be experimentally observed (i.e., whether B_direct > 0 can be established at a statistically significant level), and assess whether such an observation, together with the kinematical correlations of the three outgoing α particles, provides a quantitative discriminator of the internal α-cluster structure of the Hoyle state.
category_tag: Nuclear cluster physics / Hoyle state decay
status_search_result: No positive observation of a direct 3α decay of the Hoyle state has been reported. Subsequent experiments have only tightened the upper bound: Phys. Rev. C 101, 021302 (2020) reports Γ_{3α}/Γ < 5.7 × 10⁻⁶, and a 2018 analysis improved the limit to < 0.026% (95% C.L.). Thus the question of whether a direct 3α branch exists, and what it would reveal about the Hoyle state's α-cluster structure, remains experimentally open.

original_question: Is the first 1− state of carbon-12 an α-gas state formed by lifting one α particle from the Hoyle state into a P shell, and, if that interpretation is confirmed, how should it change the interpretation of the fifth 0+ state of oxygen-16 that has been viewed as an α particle orbiting the carbon-12 1− state?
self_contained_problem:
In a microscopic α-cluster description of light self-conjugate nuclei, the second 0⁺ state of ¹²C (the Hoyle state, near 7.65 MeV) is interpreted as a dilute, weakly interacting gas of three α particles essentially condensed into an S-wave 0s orbital. Building on this picture, consider the following two linked questions:

(a) Is the first 1⁻ state of ¹²C (the lowest J^π = 1⁻ excited state, at roughly 10.84 MeV) an "α-gas" state obtained from the Hoyle state by promoting exactly one of the three α particles from the 0s orbital into a 0p (P-shell) orbital, so that the resulting state has an anomalously large root-mean-square radius characteristic of a dilute α-condensate? Provide a theoretical demonstration (e.g., via a THSR-type α-condensate wave function, RGM/GCM, or equivalent microscopic α-cluster calculation) and/or experimental confirmation (e.g., from the matter/charge radius, monopole/dipole transition strengths, and α-decay branching) that establishes or refutes this interpretation.

(b) The fifth 0⁺ state of ¹⁶O has been interpreted as a structure consisting of an α particle orbiting the 1⁻ state of ¹²C. Assuming the interpretation in (a) is confirmed, determine how this structural assignment for the fifth 0⁺ state of ¹⁶O must be revised, and exhibit a corresponding microscopic four-α (or α + ¹²C*) cluster wave function, together with predicted observables (excitation energy, radius, decay widths, and electromagnetic transition strengths) consistent with the revised interpretation.

paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
original_question: For the oxygen-16 candidate Hoyle-analog state, does the dilute Bose gas condense as four individual α particles or as two 8Be-like bosonic molecules, and how can those two condensation pictures be distinguished when their wave functions may strongly overlap?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a self-conjugate light nucleus modeled as a dilute system of bosonic constituents in which the lowest 0⁺ state lying near the four-α breakup threshold of ¹⁶O is interpreted as a Hoyle-analog state. Two competing condensation pictures are proposed for this 0⁺ state:

(i) a Bose–Einstein-like condensate of four α particles, in which all four α clusters occupy a common 0S single-particle orbital (a Tohsaki–Horiuchi–Schuck–Röpke (THSR) type wave function built from four α's);

(ii) a Bose–Einstein-like condensate of two ⁸Be-like bosonic "molecules," in which the four α's are first paired into two ⁸Be subunits, and the two ⁸Be bosons then occupy a common 0S orbital.

Both trial wave functions are fully antisymmetrized in the underlying nucleons, and numerical experience suggests that, as with the Hoyle state of ¹²C (where the THSR wave function and the Kamimura-type 3α wave function have approximately 100% squared overlap), the two ¹⁶O wave functions may have a very large mutual overlap.

Problem. Determine, on the theoretical level, whether the Hoyle-analog 0⁺ state of ¹⁶O is best described as a condensate of four individual α particles or as a condensate of two ⁸Be-like bosonic molecules, and devise observables or mathematical criteria (e.g., occupation numbers of the one-α and one-⁸Be density matrices, intrinsic-density structure, momentum distributions, or decay-channel branching ratios) capable of unambiguously distinguishing these two condensation pictures even when their many-body wave functions have nearly unit squared overlap.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2019–2021) on the Hoyle analog in ¹⁶O reports that the experimental signature of the candidate 0⁺ state (around 15.1 MeV) remains inconclusive, and reviews of α-particle condensation continue to discuss the singles-vs-molecules distinction as an open theoretical question. No source claims a definitive resolution distinguishing four-α versus two-⁸Be condensation.

paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
original_question: Which neutron-rich nuclei with valence neutrons, such as carbon-13, carbon-14, and beryllium isotopes, contain Hoyle-like α-cluster gas states, and how do extra neutrons modify the α-cluster structure relative to self-conjugate nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers?
self_contained_problem:
In nuclear cluster physics, the Hoyle state is the second 0⁺ excited state of ¹²C near 7.65 MeV above the ground state, and is interpreted as a dilute, weakly interacting gas-like (Bose–Einstein-condensate-like) configuration of three α particles. Such configurations have so far been studied principally in self-conjugate nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers N = Z (e.g., ⁸Be, ¹²C, ¹⁶O, ²⁰Ne, …), where they are conjectured to appear near the Nα breakup threshold.

Consider neutron-rich nuclei that can be modeled as an α-cluster core surrounded by additional valence neutrons, in particular the carbon isotopes ¹³C (3α + n) and ¹⁴C (3α + 2n), and the beryllium isotopes (e.g., 2α + xn systems such as ⁹Be, ¹⁰Be, ¹¹Be, ¹²Be).

Problem:

(a) Determine which of these neutron-rich nuclei support Hoyle-like α-cluster gas states, i.e., low-density excited 0⁺ (or analogous Jᵖ) states near the multi-α + xn breakup threshold whose intrinsic structure is well approximated by a dilute condensate of α particles together with valence neutrons in single-particle (molecular-orbital or covalent) configurations.

(b) Quantify how the presence of the extra valence neutrons modifies the α-cluster structure relative to the corresponding N = Z Hoyle-like state, addressing the binding energy and excitation energy of such states relative to the multi-α threshold, the spatial extent and density profile of the α-cluster core, the rotational/vibrational band structure built upon these states, and the role of the valence neutrons (covalent "molecular" binding versus mean-field-like delocalization) in stabilizing or destabilizing the α gas configuration.

Provide a theoretical characterization of these Hoyle-like states with valence neutrons and identify experimental signatures that would distinguish them from non-clusterized excited states.
status_search_result: Substantial theoretical and experimental progress has been made on α-clustering in neutron-rich carbon and beryllium isotopes (e.g., molecular-orbital structures in ⁹⁻¹²Be, linear-chain and clustered states in ¹³C and ¹⁴C), and reviews from 2022–2024 describe valence neutrons as playing a covalent "glue" role that stabilizes α-cluster configurations. paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
context_brief: Replacing infeasible FOT with scenario simulation
original_question: How can automated-driving system verification avoid infeasible field operational testing, which may require hundreds of thousands to hundreds of billions of miles, by using simulation and short-mileage test-course reproduction of rare corner-case scenarios that have extremely low occurrence probability on actual roads?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the verification of an automated-driving system whose safety claim requires statistically significant evidence of correct behavior across the operational domain. Direct field operational testing (FOT), in which the system is driven on public roads to accumulate exposure to real traffic, is estimated to require on the order of 10^5 to 10^11 miles to attain such statistical significance, which is infeasible within realistic project time-frames. A central source of difficulty is the existence of "corner-case" scenarios — situations whose probability of occurrence on actual roads is extremely low, so that they are essentially never sampled by FOT, yet whose correct handling is critical to the system's safety case.

Develop a verification methodology that replaces, or substantially reduces reliance on, infeasible FOT by combining:
(a) simulation-based testing, in which scenarios are generated and executed in a virtual environment, and
(b) short-mileage reproduction of rare corner-case scenarios on physical test courses.

The methodology must specify:
1. A formal definition of the operational domain and of the class of corner-case scenarios to be covered.
2. A procedure for systematically generating, sampling, or enumerating corner-case scenarios with extremely low natural occurrence probability so that statistically meaningful coverage is achieved.
3. A quantitative argument relating performance measured under simulation and short test-course mileage to the safety performance that would have been measured by full-scale FOT, including a treatment of the reality gap between simulated/test-course conditions and real-road conditions.
4. Criteria under which the combined simulation plus short-mileage test-course evidence is sufficient to substitute for FOT of the order required for statistical significance.

Provide such a methodology, or prove that no methodology meeting all four requirements can exist under stated assumptions.
status_search_result: The challenge of replacing infeasible field operational testing of automated driving systems with scenario-based simulation and short-mileage test-course reproduction of rare corner cases remains an active, unresolved research area. Standards efforts (ISO 21448 SOTIF, UL 4600) and ongoing scenario-based testing research (Pegasus, NHTSA frameworks, and numerous arXiv papers through the mid-2020s) continue to propose partial methods (scenario libraries, importance sampling, adversarial scenario generation, reality-gap quantification), but no generally accepted methodology provides a quantitative substitute for full-scale FOT.

paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
original_question: How can requirements for a safety-critical subsystem that contains machine-learning models be rigorously broken down into machine-learning-model requirements while combining deductive engineering with inductive machine-learning development and using safety-analysis approaches such as black-box verification, rule-based safeguarding, redundant and diverse architectures, and modification patterns that avoid the 'Change Anything Change Everything' principle?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a safety-critical system S that is decomposed into subsystems, some of which contain one or more machine-learning (ML) models. Classical (deductive) engineering produces components whose behavior is specified and verified against explicit requirements, while ML components are obtained inductively from data and therefore carry residual uncertainty. Suppose S has a set of system-level safety requirements R_S. For each subsystem U ⊆ S that contains ML models M_1, ..., M_k, one wishes to derive a set of ML-model-level requirements R_{M_i} such that:

(i) Satisfaction of R_{M_1}, ..., R_{M_k}, together with the requirements assigned to the non-ML parts of U, formally entails the subsystem-level requirements R_U allocated from R_S.
(ii) The derivation simultaneously accommodates the deductive development process used for non-ML components and the inductive development process used for the ML models.
(iii) The derivation is compatible with, and exploits, the following safety-analysis mechanisms: (a) black-box verification of trained ML models; (b) encapsulation of ML models by rule-based safeguards that constrain their outputs; (c) redundant and diverse architectures that mitigate and absorb the uncertainty of ML models; (d) system-modification patterns that allow new requirements to be satisfied without retraining or altering the ML model, so as to limit the "Change Anything Change Everything" (CACE) effect by which any change to an ML model can affect any of its outputs.

Provide a rigorous methodology — i.e., a formal framework, a set of decomposition rules, and an associated proof obligation discharge procedure — for performing the breakdown R_U ↦ {R_{M_i}} satisfying (i)–(iii), and demonstrate its soundness.
status_search_result: Recent literature on safety assurance of ML-based systems (assurance cases, ISO 21448/SOTIF, ISO/PAS 8800, AMLAS, and surveys on ML safety) continues to treat rigorous decomposition of system-level safety requirements into ML-model-level requirements as an open engineering and methodological challenge. No general, formally validated methodology that simultaneously combines deductive/inductive development and the listed safety-analysis mechanisms (black-box verification, rule-based safeguarding, redundant/diverse architectures, CACE-avoiding modification patterns) appears to have been established.

paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
context_brief: Extending safety assurance notations for ML uncertainty
original_question: How should system-level assurance methods such as STAMP/STPA and Goal Structuring Notation be extended so that they can express uncertainty related to machine-learning models in safety-critical subsystems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider two system-level safety assurance frameworks used for engineering safety-critical systems:

1. STAMP/STPA (Systems-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes / System-Theoretic Process Analysis): a hazard analysis technique that models a system as a hierarchical control structure of controllers, actuators, sensors, and controlled processes, and identifies unsafe control actions and their causal scenarios.

2. Goal Structuring Notation (GSN): a graphical argumentation notation for safety cases, in which top-level safety goals are decomposed via strategies into subgoals, supported by context, assumptions, justifications, and evidence (solutions).

Now consider safety-critical systems that contain subsystems implemented by machine-learning models, i.e., functions f: X → Y obtained by training on data, whose behavior carries intrinsic uncertainty (epistemic uncertainty about the learned hypothesis, aleatoric uncertainty in the data and operating environment, distributional shift between training and deployment, and quantifiable confidence/calibration of predictions).

Problem. Propose a principled extension of STAMP/STPA and of GSN such that:
(a) STAMP/STPA control-structure models and unsafe-control-action / causal-scenario analyses can explicitly represent and reason about machine-learning–induced uncertainty (e.g., model confidence, input-distribution coverage, training-data assumptions, and failure modes specific to learned components);
(b) GSN safety-case arguments can express claims, strategies, contexts, assumptions, and evidence types that capture and discharge machine-learning uncertainty in a sound, auditable manner;
(c) The extensions admit a formal semantics or notational discipline that supports compositional reasoning when learned components are integrated into the broader control system.

Provide such extensions, including their syntax, semantics, and demonstration that they faithfully capture the uncertainty associated with ML components in safety-critical subsystems.
status_search_result: The question of extending STAMP/STPA and GSN to capture machine-learning uncertainty has received active attention since 2018, with multiple proposed extensions (e.g., assurance-case patterns for ML, AMLAS methodology, STPA variants for ML-enabled systems), but no single, agreed-upon, formally complete extension has emerged. The general problem remains open as a research area.

paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
original_question: Which quality characteristics of machine-learning models, beyond accuracy or confusion matrices, should be defined and evaluated for safety-critical systems, including resource behavior, time behavior, robustness against adversarial examples, analyzability or interpretability, and testability for formal verification?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a machine-learning model M (for example, a trained classifier or regressor) that is to be deployed as a component of a safety-critical system. Beyond classical predictive accuracy (e.g., confusion-matrix-based metrics), identify and rigorously define a complete set of quality characteristics that should be specified, measured, and evaluated to certify M for safety-critical use. In particular, provide precise mathematical or operational definitions, together with concrete evaluation procedures (metrics, test protocols, and acceptance criteria), for at least the following candidate characteristics:

1. Resource behavior: quantitative measures of the memory footprint required for inference (and, if relevant, training).
2. Time behavior: quantitative measures of inference latency and throughput, including worst-case execution time bounds.
3. Robustness against adversarial examples: given an input space X with a metric d and a perturbation budget ε > 0, define and evaluate the model's resistance to inputs x' with d(x, x') ≤ ε that change the model's output in an unsafe way; specify both empirical attack-based metrics and certified/provable robustness metrics.
4. Analyzability / interpretability: formal notions of the ease with which the internal computations of M can be inspected, visualized, or explained, together with quantitative measures of explanation quality.
5. Testability for formal verification: structural properties of M (e.g., architectural simplicity, piecewise-linearity, bounded depth) that enable tractable application of formal verification methods, together with measures of verification cost and coverage.

Propose a coherent quality model that integrates these characteristics, demonstrate that the proposed definitions are mutually consistent and measurable, and discuss any trade-offs (e.g., between accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and verification cost) that arise when optimizing M with respect to all of them simultaneously.
category_tag: ML quality characteristics for safety-critical systems
status_search_result: The question is an open engineering/research challenge concerning the definition of quality characteristics for safety-critical ML beyond accuracy. It remains an active area of research, with ongoing standardization efforts (e.g., ISO/IEC 25000-series adaptations to ML, ISO/IEC TR 24028, ISO/IEC 5469, and the EU AI Act's high-risk requirements) and a growing literature on robustness, interpretability, and formal verification of neural networks, but no universally accepted, complete quality model has been established.

paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
original_question: How can operation and maintenance processes for safety-critical machine-learning systems continuously check consistency between current operational data and the originally assumed test-data distribution, and update or adapt models when operational data changes over time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a supervised machine-learning system deployed in a safety-critical setting. During development, the model is trained and validated on data drawn from a fixed but unknown distribution P_test on an input–output space X × Y. After deployment, the system observes a stream of operational inputs (and, possibly delayed or partially observed, corresponding outputs) (x_t, y_t)_{t≥1} drawn from a time-varying operational distribution P_op,t that may drift away from P_test as t grows.

Develop a principled methodology for the operation and maintenance phase that simultaneously:

1. (Consistency monitoring) Provides a statistical procedure that, at each time t, tests the null hypothesis H_0: P_op,t = P_test against the alternative of drift, with controlled false-alarm rate and quantifiable detection delay, using only the streaming operational data and a finite reference sample from P_test.

2. (Adaptation) Specifies a continuous update rule that modifies the deployed model f_t whenever significant drift is detected (or continuously), in such a way that
   (a) the updated model's risk under P_op,t is bounded above by a prescribed safety threshold,
   (b) safety-relevant performance guarantees established at development time are preserved or re-established under the updated distribution, and
   (c) the procedure is robust to label scarcity, label delay, and adversarial or rare-event inputs.

Formulate precise sufficient conditions on P_test, the family {P_op,t}, the model class, and the available feedback under which such a monitoring-and-adaptation scheme exists, and characterize fundamental limits (in terms of detection delay, sample complexity, and post-update risk) on any scheme satisfying the above safety requirements.
category_tag: Distribution shift detection and continual learning
status_search_result: Concept/data drift detection and safe continual adaptation for deployed ML systems remain active research areas. While many algorithms exist (e.g., ADWIN, DDM, MMD-based two-sample tests, conformal change detection, online learning under covariate shift), no general methodology provides certified safety guarantees for arbitrary safety-critical ML systems under non-stationary operational data. Recent surveys on concept drift, distribution-shift monitoring, and assurance of safety-critical ML continue to list this as an open challenge.

paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
context_brief: Concrete interpretability and NN-visualization use cases
original_question: What concrete use cases can make interpretability and transparency methods for safety-critical machine-learning systems actionable, especially neural-network visualization methods that identify regions of interest through occlusion or activation back-propagation for debugging training and validating trained model behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a safety-critical system whose decisions depend on a trained neural network classifier f: X -> Y, where X is a space of input signals (e.g., images) and Y a finite set of labels. Two standard neural-network visualization techniques are available:

(i) Occlusion-based saliency: for an input x in X, define a region-of-interest map S_occ(x) by masking subregions of x with a baseline value and recording where f's output probability for the predicted class changes most sharply.

(ii) Activation back-propagation: starting from highly activated nodes in deeper feature-extraction layers of f, back-propagate activation values to the input space to obtain a region-of-interest map S_bp(x).

Formulate and exhibit concrete, well-defined use cases in which the maps S_occ and S_bp can be employed as actionable tools for (a) debugging the network during training and (b) validating the behavior of the trained network, in such a way that the visualizations provide verifiable interpretability and transparency guarantees suitable for safety-critical deployment. Specifically, describe operational procedures, acceptance criteria, and quantitative metrics under which these visualization methods yield decisions about model correctness that can be incorporated into a safety assurance argument.
status_search_result: The problem is engineering-oriented and remains an active open challenge in the safety-critical ML community. There is no canonical solution; ongoing work on saliency-map evaluation and assurance cases (e.g., literature on XAI for safety, ISO/PAS 21448, AMLAS) continues to seek concrete actionable use cases, but no consensus solution exists.

original_question: For the new asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds constructed by Foscolo, Haskins, and Nordstrom that are cohomogeneity-1 under an SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) action, which of the locally defined G2-instantons near the singular orbit extend to globally defined G2-instantons on the whole manifold X, and, once the global solutions are classified and a nontrivial family is found, what global properties does the resulting moduli space have? In particular, what happens for the D7 family from [FHN18]?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of asymptotically conical (AC) 7-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(X,g)$ with holonomy contained in the exceptional Lie group $G_2$ that arise as cohomogeneity-one manifolds for an isometric action of $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$ with a single singular orbit. (Here a complete Riemannian $G_2$-manifold $(X,g)$ is asymptotically conical if outside a compact set it is diffeomorphic to a cone $C(\Sigma)=(R_0,\infty)\times\Sigma$ over a smooth compact 6-manifold $\Sigma$, with the metric $g$ converging at a polynomial rate to the conical metric $dr^2+r^2 g_\Sigma$ where $g_\Sigma$ is a nearly Kähler metric on $\Sigma$.) Among the families of such metrics constructed via cohomogeneity-one methods, distinguish in particular the family denoted $D_7$.

A $G_2$-instanton on $X$ is a connection $A$ on a principal $G$-bundle $P\to X$ (for $G$ a compact Lie group, e.g. $SU(2)$) whose curvature $F_A\in\Omega^2(X;\mathrm{ad}\,P)$ satisfies $F_A\wedge\psi=0$, where $\psi=*\varphi$ is the Hodge dual of the defining $G_2$ 3-form $\varphi$ on $X$. An $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$-invariant $G_2$-instanton is one for which the action lifts to $P$ and preserves $A$.

Local existence of invariant $G_2$-instantons in a neighborhood of the singular orbit is known; equivariantly, near the singular orbit the equations reduce to an ODE system whose solutions are parameterized by a finite-dimensional moduli of initial data compatible with the isotropy representation.

Problems:
(a) For each of these AC $G_2$-manifolds $X$ (and especially for the $D_7$ family), determine which of the locally defined $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$-invariant $G_2$-instantons defined in a neighborhood of the singular orbit extend to globally defined smooth $G_2$-instantons on all of $X$ with finite Yang–Mills energy and an appropriate decay rate at infinity.
(b) Classify all such global invariant $G_2$-instantons, and, when a nontrivial family exists, describe the global properties of the resulting moduli space (dimension, smoothness, compactness, behavior at the boundary corresponding to bubbling or to limits along the asymptotic cone).
status_search_result: For some of the cohomogeneity-one AC/ALC $G_2$-manifolds in the FHN family, invariant $G_2$-instantons have been constructed: in particular for the $B_7$ and $C_7$ families (work by Matos, Lotay–Oliveira, and others) one-parameter families of $SU(2)^2$- or $SU(2)^2\times U(1)$-invariant $G_2$-instantons are known. The $D_7$ case, explicitly singled out in the original problem, does not appear to have been treated in the available literature, and the global structure of the moduli space (compactification, bubbling) remains open in general.

original_question: What is the local deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical G2-manifolds? More specifically, can one understand the local geometry of their moduli space, prove a uniqueness result for the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, decide whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries, and determine the properties of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons, including whether that projection is surjective?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^7, \varphi, g)$ be an asymptotically conical $G_2$-manifold; that is, a complete 7-manifold equipped with a torsion-free $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ (with associated metric $g$) which, outside a compact set, is asymptotic at a polynomial rate to the Riemannian cone $C(\Sigma) = (\mathbb{R}_{>0} \times \Sigma, dr^2 + r^2 g_\Sigma)$ over a nearly Kähler 6-manifold $(\Sigma, g_\Sigma)$. Let $P \to M$ be a principal $G$-bundle with compact structure group $G$. A $G_2$-instanton on $P$ is a connection $A$ whose curvature $F_A$ satisfies $F_A \wedge \psi = 0$, where $\psi = *\varphi$. Asymptotic to a fixed dilation-invariant $G_2$-instanton on $C(\Sigma)$ (equivalently, a pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills/$SU(3)$-instanton on $\Sigma$), one obtains a moduli space $\mathcal{M}(M)$ of asymptotically conical $G_2$-instantons on $M$ and a moduli space $\mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$ of nearly Kähler instantons on $\Sigma$, together with a natural restriction-to-link projection $\pi:\mathcal{M}(M) \to \mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$.

Address the following:

(a) Describe the local structure of $\mathcal{M}(M)$ near a given asymptotically conical $G_2$-instanton (its expected dimension, obstruction theory, and smoothness conditions).

(b) Prove a uniqueness statement for the "basic" $G_2$-instanton on $\mathbb{R}^7$ with gauge group $G_2$ (the canonical $G_2$-instanton built from the spin connection / octonionic structure on flat $\mathbb{R}^7$): show that, within an appropriate class of asymptotically conical $G_2$-instantons on $\mathbb{R}^7$ with gauge group $G_2$, the basic instanton is the unique solution.

(c) Suppose $H$ is a Lie group acting on $(M, \varphi)$ by $G_2$-automorphisms preserving a given $H$-invariant $G_2$-instanton $A_0$. Show, or determine the obstructions to showing, that every sufficiently small deformation of $A_0$ within $\mathcal{M}(M)$ is gauge-equivalent to an $H$-invariant connection.

(d) Determine geometric and analytic properties of the projection $\pi:\mathcal{M}(M) \to \mathcal{M}(\Sigma)$; in particular, decide whether $\pi$ is surjective.
status_search_result: Joe Driscoll's 2020 PhD thesis (University of Leeds) "Deformations of Asymptotically Conical G2-Instantons" develops the local deformation theory addressing part (a), relating deformations to the kernel of a twisted Dirac operator on M and to eigenvalues on the nearly Kähler link. Subsequent work (e.g., Driscoll's paper on G2-instantons on the spinor bundle of S^3, J. Geom. Anal. 2024) builds on this. The full uniqueness of the basic G2-instanton on R^7, the symmetry-preservation question for general H, and surjectivity of the projection to the nearly Kähler instanton moduli space do not appear settled in the literature, so the overall problem is partially solved.

original_question: On the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, Proposition 6 gives a local 1-parameter family of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) that extend smoothly over the singular orbit on the bundle P_id, and Theorem 5 shows that the member with parameter y_0 = 0 extends globally. Do any of the other local instantons from that family, namely those with y_0 != 0, also extend globally, and if they do, is their curvature necessarily unbounded at infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\varphi)$ denote the Bryant–Salamon $G_2$-holonomy manifold $M = \mathbb{R}^4 \times S^3$, regarded as the spinor bundle of $S^3$ equipped with its complete torsion-free $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ of cohomogeneity one under the natural action of $SU(2)^2 \times U(1)$, with singular orbit the associative $3$-sphere $S^3 \subset M$. Over the principal stratum, the isotropy of a point is the diagonal $U(1)$ and one has the principal $SO(4)$-bundle of frames; restrict attention to the $SU(2)$-bundle $P_{\mathrm{id}} \to M$ corresponding to the identity homomorphism $U(1) \hookrightarrow SU(2)$ (so that $P_{\mathrm{id}}$ extends smoothly across the singular orbit $S^3$).

A connection $A$ on $P_{\mathrm{id}}$ with curvature $F_A$ is a $G_2$-instanton if $F_A \wedge \psi = 0$, where $\psi = *\varphi$ is the coassociative $4$-form of $\varphi$.

Suppose it is known that there exists a smooth one-parameter family $\{A_{y_0}\}_{y_0 \in \mathbb{R}}$ of $SU(2)^2 \times U(1)$-invariant $G_2$-instantons on $P_{\mathrm{id}}$, each defined on an open neighbourhood of $S^3$ in $M$ and extending smoothly across $S^3$, and that the distinguished member $A_0$ corresponding to $y_0 = 0$ extends to a globally defined $SU(2)^3$-invariant $G_2$-instanton on all of $M$.

Determine:
(a) whether there exists any $y_0 \neq 0$ for which the locally defined $G_2$-instanton $A_{y_0}$ extends to a smooth $G_2$-instanton on the whole of $M = \mathbb{R}^4 \times S^3$;
(b) for every such $y_0 \neq 0$ for which a global extension exists, whether the pointwise norm $|F_{A_{y_0}}|$ of the curvature, measured with respect to the Bryant–Salamon metric, is necessarily unbounded as one tends to infinity in $M$.
status_search_result: Subsequent works by Alonso (arXiv:2311.08378, "New examples of G_2-instantons on R^4 x S^3") and related Springer papers on G_2-instantons on the spinor bundle of S^3 study families of SU(2)^2-invariant G_2-instantons on R^4 x S^3, but I could not find a publicly accessible source explicitly resolving whether the y_0 ≠ 0 members of the relevant one-parameter family on P_id extend globally on the Bryant–Salamon metric, nor confirming the predicted unboundedness of curvature at infinity. The status therefore appears unverified from the available search.

original_question: For the many asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds that are close to a degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit and are typically only U(1)-invariant, can one construct G2-instantons that are correspondingly close, in an appropriate sense, to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the limiting cone?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(C,g_C)$ be a Calabi-Yau cone of complex dimension $3$, and let $(M,\varphi,g)$ be a complete asymptotically locally conical (ALC) $G_2$-manifold of dimension $7$, meaning that outside a compact set $M$ is diffeomorphic to a circle bundle over the link of $C$ whose $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ approaches, with suitable decay, the product of $g_C$ with the standard metric on a circle of fixed asymptotic length. Assume $M$ lies in a one-parameter family of ALC $G_2$-manifolds that collapses, as the asymptotic circle length tends to $0$, to the Calabi-Yau cone $C$ in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense (the "degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit"); in particular such $M$ may have only a $U(1)$ symmetry (acting by rotation of the asymptotic circle fibers).
   
A $G_2$-instanton on a principal $G$-bundle $P \to M$ is a connection $A$ whose curvature $F_A$ satisfies $F_A \wedge \psi = 0$, where $\psi = *\varphi$ is the coassociative $4$-form. A Calabi-Yau monopole on $C$ is a pair $(B,\Phi)$ consisting of a connection $B$ and a Higgs field $\Phi$ on a principal $G$-bundle over $C$ satisfying $F_B \wedge \tfrac{1}{2}\omega^2 = *_{C}\, d_B\Phi$, where $\omega$ is the Kähler form of the Calabi-Yau structure on $C$.
   
Problem. For ALC $G_2$-manifolds $M$ close to the degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit (and in particular for examples that are only $U(1)$-invariant rather than enjoying larger continuous symmetry), construct $G_2$-instantons on $M$ that, in the collapsing limit, converge in an appropriate gauge-theoretic sense to a prescribed Calabi-Yau monopole $(B,\Phi)$ on the cone $C$. More precisely, given a Calabi-Yau monopole $(B,\Phi)$ on $C$, produce a family of $G_2$-instantons $A_\epsilon$ on the corresponding ALC $G_2$-manifolds $M_\epsilon$ (parameterized by the asymptotic circle length $\epsilon$) such that $A_\epsilon$ converges to $(B,\Phi)$ as $\epsilon \to 0$, with $\Phi$ recovered from the component of $A_\epsilon$ along the collapsing circle.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., the 2025 study of the large-mass limit of G2 and Calabi-Yau monopoles, and related works on invariant gauge theory on asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-folds) develops structural results in the Donaldson-Segal programme connecting Calabi-Yau monopoles to G2-instantons via collapse, and constructs explicit invariant G2-instantons in highly symmetric examples (e.g., SU(2)^2-invariant settings on the spinor bundle of S^3). However, no general construction of G2-instantons on the merely U(1)-invariant ALC G2-manifolds close to a degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit, converging to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the cone, appears to have been carried out. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant SU(2) G2-instantons on the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 x S^3 that extend smoothly on the bundle P_1, what happens in the unresolved parameter region 0 < f_1^+ - 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+? In particular, which initial conditions in that region produce globally defined instantons with bounded curvature, which do not, and how should the corresponding existence and non-existence picture be completed for the broader Bogoyavlenskaya family of metrics?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M = \mathbb{R}^4 \times S^3$ equipped with the Brandhuber–Gauntlett–Gibbons–Gukov (BGGG) complete $G_2$-holonomy metric, viewed as a cohomogeneity-one manifold under the action of $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2 \times \mathrm{U}(1)$, with principal orbit $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2 \times \mathrm{U}(1)/\Delta\mathrm{U}(1) \cong S^3 \times S^3$ and singular orbit $S^3$. Let $P_1 \to M$ be the principal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-bundle whose connections extend smoothly across the singular orbit in the standard way considered for this cohomogeneity-one reduction, and consider $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2 \times \mathrm{U}(1)$-invariant $G_2$-instantons $A$ on $P_1$.

Such invariant connections on the principal orbit are described by an ODE system in two real-valued radial functions $f_1(t), g_1(t)$ (the standard parameters appearing in the cohomogeneity-one ansatz for $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2 \times \mathrm{U}(1)$-invariant $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-connections). Smooth extension across the singular orbit determines initial data $(f_1^+, g_1^+) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, namely the values of $(f_1, g_1)$ at the singular orbit.

Known results for this setup state:
(i) If $f_1^+ \le 1/2$, or if $g_1^+ \ge 0$ with $g_1^+ \ge f_1^+$, then any $G_2$-instanton $A$ extending globally to $M$ with bounded curvature must have abelian gauge group $\mathrm{U}(1)$.
(ii) If $f_1^+ \ge 1/2 + g_1^+ > 1/2$, then $A$ is irreducible and extends globally to $M$ with bounded curvature.

These leave open the parameter region
$$\mathcal{R} = \{(f_1^+, g_1^+) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 0 < f_1^+ - \tfrac{1}{2} < g_1^+ < f_1^+\}.$$

Problem. 
(a) Determine, for each $(f_1^+, g_1^+) \in \mathcal{R}$, whether the corresponding irreducible $\mathrm{SU}(2)^2 \times \mathrm{U}(1)$-invariant $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $G_2$-instanton on $P_1$ extends to a globally defined $G_2$-instanton on $M$ with bounded curvature, or fails to do so. In particular, identify the subset of $\mathcal{R}$ giving rise to globally defined bounded-curvature instantons and the complementary subset on which global extension or curvature boundedness fails, thereby completing the description of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{BGGG}}_{P_1}$.
(b) Extend the analogous existence/non-existence picture to the full Bogoyavlenskaya family of complete cohomogeneity-one $G_2$-metrics on $\mathbb{R}^4 \times S^3$ (which interpolates with the BGGG metric and which contains it), specifying precisely how the dichotomy in (a) deforms across this family.
status_search_result: Searches for follow-up work on SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on the BGGG metric (including the 2022 paper on the AC limit of the C7 family and the 2023 paper "New examples of G2-instantons on R^4 × S^3") did not produce evidence that the specific parameter region 0 < f_1^+ − 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+ has been resolved or that the full Bogoyavlenskaya extension has been completed. The problem appears to remain open.
