original_question: The moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1} of irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on the BGGG manifold is non-compact. Can this moduli space be compactified, and what bubbling behavior occurs as one or both of the parameters f_1^+ and g_1^+ tend to infinity? In particular, does one obtain bubbling phenomena analogous to those proved for the Bryant-Salamon case, possibly related to anti-self-dual instantons on Taub-NUT?
self_contained_problem:
Let M = ℝ⁴ × S³ be equipped with the BGGG (Brandhuber–Gauntlett–Gibbons–Gubser) complete G₂-holonomy metric, which admits an isometric action of SU(2) × SU(2) × U(1). Let P₁ → M denote the principal SU(2)-bundle on which one studies SU(2)²×U(1)-invariant G₂-instantons that extend smoothly across the singular orbit. It is known that the moduli space M^{BGGG}_{P₁} of irreducible such G₂-instantons (with gauge group SU(2)) contains a nonempty unbounded open subset parametrized by an open set U ⊂ ℝ², with two real parameters f₁⁺ and g₁⁺ that may tend to infinity.

(a) Construct a natural compactification of the moduli space M^{BGGG}_{P₁}.

(b) Describe the bubbling behaviour of the family of G₂-instantons as one or both of the parameters f₁⁺ and g₁⁺ tend to infinity. In particular, determine whether the limiting bubbles correspond to anti-self-dual instantons on the Taub-NUT space (analogous to the bubbling phenomenon established for the Bryant–Salamon G₂-metric, where bubbles are ASD instantons on ℝ⁴).
status_search_result: Searches surface the foundational work on SU(2)²-invariant G₂-instantons on the BGGG and Bryant–Salamon metrics, where bubbling and removable singularity phenomena are described in the Bryant–Salamon case, and the analogous compactification/bubbling problem on the BGGG side (with conjectural relation to ASD instantons on Taub-NUT) is posed as an open question. No subsequent paper resolving the BGGG compactification and bubbling description was located.

context_brief: Extend perfectness and simplicity criteria for PE(V)
original_question: Determine whether the two theorems cited from [Lo5] continue to hold for broader classes of Jordan pairs: namely, whether PE(V) is perfect exactly when V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F2, F2), (F3, F3), or (H2(F2), H2(F2)), and whether PE(V) is simple exactly when V is simple and avoids those exceptional factors.
self_contained_problem:
Let V = (V⁺, V⁻) be a Jordan pair, and let L(V) denote its Tits–Kantor–Koecher Lie algebra. The projective elementary group PE(V) is defined as the subgroup of Aut(L(V)) generated by the one-parameter subgroups exp(ad x) for x ∈ V⁺ and x ∈ V⁻. A Jordan pair V is called simple if it has no nonzero proper ideals and its product is nonzero; the simple factors of V are the simple Jordan pairs occurring in a decomposition of V. Distinguish three "exceptional" simple Jordan pairs: (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), and (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂)) (where Hₙ(F) denotes the Jordan pair of n×n hermitian matrices over F).

Two known theorems for finite-dimensional Jordan pairs over a field state:
(T1) PE(V) is a perfect group if and only if V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂));
(T2) PE(V) is a simple group if and only if V is simple and not isomorphic to any of those three exceptional Jordan pairs.

Problem: Determine whether (T1) and (T2) extend to broader classes of Jordan pairs (for instance, infinite-dimensional Jordan pairs, or Jordan pairs over arbitrary commutative rings). Specifically, prove or disprove that for the broader class under consideration:
(a) PE(V) is perfect ⇔ V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂));
(b) Assuming V is simple, PE(V) is simple ⇔ V is not isomorphic to any of (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂)).
category_tag: Jordan pairs and projective elementary groups
status_search_result: The classical perfectness and simplicity theorems for PE(V) are due to Loos for finite-dimensional Jordan pairs, and Loos–Neher have developed Steinberg groups and simplicity results for elementary groups defined by Jordan pairs graded by 3-graded root systems, recovering analogous statements with the same exceptional factors. However, no source verified definitively settles the extension of both theorems to fully general Jordan pairs, so the status is taken to be unknown / partially addressed.

original_question: Assume V is defined over a field F and has a fully idempotent root grading R that is a division grading, meaning that every nonzero x in a root space V_alpha makes Q(x)|V_alpha invertible on the opposite root space. In the low-rank cases 2 <= rank R <= 4, is it true that whenever the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, every root space V_alpha must be one-dimensional over F and the field F must satisfy exactly the exceptional small-field restrictions listed in table (3.2.1)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let F be a field and let V = (V^+, V^-) be a Jordan pair over F equipped with a quadratic operator Q: V^σ → Hom(V^{-σ}, V^σ). Suppose V carries a root grading R, that is, a decomposition V^σ = ⨁_{α ∈ R_1} V^σ_α indexed by the set R_1 of "one-roots" of a (possibly non-reduced) finite root system R, satisfying the standard compatibility axioms with the Jordan pair structure. Assume:

(i) The grading R is fully idempotent (every root space contains a non-degenerate idempotent giving the expected Peirce decomposition consistent with R).

(ii) The grading R is a division grading: for every root α ∈ R_1 and every nonzero x ∈ V_α, the operator Q(x) restricts to an invertible F-linear map from the opposite root space V_{-α} onto V_α.

Let St(V, R) denote the Steinberg group associated to (V, R), defined by generators x_α(v) for α ∈ R_1, v ∈ V_α subject to the standard Steinberg relations attached to the root grading. Recall that St(V, R) is said to be centrally closed if its canonical central extension (the universal central extension in the appropriate category) is trivial, i.e. the kernel of the natural projection from a universal central extension to St(V, R) is trivial.

A finite list T of "exceptional small-field restrictions" is fixed in advance, consisting of pairs (R, F) where R is a root system of rank between 2 and 4 and F is a field belonging to a small finite list of small fields (e.g. small finite fields such as F_2, F_3, F_4, depending on the type of R).

Question. Is the following statement true? For every Jordan pair V over F with fully idempotent division root grading R of rank r with 2 ≤ r ≤ 4, if the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, then:

(a) dim_F V_α = 1 for every α ∈ R_1, and

(b) the pair (R, F) lies in the prescribed exceptional list T.
category_tag: Steinberg groups of root-graded Jordan pairs
status_search_result: The statement is presented as a conjecture based on preliminary investigations, and web searches for "central closedness" of Steinberg groups for root-graded Jordan pairs in low rank do not surface a published proof or refutation. Related work on Steinberg groups for root systems (e.g., by Loos–Neher and others) establishes central closedness in higher-rank or 3-spherical cases, but the precise low-rank (rank 2 to 4) division-grading characterization appears not to be settled.

context_brief: Centrality of the kernel of pi
original_question: Let pi: St(V, R) -> PE(V) be the homomorphism from Theorem 2.11(a), and assume the root system R is irreducible of finite rank. Find sufficient conditions under which the kernel Ker(pi) is central.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V = (V^+, V^-)$ be a Jordan pair equipped with an idempotent root grading $\Gamma = (V_\alpha)_{\alpha \in R}$ by an irreducible locally finite root system $R$ of finite rank, in the sense of Loos–Neher. Associated with $(V, \Gamma)$ are:

(i) the projective elementary group $\mathrm{PE}(V)$, generated inside the automorphism group of $V$ by the elementary inner automorphisms determined by elements of the root spaces $V_\alpha$; and

(ii) the Steinberg group $\mathrm{St}(V, R)$, defined by generators $x_\alpha(v)$ for $\alpha \in R$ and $v \in V_\alpha$, subject to the additivity relations in each $V_\alpha$ and the standard Steinberg-type commutator relations modeled on those satisfied in $\mathrm{PE}(V)$.

There is a canonical surjective group homomorphism
$$\pi : \mathrm{St}(V, R) \longrightarrow \mathrm{PE}(V)$$
sending each generator $x_\alpha(v)$ to the corresponding elementary automorphism of $V$.

Determine sufficient conditions on the pair $(V, \Gamma)$ (and on the irreducible finite-rank root system $R$) under which the kernel $\ker(\pi)$ is contained in the center of $\mathrm{St}(V, R)$, i.e., conditions guaranteeing that $\pi$ is a central extension.
status_search_result: The literature establishes centrality and universality of $\ker(\pi)$ when $R$ has infinite rank (or rank $\geq 5$ in some settings), but the finite-rank case is explicitly raised as an open problem requiring sufficient conditions; no comprehensive solution was located.

paper_title: The Erdős-Ulam problem, Lang's conjecture, and uniformity
original_question: Does there exist a subset S of the Euclidean plane R^2 such that the distance between any two points of S is rational and S is dense in R^2 with respect to the usual Euclidean topology?
self_contained_problem: Call a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a *rational distance set* if for every pair of points $p, q \in S$ the Euclidean distance $\|p - q\|$ is a rational number. Does there exist a rational distance set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is dense in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with respect to the standard Euclidean topology?
status_search_result: The Erdős–Ulam question of whether a dense rational distance set exists in the plane remains open. Conditional negative answers are known: Shaffaf and Tao independently showed the Bombieri–Lang conjecture implies no such set exists, and Pasten showed the abc conjecture also implies a negative answer. Solymosi–de Zeeuw proved related results restricting infinite rational-distance subsets of algebraic curves to lines and circles.

context_brief: Seven-point rational distance set in general position
original_question: Does there exist a set S of seven points in R^2 such that every pairwise Euclidean distance between points of S is rational, no three points of S lie on one line, and no four points of S lie on one circle?
self_contained_problem:
A rational distance set is a finite subset $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a rational number. A set of seven points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is said to be in general position if no three of them are collinear and no four of them lie on a common circle.

Question: Does there exist a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of seven points that is simultaneously a rational distance set and in general position?
status_search_result: The problem was posed by Erdős and answered affirmatively by Kreisel and Kurz (2008), who explicitly constructed a seven-point rational distance set in general position (no 3 on a line, no 4 on a circle). The analogous question for 8 or more points remains open.

paper_title: The Erdős-Ulam problem, Lang's conjecture, and uniformity
context_brief: Unbounded cardinalities of rational distance sets in general position
original_question: Do there exist rational distance sets in R^2 in general position whose cardinalities are larger than any fixed constant, where a rational distance set has rational pairwise Euclidean distances and a finite set S of size n is in general position when no n − 4 of its points lie on one line and no n − 3 of its points lie on one circle?
self_contained_problem:
A rational distance set is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a rational number. A finite subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of cardinality $n$ is said to be in general position if no $n-4$ of its points are collinear and no $n-3$ of its points lie on a single circle.

Question: Does there exist, for every positive integer $N$, a rational distance set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is in general position and satisfies $|S| > N$? Equivalently, are the cardinalities of rational distance sets in general position unbounded?
status_search_result: The question is open unconditionally. It is known that, conditional on Lang's conjecture (and earlier, the Bombieri–Lang conjecture for surfaces), the cardinalities of rational distance sets in general position are uniformly bounded, so under those conjectures the answer would be negative. No unconditional resolution has appeared.

original_question: Develop an algorithmic procedure that, given an ordinary differential equation with the Painleve property, decides whether the equation can be solved in terms of one of the Painleve equations or an associated Painleve sigma-equation.
self_contained_problem:
An ordinary differential equation is said to have the Painlevé property if every movable singularity of every solution (i.e., a singularity whose location depends on the initial conditions) is a pole. The six Painlevé equations P_I, ..., P_VI are the canonical second-order ODEs with the Painlevé property whose general solutions define new transcendental functions (the Painlevé transcendents); to each Painlevé equation P_J there is also an associated Hamiltonian "sigma-equation" (the Painlevé sigma-equation) satisfied by an auxiliary Hamiltonian function.

Problem. Devise an algorithmic procedure (taking as input an ordinary differential equation that is known to have the Painlevé property) which decides, in finitely many effective steps, whether the given equation can be solved in closed form in terms of one of the Painlevé equations P_I,...,P_VI or one of the associated Painlevé sigma-equations, and, when it can, produces an explicit transformation reducing the given equation to that Painlevé (or sigma-) equation.
status_search_result: The Painlevé equivalence problem remains an active area of research with no fully general algorithm known. Recent work using algebro-geometric methods (Okamoto's spaces of initial conditions, iterative blow-up regularisation) has produced essentially algorithmic step-by-step identification procedures that work for specific classes of systems (e.g., Bureau–Guillot systems, certain constrained 3D systems, identifications with Painlevé VI), so the problem is partially solved in those settings but a complete general algorithm has not been established.

original_question: Can numerical methods that exploit the integrable structure of the Painleve equations do better than standard Runge-Kutta methods and related generic ordinary-differential-equation solvers when computing Painleve solutions?
self_contained_problem:
The six Painlevé equations P_I, P_II, ..., P_VI are a distinguished family of second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equations in the complex plane whose solutions (the Painlevé transcendents) define new transcendental functions and possess a rich integrable structure: each admits an isomonodromic Lax-pair representation, a Riemann–Hilbert problem characterization, Bäcklund transformations, tau-function descriptions, and (for special parameter values) hierarchies of rational and special-function solutions.

Standard initial-value solvers (e.g., explicit and embedded Runge–Kutta methods such as RK4, Dormand–Prince, and related adaptive ODE schemes) treat these equations as generic stiff or non-stiff nonlinear ODEs and do not make use of any of the integrable structure listed above.

Problem. Design and analyze numerical methods for computing solutions of the Painlevé equations along real or complex paths that explicitly exploit their integrable structure (for example, by basing the computation on the associated isomonodromic Riemann–Hilbert problem, on the Lax-pair / isomonodromic deformation, on Bäcklund transformations, on tau-function identities, or on Hamiltonian/symplectic structure preserving discretizations), and prove that such methods can achieve strictly better performance — in accuracy, stability across movable singularities, global validity in the complex plane, or computational cost — than what is attainable by Runge–Kutta methods and other generic ODE solvers. Equivalently: do there exist integrability-aware algorithms that demonstrably outperform generic Runge–Kutta-type ODE solvers for the Painlevé transcendents?
status_search_result: There exist published Riemann–Hilbert / isomonodromic numerical methods (e.g., Olver, Trogdon, Bornemann and collaborators) that compute Painlevé transcendents accurately throughout the complex plane, including across the Stokes lines and near movable poles, where standard Runge–Kutta solvers degrade or fail. These works demonstrate concrete advantages of integrability-based algorithms. However, the broader question of systematically characterizing when and by how much integrable-structure-aware methods outperform generic ODE solvers across all six Painlevé equations and regimes remains an active research direction rather than a closed problem, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Should numerical work on Painleve equations use integrable discretizations, namely discrete Painleve equations that tend to the associated continuous Painleve equations in an appropriate continuum limit, instead of relying only on generic discretizations of the differential equations?
self_contained_problem: The six Painlevé equations are a distinguished family of second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equations whose solutions (the Painlevé transcendents) define new special functions and arise widely in mathematical physics, random matrix theory, and integrable systems. In parallel, there exist discrete Painlevé equations: integrable second-order nonlinear difference equations that, under appropriate continuum limits of their parameters and step sizes, converge to the continuous Painlevé equations. These discrete equations preserve key structural features of the continuous theory (such as affine Weyl group symmetries, isomonodromic deformation interpretations, and Lax pair structures), in contrast to a generic finite-difference or Runge–Kutta–type discretization which need not preserve any such structure.\n\nProblem. Determine whether numerical computation of solutions to the continuous Painlevé equations should be carried out via integrable discretizations (i.e., discrete Painlevé equations admitting the prescribed continuum limit to the target Painlevé equation) rather than via generic discretizations of the differential equations. Specifically, establish (or refute) that integrable discretization yields demonstrably superior numerical behavior — for example, in long-time accuracy, preservation of pole/movable-singularity structure, parameter dependence, connection-problem asymptotics, or stability — compared with standard general-purpose ODE discretizations applied to the same Painlevé equation. Provide rigorous comparative error and stability analyses, or counterexamples showing that integrable discretization offers no systematic advantage.
status_search_result: The question of whether integrable (geometric/structure-preserving) discretizations of the Painlevé equations should be preferred for numerical work is posed as an open methodological question. While discrete Painlevé equations are well studied as integrable systems and some numerical experiments using them exist, no general theorem or consensus establishes their systematic numerical superiority over generic discretizations across the full Painlevé hierarchy. The problem appears to remain open as a research direction.

paper_title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions
original_question: Can a classical de Sitter solution of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources, in the standard smeared compactification ansatz on a compact 6-dimensional group manifold with constant fluxes, simultaneously have large internal volume, weak string coupling, a bounded number of orientifold planes, and quantized fluxes, or is that combination impossible?
self_contained_problem:
Consider ten-dimensional type II supergravity (type IIA or type IIB) compactified on a compact six-dimensional group manifold M_6 (a quotient of a six-dimensional Lie group by a discrete subgroup), with the following standard "smeared" ansatz:

(i) The ten-dimensional spacetime is a warped product dS_4 × M_6 of four-dimensional de Sitter space and M_6, in the regime where warping is dropped and the metric on M_6 is left-invariant.

(ii) The bosonic content includes the dilaton φ (assumed constant on M_6), the NSNS three-form H, and the RR field strengths F_q. All form fluxes are taken to be left-invariant (constant) on M_6.

(iii) Sources are present in the form of Op-planes and/or Dp-branes (for some fixed p ∈ {3,4,5,6,7,8}) wrapping calibrated cycles, smeared over their transverse directions, with their localized contributions to the Bianchi identities replaced by their integrated charges.

For such a solution, define:
 • The internal volume V = vol(M_6) measured in string units ℓ_s = √α′.
 • The string coupling g_s = e^{φ}.
 • The orientifold number N_O = total number of Op-planes appearing in the source content (counted with multiplicity in the relevant homology class).
 • Quantized fluxes: the periods of H/(2π α′) and of the F_q/(2π α′)^{(q)} over integral cycles of M_6 are required to take integer values.

Question: Does there exist any classical de Sitter solution of the above kind that simultaneously satisfies all four of the following conditions?

 (a) Large internal volume: V can be made arbitrarily large (V → ∞);
 (b) Weak string coupling: g_s can be made arbitrarily small (g_s → 0);
 (c) Bounded orientifold number: N_O remains bounded by a fixed constant independent of the limits in (a), (b);
 (d) Properly quantized fluxes as defined above.

Equivalently: prove or disprove that no solution in this class can realize (a)–(d) simultaneously.
status_search_result: The conjecture remains an open problem. Searches turn up only partial results and concrete case studies (e.g. work on parametric control of classical de Sitter solutions in 2024 and "Almost classical de Sitter?" JHEP 2024), with no general proof or counterexample. Recent papers explicitly describe the conjecture as motivated and tested in particular cases without a general proof.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
original_question: Above roughly 10^19.4 eV, are the differences between the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray energy spectra measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory and the Telescope Array caused by experiment-specific systematic effects in energy reconstruction and calibration, or by astrophysical differences because the observatories view different parts of the sky?
self_contained_problem:
Two large ground-based ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatories independently measure the all-particle differential energy spectrum J(E) of cosmic rays at energies E ≳ 10^19 eV. One observatory is located in the Southern Hemisphere and views the sky in the declination band roughly −90° ≤ δ ≲ +45°; the other is located in the Northern Hemisphere and views roughly −16° ≲ δ ≤ +90°. Each observatory reconstructs primary energies via its own calibration chain (combining surface-detector signals with fluorescence-detector calorimetric measurements) and reports its spectrum with associated systematic uncertainties on the absolute energy scale.

When the two reported spectra J_A(E) and J_T(E) are compared above approximately E* = 10^19.4 eV, statistically significant differences remain even after applying any single global rescaling E → (1+α)E of one observatory's energy scale relative to the other (i.e., no energy-independent shift α can simultaneously reconcile the spectra in this regime, in particular reconciling the inferred flux-suppression energies).

Determine which of the following is the dominant cause of these residual differences above ~10^19.4 eV:

(a) experiment-specific systematic effects in energy reconstruction and calibration that depend on energy (so that the effective miscalibration grows with E and cannot be captured by a constant rescaling), or

(b) genuine astrophysical anisotropy of the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sky, so that the two observatories sample intrinsically different flux distributions because their fields of view (declination bands) cover different regions of the celestial sphere.

Equivalently, decide whether the residual discrepancy is removed once one allows for an energy-dependent (but isotropic) inter-observatory energy-scale correction, or whether it persists when the comparison is restricted to the common declination band accessible to both instruments and therefore must be attributed to a declination-dependent astrophysical flux.
status_search_result: Recent joint Auger–Telescope Array working-group analyses (2024–2025) provide strong evidence that an energy-independent rescaling cannot eliminate the discrepancy above ~10^19.4 eV: the inferred suppression energies differ by ~42% (Auger ~48 EeV vs TA ~68 EeV, >3σ). Telescope Array has reported a declination-dependent feature in its spectrum, and updated comparisons indicate the tension is largely accounted for by a combination of an energy-dependent energy-scale mismatch and astrophysical (declination-dependent) effects, with proposed source-based explanations also under discussion. A definitive single-cause resolution has not yet been established, so the question is partially solved.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
original_question: What is the mass composition of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays at the highest energies, especially around and above 10^20 eV, and does the observed trend toward heavier primaries near ultrahigh energies continue, flatten, or change when larger statistics and better hadronic-interaction modeling become available?
self_contained_problem:
Ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) are charged particles (atomic nuclei) of astrophysical origin observed with energies exceeding roughly 10^18 eV. Their primary mass is inferred indirectly from extensive air showers, principally via the depth of shower maximum X_max, whose first two moments (mean and standard deviation) are interpreted through hadronic-interaction Monte Carlo models to estimate the fractional abundances of light, intermediate, and heavy nuclear species as functions of primary energy E.

Existing measurements indicate that the mean primary mass decreases with E up to about 10^18.3 eV (the "ankle" of the energy spectrum) and then increases (composition becomes heavier) as E approaches 10^20 eV; however, no composition fractions have been established at and above E ≈ 10^20 eV due to limited event statistics and uncertainties in hadronic-interaction models.

Problem. With substantially increased exposure and improved hadronic-interaction modeling:

(a) Determine the mass composition (the fractional abundances of proton, helium, nitrogen/CNO, and iron-like primary nuclei) of UHECRs at energies E ≥ 10^20 eV.

(b) Decide whether the observed trend of increasing mean primary mass with energy in the range 10^18.3 eV ≲ E ≲ 10^20 eV continues monotonically toward heavier primaries above 10^20 eV, flattens to an approximately constant heavy composition, or changes character (for example, by re-emergence of a light component) at the highest energies.

Provide quantitative composition fractions with uncertainties at E ≥ 10^20 eV and a determination of the qualitative behavior in (b).
status_search_result: Recent work by the Pierre Auger Collaboration (2024) using deep-learning reconstruction has extended X_max-based composition measurements up to ~10^20 eV (100 EeV), indicating that the composition becomes increasingly heavier and purer with energy and is incompatible with a large light-nuclei fraction in the 50–100 EeV range, with three break features near spectral features. However, robust composition fractions strictly above 10^20 eV remain limited by statistics and hadronic-interaction-model uncertainties, so the question is best characterized as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
original_question: How does the average rigidity R = E/Z of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays evolve with energy, and does that evolution make magnetic deflections small enough at the highest energies for anisotropy and source-correlation studies, despite the simultaneous trend toward heavier average mass?
self_contained_problem:
Ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays are charged nuclei with energies E ≳ 10^18 eV arriving at Earth from astrophysical sources. For a nucleus of charge number Z and energy E, define its magnetic rigidity by R = E/Z. The typical angular deflection of such a particle traveling a distance L through a (turbulent or coherent) magnetic field of characteristic strength B scales inversely with rigidity, so that small deflections—and hence the feasibility of identifying point sources or large-scale anisotropies pointing back to astrophysical accelerators—require sufficiently large R.

Let ⟨ln A⟩(E) denote the energy-dependent mean of the logarithm of the cosmic-ray mass number, and let ⟨ln Z⟩(E) denote the corresponding mean of ln Z, both inferred from air-shower observables (such as depth of shower maximum X_max and its fluctuations) under a chosen hadronic interaction model. Define the average (logarithmic) rigidity by

  ⟨ln R⟩(E) = ln E − ⟨ln Z⟩(E).

Determine the function ⟨ln R⟩(E) (equivalently, the energy dependence of the mean rigidity ⟨R⟩(E) = ⟨E/Z⟩) of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays across the range roughly 10^18 eV ≤ E ≤ 10^20.5 eV, and decide whether ⟨R⟩(E) grows fast enough with E that, given realistic Galactic and extragalactic magnetic-field models, the typical magnetic deflection at the highest observed energies becomes small enough (e.g., on the order of a few degrees or less) to permit meaningful anisotropy and source-correlation studies, despite the simultaneous observed trend of increasing average mass ⟨A⟩(E) with E.
status_search_result: Recent reviews and observational analyses (Pierre Auger and Telescope Array, 2021–2025) confirm that the mean rigidity of UHECRs increases with energy and that the dipole amplitude grows with energy consistent with rigidity-ordered deflections, but the precise evolution of ⟨R⟩(E) and whether deflections at the highest energies are small enough for robust source identification remain unresolved due to mass-composition uncertainties and limited statistics. The question is still considered an open problem in UHECR research.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
context_brief: Resolution and exposure for source searches
original_question: What event-by-event energy resolution, mass resolution, and total exposure are needed for future ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatories to identify individual sources while limiting spillover from lower-energy isotropic events and limiting the blurring produced by heavier, more strongly deflected primaries?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a future observatory that detects ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), with each detected air shower yielding an estimate of the primary particle's energy E and mass number A. Suppose the true differential flux dN/dE follows a steeply falling spectrum (with a suppression above roughly 4×10^19 eV), and that events with true energy below a threshold E_thresh are isotropically distributed on the celestial sphere, while events with true energy above E_thresh are clustered around a discrete set of astrophysical point sources. Reconstructed energies are subject to a Gaussian (or similar) event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, and reconstructed mass numbers are subject to a mass resolution σ_lnA. Heavier primaries are deflected by intervening magnetic fields by an angle proportional to their charge Z, broadening the apparent source spots.

Determine quantitative requirements on (i) the event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, (ii) the event-by-event mass resolution σ_lnA, and (iii) the total integrated exposure (in km² sr yr) such that, after applying energy and mass cuts above E_thresh, the resulting sample (a) contains less than a specified fraction f_bg of isotropic spillover events from the steeply falling sub-threshold population that pass cuts due to finite energy resolution, and (b) localizes individual point sources to within a specified angular scale despite magnetic deflections of heavier primaries, while retaining enough events above threshold to detect the sources at a prescribed statistical significance.

In particular, quantify how relaxing the energy resolution from 10% to 30% must be compensated by an increase in exposure given the steepness of the spectrum, and identify the minimum mass-resolution requirement that suppresses heavy-primary blurring of source images.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
original_question: What are the strength, structure, and local-universe distribution of Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields, and how do these fields deflect and time-delay ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays strongly enough to affect spectrum, composition, anisotropy, and the feasibility of charged-particle astronomy?
self_contained_problem:
Determine the strength, spatial structure, and local-universe distribution of Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields, and quantify their effect on the propagation of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (charged nuclei with energies above roughly 10^18 eV). Specifically:

1. Provide a model of the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) consisting of a regular (coherent) component B_reg(x) and a turbulent component B_turb(x) defined on the Milky Way volume, including disk and halo contributions, with field strengths typically of order microgauss.

2. Provide a model of the extragalactic magnetic field (EGMF) B_ext(x) on the cosmological volume out to ~100 Mpc, characterized by a coherence length λ_B and an rms strength B_rms, including its correlation with the large-scale structure of the local universe (filaments, voids, clusters).

3. For a charged particle of charge Ze, energy E, and rigidity R = E/Z propagating along a path from a source at distance D to Earth, compute:
   (a) the integrated deflection angle θ(E,Z,direction) induced by B_reg and the rms deflection induced by B_turb and B_ext,
   (b) the time delay Δt(E,Z,D) relative to rectilinear propagation at the speed of light,
   (c) the resulting smearing of arrival directions and its impact on the observed energy spectrum, mass composition, and large- and small-scale anisotropies.

4. Determine quantitatively under what combinations of (B_reg, B_turb, B_ext, λ_B, source distribution, composition) the deflections are small enough (e.g., ≲ a few degrees at the highest rigidities) for charged-particle astronomy — i.e., the unambiguous identification of individual ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sources — to be feasible.
status_search_result: Recent reviews and modeling efforts (e.g., updated GMF models by Jansson–Farrar variants and 2024–2025 work on coherent+random Galactic fields, as well as constrained MHD simulations of the local extragalactic magnetic field) report that significant uncertainties remain in both Galactic and extragalactic magnetic field strength and structure, and that UHECR deflections—and thus the feasibility of charged-particle astronomy—are still model-dependent. The problem is widely regarded as open.

paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
original_question: Which accelerator, fixed-target, forward-physics, and air-shower measurements are needed to improve hadronic-interaction models enough to reduce systematic uncertainties in ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray mass-composition inference, especially for pion-proton, kaon-proton, pion-light-nuclei, kaon-light-nuclei, proton-oxygen, and forward secondary-particle production?
self_contained_problem:
In the study of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (with primary energies extending up to center-of-mass nucleon-nucleon energies of order √s ∼ 400 TeV), the inference of the mass composition of primary cosmic rays from extensive air-shower observables (such as the depth of shower maximum X_max and its fluctuations, muon content, and longitudinal profile) is limited by systematic uncertainties in hadronic-interaction Monte Carlo models. These models must extrapolate accelerator data to (i) center-of-mass energies far beyond those accessible at current colliders, (ii) forward phase-space regions (large pseudorapidity / large Feynman-x) not covered by central detectors, and (iii) projectile–target combinations not measured experimentally.

Identify and specify a concrete program of accelerator (collider), fixed-target, forward-physics, and air-shower measurements that would, if carried out, reduce these systematic uncertainties to a level sufficient for unambiguous mass-composition inference at ultrahigh energies. In particular, determine the required measurements (energy ranges, kinematic coverage, and observables — total and inelastic cross sections together with leading-secondary momentum and multiplicity distributions) for each of the following interaction channels:

1. pion–proton (π–p),
2. kaon–proton (K–p),
3. pion–light-nuclei (π–A, with A a light nucleus such as carbon, nitrogen, or oxygen),
4. kaon–light-nuclei (K–A),
5. proton–oxygen (p–O), including the feasibility and benefit of running such collisions at the LHC,
6. forward secondary-particle production (production spectra of π^±, K^±, K_L, neutrons, protons, and Λ at large Feynman-x in proton–proton, proton–nucleus, and pion–nucleus collisions).

For each channel, state the kinematic coverage (√s, x_F or pseudorapidity, p_T) needed, and quantify how the resulting reduction in uncertainty of the predicted air-shower observables would translate into improved discrimination among primary mass groups (proton, helium, CNO, iron) at energies E ≳ 10^18 eV.
status_search_result: This is a programmatic open question in ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray physics. Several of the requested measurements are being pursued (e.g., the LHCf forward measurements, the LHC oxygen-beam run planned/performed in Run 3, NA61/SHINE pion-carbon data), but the full program needed to fully resolve hadronic-model uncertainties in mass-composition inference has not been completed, and the question remains active in the field as of 2026.

paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
context_brief: Integrality of integral-form Jack superpolynomial coefficients
original_question: Let J_Λ^(α) denote the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial indexed by a superpartition Λ, defined by J_Λ^(α)=v_Λ(α)P_Λ^(α), and let its monomial expansion be J_Λ^(α)=Σ_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions Ω≤Λ, each expansion coefficient v_{ΛΩ}(α) is a polynomial in α with integer coefficients, i.e. v_{ΛΩ}(α)∈ℤ[α]?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A superpartition is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$, where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_m)$ is a strictly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda_{m+1},\Lambda_{m+2},\dots)$ is a partition (weakly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers). Superpartitions index a basis of the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, which is the ring of polynomials in commuting variables $x_1,x_2,\dots$ and anticommuting variables $\theta_1,\theta_2,\dots$ that are invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group permuting simultaneously the $x_i$ and the $\theta_i$.

For each superpartition $\Lambda$, let $m_\Lambda$ denote the monomial symmetric function in superspace indexed by $\Lambda$. Equip the set of superpartitions of a fixed bidegree with the dominance order $\le$. The Jack symmetric functions in superspace $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda$ (depending on a parameter $\alpha$) are the unique basis characterized by:
(i) $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = m_\Lambda + \sum_{\Omega<\Lambda} c_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega$,
(ii) orthogonality with respect to the natural one-parameter scalar product on superspace.

Define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial by
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta) := v_\Lambda(\alpha)\, P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta),$$
where $v_\Lambda(\alpha)$ is the natural normalization factor (the product over the cells of the diagram of $\Lambda$ of the appropriate hook-type linear factors in $\alpha$) that generalizes the classical normalization for Jack polynomials. Expanding in the monomial basis,
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = \sum_{\Omega \le \Lambda} v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega,$$
with $v_{\Lambda\Lambda}(\alpha) = v_\Lambda(\alpha)$.

Question. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions $\Omega \le \Lambda$, the coefficient $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)$ is a polynomial in $\alpha$ with integer coefficients, i.e., $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha) \in \mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$?
status_search_result: Web searches surface foundational works on Jack polynomials in superspace (e.g., the determinantal-formulas paper of Desrosiers–Lapointe–Mathieu and the Pieri-rules paper) and related Macdonald-superspace positivity conjectures, but no source confirming or refuting the integrality conjecture $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\in\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ for the integral-form Jack superpolynomials was located. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
context_brief: Basis conjecture for admissible Jack superpolynomials
original_question: Fix k≥1 and N≥k+1, and let F_N^(k) be the ideal of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables x_1,…,x_N and N odd variables θ_1,…,θ_N over ℂ that vanish whenever x_1=x_2=⋯=x_{k+1}. For α_{k,2}=-(k+1), do the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_{k,2}) indexed by all (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions Λ form a basis of F_N^(k)?
self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{C}$. Let $N\ge 1$ and consider the superspace algebra in $N$ commuting variables $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and $N$ anticommuting (Grassmann) variables $	heta_1,\dots,	heta_N$, where $	heta_i	heta_j=-	heta_j	heta_i$ and $	heta_i^2=0$. The symmetric group $S_N$ acts diagonally by simultaneous permutation of $(x_i,	heta_i)$, and a superpolynomial $f(x,	heta)$ is called symmetric if it is invariant under this diagonal action. Denote the algebra of symmetric superpolynomials by $\mathcal{S}_N$.

A superpartition $\Lambda$ with exactly $N$ parts is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1^a>\Lambda_2^a>\cdots>\Lambda_m^a\ge 0)$ is a strict partition (the antisymmetric/fermionic part) and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda^s_1\ge\Lambda^s_2\ge\cdots\ge 0)$ is a partition (the symmetric/bosonic part), with the total number of (allowed-zero) parts equal to $N$. Associated to $\Lambda$ are two ordinary partitions, $\Lambda^*$ obtained by reordering the concatenation $(\Lambda^a,\Lambda^s)$ into a weakly decreasing sequence, and $\Lambda^\circledast$ obtained from $\Lambda^*$ by adding $1$ to each entry of $\Lambda^a$ before reordering. For fixed integers $k\ge 1$ and $r\ge 2$, $\Lambda$ is called $(k,r,N)$-admissible if
$$\Lambda_i^\circledast - \Lambda_{i+k}^* \ge r \qquad \text{for all } 1\le i\le N-k.$$

For a parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^\times$, let $P_\Lambda^{(\alpha)}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N)$ denote the Jack superpolynomial indexed by the superpartition $\Lambda$ (the unique simultaneous eigenfunction of the supersymmetric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland Hamiltonians with parameter $\alpha$ that is upper-triangular, in the dominance ordering on superpartitions, with respect to the basis of monomial symmetric superpolynomials, with leading monomial indexed by $\Lambda$).

Fix $k\ge 1$ and $N\ge k+1$, and set $\alpha_{k,2}=-(k+1)$. Let $F_N^{(k)}\subseteq\mathcal{S}_N$ be the ideal consisting of all symmetric superpolynomials $f(x,\theta)$ that vanish whenever $x_1=x_2=\cdots=x_{k+1}$.

Prove or disprove: the family
$$\bigl\{\, P_\Lambda^{(\alpha_{k,2})}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N) \;:\; \Lambda \text{ is } (k,2,N)\text{-admissible}\,\bigr\}$$
forms a $\mathbb{C}$-vector space basis of $F_N^{(k)}$.
status_search_result: Web searches for results on the conjecture that Jack superpolynomials at α = −(k+1) indexed by (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions form a basis of the vanishing ideal $F_N^{(k)}$ did not surface a definitive proof or disproof. Related work establishes clustering properties and connections with super-Virasoro ideals, but the basis statement itself does not appear to have been confirmed as resolved in the literature accessible via the search.

paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
context_brief: Second duality conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials
original_question: Let ρ̂_{q,t} be the automorphism of the supersymmetric function ring defined on power sums by ρ̂_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}(1-q^r)/(1-t^r)·p_r and ρ̂_{q,t}(~p_r)=Σ_{Λ⊢(r|1)} z_Λ^{-1} ω_Λ ∏_i(1-q^{Λ^s_i}) p_Λ. For every superpartition Λ, does this automorphism satisfy the second duality relation ρ̂_{q,t}(P_Λ(q,t)) = t^{|Λ'^a|} Q_{Λ'}(t,q)?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, generated over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$ by the bosonic power sums $p_r$ ($r\ge 1$) and the fermionic power sums $\tilde p_r$ ($r\ge 0$), where superpartitions $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ have an antisymmetric part $\Lambda^a$ (a strict partition, possibly containing $0$) and a symmetric part $\Lambda^s$ (an ordinary partition). For a superpartition $\Lambda$ with $m$ fermionic parts, write $p_\Lambda=\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_1}\cdots\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_m}\,p_{\Lambda^s_1}p_{\Lambda^s_2}\cdots$, and let $z_\Lambda$ and $\omega_\Lambda=\pm1$ be the standard combinatorial constants associated to $\Lambda$ in superspace. The conjugate superpartition is denoted $\Lambda'$, with antisymmetric part $\Lambda'^a$.

Define the $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$-algebra automorphism $\hat\rho_{q,t}$ of this ring by
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}\,\frac{1-q^r}{1-t^r}\,p_r\qquad(r\ge 1),$$
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=\sum_{\Lambda\vdash (r\mid 1)} z_\Lambda^{-1}\,\omega_\Lambda\,\prod_i\bigl(1-q^{\Lambda^s_i}\bigr)\,p_\Lambda\qquad(r\ge 0),$$
where the sum is over superpartitions of bidegree $(r\mid 1)$ (total bosonic degree $r$ with exactly one fermionic part).

Let $P_\Lambda(q,t)$ and $Q_\Lambda(q,t)$ denote the two normalizations of the Macdonald superpolynomials indexed by superpartitions $\Lambda$.

Prove or disprove: for every superpartition $\Lambda$,
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}\bigl(P_\Lambda(q,t)\bigr)=t^{|\Lambda'^a|}\,Q_{\Lambda'}(t,q).$$

The conjecture appears to remain open, though no explicit confirmation of its current status was located.

paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
original_question: Let J_Λ(q,t)=h_Λ^{lo}(q,t)P_Λ(q,t) be the integral form of the Macdonald superpolynomial, let φ_t be the automorphism defined by φ_t(p_r)=(1-t^r)^{-1}p_r and φ_t(~p_s)=~p_s, and let H_Λ(q,t)=φ_t(J_Λ(q,t)). When H_Λ(q,t) is expanded in the Schur-superpolynomial basis as H_Λ(q,t)=Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t)s_Ω, are all coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the algebra A of symmetric functions in superspace over Q(q,t), generated by the commuting power sums p_r (r ≥ 1) and the anticommuting power sums ~p_s (s ≥ 0). Symmetric functions in superspace are indexed by superpartitions Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s), where Λ^a is a strict partition of distinct nonnegative parts (the "anticommuting" sector) and Λ^s is an ordinary partition.

Let {P_Λ(q,t)}_Λ denote the Macdonald superpolynomials, the basis of A characterized by suitable triangularity and orthogonality with respect to the (q,t)-deformed scalar product on superspace. Let h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) be the "lower-hook" normalization factor, and define the integral form
   J_Λ(q,t) = h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) · P_Λ(q,t).

Let φ_t : A → A be the Q(q,t)-algebra automorphism determined by
   φ_t(p_r) = (1 − t^r)^{−1} p_r  for all r ≥ 1,   φ_t(~p_s) = ~p_s  for all s ≥ 0,
and define the modified Macdonald superpolynomial
   H_Λ(q,t) = φ_t( J_Λ(q,t) ).

Let {s_Ω}_Ω denote the Schur superpolynomial basis of A. Expand
   H_Λ(q,t) = Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) · s_Ω,
defining the (q,t)-Kostka coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) in superspace.

Prove or disprove: for every pair of superpartitions Λ and Ω, the coefficient K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) lies in N[q,t], i.e. is a polynomial in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients.
status_search_result: The (q,t)-Kostka positivity conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials was formulated by Blondeau-Fournier, Desrosiers, Lapointe, and Mathieu (2012), generalizing Macdonald's classical positivity (proved by Haiman, 2001) to superspace. Searches for proofs through 2024–2025 turn up only restatements of the conjecture, partial/related results (e.g. nonnegativity of stable-limit double Macdonald (q,t)-Kostka coefficients and Schur-positivity in special cases), but no proof of the full superspace positivity statement. The conjecture appears to remain open.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L × L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d,D\ge 2$ and $L\ge 2$. A translationally invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on the $L\times L$ torus is determined by a single local tensor
$$A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D},$$
with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ associated to the four lattice directions. Placing a copy of $A$ at every vertex of the torus and contracting all virtual indices along edges shared by neighbouring sites yields the PEPS vector $|\Psi_A\rangle\in(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L^2}$.

For a square region $R\subset\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L$ of size $n\times n$, let $\mathcal{V}_R:(\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4n}\to(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$ be the linear map obtained by contracting the $n^2$ copies of $A$ inside $R$, viewing the $4n$ virtual indices on $\partial R$ as input and the $n^2$ physical indices as output. Let $\Pi_R$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $\mathrm{Range}(\mathcal{V}_R)\subset(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$, and define the local term $h_R:=\mathbb{1}-\Pi_R\ge 0$. The parent Hamiltonian is
$$H \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L}\tau(h_R),$$
where $\tau$ acts on operators by lattice translation. By construction $H\ge 0$ and $H|\Psi_A\rangle=0$.

Problem. Determine the weakest possible conditions on the tensor $A$ together with the smallest possible side length $n$ of the square region $R$ such that, for all sufficiently large $L$, the following two properties simultaneously hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|\Psi_A\rangle$ is the unique ground state of $H$ (so that the kernel of $H$ is one-dimensional);
\item[(ii)] $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground state that is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $L$.
\end{enumerate}
Identify the minimal hypotheses on $A$ (e.g. injectivity-type, normality-type, or strictly weaker algebraic/spectral conditions on the transfer operator of $A$) and the minimal $n$ for which (i) and (ii) can be guaranteed.

However, identifying the minimal conditions on the tensor and the minimal region size that simultaneously guarantee uniqueness and a uniform spectral gap of the parent Hamiltonian on a 2D torus remains an open problem; in 2D the gap can fail even under injectivity, and no minimal characterization is known.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: For a normal translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index, meaning the smallest scale at which the associated tensor becomes injective?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and $D\ge 1$. A translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) on $n$ sites with physical dimension $d$ and bond dimension $D$ is determined by a tensor $A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}$, regarded as a tuple $(A_1,\dots,A_d)$ of $D\times D$ matrices. For each integer $L\ge 1$, define the linear map
$$\Gamma_L(A):\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L},\qquad X\mapsto \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_L=1}^{d}\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(X\,A_{i_1}A_{i_2}\cdots A_{i_L}\bigr)\,|i_1\cdots i_L\rangle.$$
Equivalently, $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective iff the family $\{A_{i_1}\cdots A_{i_L}\}_{i_1,\dots,i_L}$ spans the full matrix algebra $M_D(\mathbb{C})$.

The tensor $A$ is called normal if there exists some finite $L$ for which $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective. For a normal tensor $A$, its injectivity index is
$$\iota(A)\;=\;\min\{\,L\ge 1\,:\,\Gamma_L(A)\text{ is injective}\,\}.$$

Problem. Determine the exact best possible upper bound, as a function of the bond dimension $D$ alone, for the injectivity index of a normal translationally invariant MPS. That is, find the smallest function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\iota(A)\;\le\;f(D)$$
holds for every normal tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$ (over all physical dimensions $d$), and exhibit normal tensors achieving (or asymptotically achieving) this bound.
status_search_result: The question of the optimal upper bound on the injectivity index of a normal MPS is closely tied to the quantum Wielandt inequality, where the best known general upper bound is on the order of $D^2\log D$ (Sanz–Pérez-García–Wolf–Cirac), while the best known lower-bound examples scale as $\Theta(D^2)$. Recent work has produced a "generic" quantum Wielandt inequality showing improved bounds for almost-all tensors, but the exact optimal worst-case bound in terms of $D$ alone remains unresolved in the literature.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: Give an explicit and computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a translation-invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on the two-dimensional square lattice defined by a single tensor

  A : (C^D)^{⊗4} → C^d,

where D is the bond dimension and d is the physical dimension. For any finite simply connected region R of the lattice, contracting copies of A on the sites of R with open physical indices and with open virtual indices on the boundary ∂R yields a linear map

  Γ_R : (C^D)^{⊗|∂R|} → (C^d)^{⊗|R|}.

The PEPS tensor A is said to be injective on R if Γ_R is injective. The injectivity index i(A) is the smallest integer L such that Γ_R is injective for every square block region R of side length at least L. The PEPS is called normal if some such finite L exists, i.e. i(A) < ∞.

It is known that there exists a function f : N → N such that i(A) ≤ f(D) for every normal PEPS tensor A with bond dimension D, but the only proofs of existence available do not yield a computable f.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit, computable function f : N → N — and ideally a polynomial one — such that for every normal PEPS tensor A with bond dimension D one has

  i(A) ≤ f(D).
status_search_result: A search of recent literature on PEPS injectivity, normal PEPS, and quantum Wielandt-type inequalities in 2D shows that, while the 1D analogue (matrix product states) admits an O(D^2 log D)-type bound via the quantum Wielandt inequality, no explicit computable upper bound on the injectivity index of a normal 2D PEPS in terms of the bond dimension D appears to have been established. Recent work (e.g. on computational complexity of injective PEPS and on generalizations of the injectivity condition) does not provide such a function. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: In two dimensions, does every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian admit a global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption alone, without any additional assumptions about the low-energy spectrum?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces attached to each site. Let $H_\Lambda = \sum_{x \in \Lambda} h_x$ be a local Hamiltonian on a finite region $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, where each $h_x$ acts non-trivially only on a bounded neighborhood of the site $x$ and has bounded operator norm. Assume that the family $\{H_\Lambda\}$ is uniformly gapped: there exists a constant $\gamma > 0$, independent of $|\Lambda|$, such that the spectral gap above the ground space of $H_\Lambda$ is at least $\gamma$ for all sufficiently large $\Lambda$.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension $D$ on $\Lambda$ is a state obtained by placing a maximally entangled pair of $D$-dimensional auxiliary systems on each edge of the lattice and applying a local linear map at each site that projects the auxiliary systems into the physical Hilbert space.

Question: Does there exist a function $D(N, \varepsilon)$, polynomial in $N = |\Lambda|$ and $1/\varepsilon$, such that for every such uniformly gapped local Hamiltonian on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, every ground state $|\psi_\Lambda\rangle$ of $H_\Lambda$ can be approximated in trace norm to within $\varepsilon$ by a PEPS of bond dimension at most $D(N,\varepsilon)$, using only the spectral gap assumption and no additional hypothesis on the low-energy spectrum?
status_search_result: The 2D global PEPS approximation problem under only the spectral gap assumption appears to remain open. Existing results provide global PEPS approximations for ground states of 2D gapped local Hamiltonians only under additional assumptions on the low-energy spectral density; no proof is known under the spectral gap assumption alone, and the analogous 1D MPS result has not been extended to 2D without extra hypotheses.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(ε) be chosen polynomial in 1/ε?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space at each site. Let $H = \sum_{x} h_x$ be a translationally invariant local Hamiltonian, where each term $h_x$ acts on a bounded neighbourhood of the site $x$, and assume that $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground-state energy that is bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in the system size.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension $D$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is a translationally invariant tensor network state obtained by placing at each lattice site a tensor with one physical index (of the local Hilbert space dimension) and four virtual indices of dimension $D$, and contracting virtual indices along the edges of the lattice.

Question. Does the following 2D local approximation theorem hold? For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a bond dimension $D = g(\varepsilon)$ and a translationally invariant PEPS $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ of bond dimension at most $g(\varepsilon)$ such that for every finite region $R \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the reduced density matrix of $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ on $R$ approximates the reduced density matrix of the ground state of $H$ on $R$ to within $\varepsilon$ in trace distance (with constants possibly depending on $|R|$ in a controlled way).

Specifically:
(a) Does such a local approximation theorem exist in two dimensions?
(b) Can it be established assuming only the spectral gap hypothesis (without further assumptions such as frustration-freeness, injectivity of a parent Hamiltonian, or uniform local gap)?
(c) Can the bond-dimension bound $g(\varepsilon)$ be taken to be polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$?
status_search_result: The 1D analogue (locally accurate MPS approximation of ground states of 1D gapped local Hamiltonians with polynomial bond dimension) was established by Dalzell–Brandão (2019). In 2D, area-law results for frustration-free systems (Anshu–Arad–Gosset, 2021) and quasi-/polynomial-time algorithms for ground-state observables of injective/uniformly gapped PEPS exist, but a general 2D local approximation theorem assuming only a spectral gap, with polynomial $g(\varepsilon)$, does not appear to have been proved. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, interpolating between the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality is undecidable.
self_contained_problem:
A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is defined by associating to each site a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times D \times D \times D \times D}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of bond dimension $D$, and contracting copies of $A$ along the edges of a finite region $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ (with chosen boundary conditions) to obtain a vector $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle$ in the physical Hilbert space $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes |\Lambda|}$.

A "Fundamental Theorem" for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of PEPS tensors is a theorem of the following form: there exists an explicit list of local "gauge" relations on tensors (such as application of invertible matrices on virtual indices, possibly together with additional structural moves) such that, for every pair $A, B \in \mathcal{C}$, one has $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle = |\Psi_\Lambda(B)\rangle$ for all sufficiently large regions $\Lambda$ if and only if $A$ and $B$ are related by a finite sequence of these gauge relations.

For one-dimensional Matrix Product States, such a fundamental theorem is known in full generality. In two dimensions, it is established for the subclass of "normal" PEPS (tensors whose associated transfer-type map becomes injective after blocking). At the other extreme, equality of PEPS for arbitrary tensors is known to be undecidable, ruling out any complete fundamental theorem for the full class.

Problem: Identify a class $\mathcal{C}$ of two-dimensional (and, more generally, $d$-dimensional with $d \ge 2$) PEPS tensors that strictly contains the normal PEPS but is as large as possible while still admitting an explicit Fundamental Theorem in the above sense, and prove the corresponding theorem for $\mathcal{C}$.
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. While a Fundamental Theorem is established for normal PEPS in 2D and undecidability results (e.g., Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 210504) preclude a fully general version, recent surveys and works (such as the 2020 review on MPS/PEPS concepts, symmetries, and theorems, and 2024–2025 works on PEPS with flexible geometry and injective PEPS complexity) continue to identify the extension of the Fundamental Theorem to broader-than-normal classes of 2D PEPS as an outstanding goal, with no complete resolution found.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Consider supervised machine-learning models whose hypothesis class consists of functions parameterized by a tensor network of fixed structure (e.g. a matrix product state / tensor train, a tensor ring, a CP or Tucker decomposition) with bond dimension (rank) D. Concretely, fix a tensor network architecture on N sites with local physical dimension d and a uniform bond dimension D, and let H_{N,d,D} denote the associated class of real-valued classifiers (or regressors) obtained by contracting an input feature embedding against the network and reading out a scalar.

Provide explicit closed-form expressions, as functions of the bond dimension D (and of N, d), for:

(a) the Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension VC(H_{N,d,D}) of the resulting binary classifier family, and
(b) the (empirical or population) Rademacher complexity R_m(H_{N,d,D}) of the hypothesis class on samples of size m.

In particular, determine matching upper and lower bounds in D that exhibit the exact dependence of these complexity measures on the bond dimension for matrix product state classifiers and for related tensor network classifiers.
status_search_result: Khavari and Rabusseau (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.11827) derived matching upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension and pseudo-dimension of tensor network classifiers (including MPS/tensor train, tensor ring, CP, Tucker) as functions of the bond dimension, explicitly addressing the VC-dimension part of the question. Explicit closed-form Rademacher complexity expressions in terms of bond dimension do not appear to be fully resolved in the same generality, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
original_question: Given a finite group G and a normal subgroup H, does there exist a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group and let H be a normal subgroup of G. For any finite group K, let D(K) denote Kitaev's quantum double model defined on a 2-dimensional lattice: the local Hilbert space on each edge is C[K], and the Hamiltonian is the standard sum of mutually commuting vertex operators (enforcing gauge invariance under K) and plaquette operators (enforcing flatness of the K-gauge connection). The ground space of D(K) realizes the topological phase whose anyon content is the Drinfeld center Z(Rep(K)).

A "low-depth noisy quantum circuit" is a quantum channel obtained by composing a number of layers, independent of the system size (or growing at most poly-logarithmically), where each layer is a tensor product of local quantum channels (CPTP maps) acting on O(1)-sized regions of qudits, possibly using ancillas and measurements with classical feed-forward.

Question: Does there exist such a low-depth noisy quantum circuit Φ that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H? More precisely, does there exist a constant-depth (or poly-logarithmic-depth) local quantum channel Φ such that Φ sends any ground state of the D(G) Hamiltonian to a state in the topological phase of D(H), implementing the anyon condensation associated with the inclusion of the normal subgroup H ⊴ G?
status_search_result: A web search shows active research on related questions—anyon condensation via locality-preserving channels, mixed-state topological order under decoherence, and adaptive constant-depth circuits for non-Abelian quantum doubles—but no source explicitly resolves the general question of whether a low-depth noisy circuit can map the D(G) phase to the D(H) phase for an arbitrary normal subgroup H ⊴ G. Status appears unresolved in full generality.

original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic? Here "closed" means there are no unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and a geodesic multinet is the version of a geodesic net that allows edge multiplicities and self-intersections.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net in $M$ is a finite graph immersed in $M$ whose edges are geodesic arcs and which satisfies a balancing condition at each vertex: at every vertex $v$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors of the edges emanating from $v$, counted with edge multiplicities, equals the zero vector in $T_v M$. A geodesic multinet is a geodesic net in which edges are allowed to have positive integer multiplicities and edges are allowed to self-intersect or coincide. Such a multinet is called closed if every vertex satisfies the balancing condition (i.e. there are no unbalanced "boundary" vertices). A non-trivial periodic geodesic is a closed geodesic that is not a constant map.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic as a subset (i.e., none of the geodesic arcs traced by the multinet, with their multiplicities, decompose to include a non-trivial closed geodesic)?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on geodesic nets and multinets. A targeted web search did not return any subsequent work announcing a resolution, and standard references on closed geodesics do not address this specific question about geodesic multinets. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension >= 3 admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is a theta-graph, namely a graph with two vertices joined by three distinct edges?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite multigraph $G$ together with a continuous map $f : G \to M$ such that:
(i) the restriction of $f$ to the interior of each edge of $G$ is a (nonconstant) geodesic arc parametrized by arc length;
(ii) at each vertex $v$ of $G$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ of the geodesic edges meeting $v$ (taken with the outgoing orientation) equals zero in $T_{f(v)} M$.
Such a geodesic net is called a closed geodesic net. The theta-graph $\theta$ is the multigraph with exactly two vertices joined by three distinct edges.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n \geq 3$ admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is the theta-graph $\theta$ (i.e., two vertices $p, q \in M$ together with three geodesic arcs from $p$ to $q$ such that the three unit tangent vectors at $p$ sum to zero, and the three unit tangent vectors at $q$ sum to zero)?
status_search_result: The problem of existence of theta-graph shaped stationary geodesic nets on general closed Riemannian manifolds appears to remain open. While there are partial results (e.g., existence on manifolds with nontrivial second homology, where a geodesic net of length at most 3·diam(M) exists but may be a closed geodesic, two loops, or a theta-graph; and existence on convex 2-spheres close to round), no general existence theorem in dimension ≥ 3 is recorded. Recent work (2025) on generic density of stationary geodesic nets explicitly notes that such nets may degenerate to unions of closed geodesics, leaving the theta-graph existence question unresolved.

original_question: Let Sigma be the set of all triples S of points in the Euclidean plane for which there exist geodesic multinets with exactly three unbalanced vertices located at S and with arbitrarily many balanced vertices. Is Sigma a measure-zero subset of (R^2)^3?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic multinet is a finite multigraph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight line segments (geodesics), where multiple edges between the same pair of vertices are allowed. A vertex $v$ of a geodesic multinet is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ along all edges incident to $v$ (each multi-edge contributing its own unit tangent vector) equals the zero vector; otherwise $v$ is called unbalanced.

Let $\Sigma \subset (\mathbb{R}^2)^3$ be the set of all ordered triples $S = (p_1, p_2, p_3)$ of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ for which, for every positive integer $N$, there exists a geodesic multinet whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the three points of $S$ and which contains at least $N$ balanced vertices.

Determine whether $\Sigma$ has Lebesgue measure zero in $(\mathbb{R}^2)^3 \cong \mathbb{R}^6$.

original_question: Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic multinet is a finite connected graph $\Gamma$ embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ is finite and whose edges are straight line segments (geodesics), with the convention that multiple edges between the same pair of vertices and isolated loops are allowed only insofar as each edge is realized as a (possibly degenerate) straight segment; each edge $e$ is assigned a positive integer multiplicity $m(e) \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

For a vertex $v \in V(\Gamma)$ and an edge $e$ incident to $v$, let $u_{v,e} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the unit vector at $v$ pointing along $e$ away from $v$. The vertex $v$ is called balanced if
$$\sum_{e \ni v} m(e)\, u_{v,e} \;=\; 0,$$
and unbalanced otherwise. (Equivalently, a geodesic multinet is the 1-skeleton of a stationary integer 1-varifold in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose stationarity may fail at a prescribed finite set of vertices, the unbalanced ones.)

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to similarity of $\mathbb{R}^2$, of all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices. The classification should describe the combinatorial structure (graph with edge multiplicities), the possible positions of the unbalanced vertices and of any additional balanced vertices, and the resulting straight-edge embeddings.
status_search_result: For ordinary geodesic nets (all edges multiplicity one) with three unbalanced/boundary vertices in a non-positively curved plane, it is known (Parsch, J. Differential Geom. 119 (2021)) that there is at most one balanced vertex, located at the Fermat point of the three unbalanced vertices, giving the classical Fermat-Torricelli configuration. However, the broader classification problem for geodesic multinets (allowing edge multiplicities) with three unbalanced vertices does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; subsequent work (e.g., on four-boundary-vertex multinets, 2024–2025) continues to treat such classification questions as open.

context_brief: Arbitrarily many balanced vertices from four boundary points
original_question: Do there exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices? The conjecture further suggests that this may already hold when the four unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square.
self_contained_problem:
A geodesic net in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight line segments, together with a designated subset of its vertices called boundary (or unbalanced) vertices. A non-boundary vertex $v$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges emanating from $v$ equals the zero vector; every non-boundary vertex is required to be balanced. The boundary vertices are those at which the corresponding sum of unit tangent vectors is allowed to be nonzero.

Question: Does there exist, for every positive integer $N$, a geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^2$ having exactly four unbalanced vertices and at least $N$ balanced vertices? In particular, does such a family exist in which the four unbalanced vertices are the four vertices of a square?
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. A November 2025 preprint reports progress by constructing an irreducible geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices (improving an earlier example with 16), and suggests the construction might generalize to give arbitrarily many balanced vertices, but does not prove the full conjecture.

context_brief: Fixed boundary set with unbounded complexity
original_question: Does there exist an integer N0 and an N0-tuple S of points in the Euclidean plane such that, for every N, there is a geodesic net whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly S and whose number of balanced vertices is greater than N? Moreover, do such N0-tuples S form a subset of (R^2)^N0 of positive measure, or even a non-empty open subset?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic net is a finite straight-line graph $G \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (a finite set of vertices together with straight segments joining some pairs of them) in which each edge is a geodesic segment of $\mathbb{R}^2$. A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$, taken along all edges of $G$ incident to $v$, equals the zero vector; otherwise $v$ is called unbalanced. For a positive integer $N_0$, an $N_0$-tuple $S = (p_1, \dots, p_{N_0}) \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ is said to admit unboundedly complex balanced extensions if for every positive integer $N$ there exists a geodesic net $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose set of unbalanced vertices equals $\{p_1, \dots, p_{N_0}\}$ and whose number of balanced vertices exceeds $N$.

(a) Does there exist an integer $N_0 \ge 1$ and an $N_0$-tuple $S \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ which admits unboundedly complex balanced extensions?

(b) If so, does the set of such $N_0$-tuples form a subset of $(\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ of positive Lebesgue measure, or even contain a non-empty open subset of $(\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$?
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. For three unbalanced vertices, it has been proved that there can be at most one balanced vertex, ruling out unbounded complexity in that case. For four unbalanced vertices, only finite constructions are known: an irreducible geodesic net with four boundary points and 25 balanced vertices was recently constructed (raising the prior record of 16), and this work is presented as progress toward, but not a proof of, the conjecture that arbitrarily many balanced vertices are achievable. The measure-theoretic / openness refinement (part 2) does not appear to be settled.
