paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: Can differentially private GAN mechanisms for time-series generation be improved enough to provide meaningful privacy guarantees without destroying the fidelity of the generated time-series data?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution over multivariate time series $x = (x_1,\dots,x_T) \in \mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$ optionally accompanied by metadata $m \in \mathcal{M}$. A generator is a (possibly randomized) map $G_\theta$ taking a noise seed $z$ (and optionally metadata) to a synthetic sample. A training mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ takes a dataset $S = \{(x^{(i)}, m^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^n \sim \mathcal{D}^n$ and outputs trained parameters $\theta = \mathcal{A}(S)$.

Differential privacy. The mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private if, for any two datasets $S, S'$ differing in a single record and every measurable set $E$ of parameter outputs,
$$\Pr[\mathcal{A}(S) \in E] \le e^{\varepsilon}\, \Pr[\mathcal{A}(S') \in E] + \delta.$$

Fidelity. Fix a finite collection of statistics $\mathcal{T} = \{T_1,\dots,T_K\}$ where each $T_k$ maps a dataset of time series to a value in a metric space $(\mathcal{Y}_k, \rho_k)$ (e.g.\ marginal distributions, autocorrelation functions, cross-feature joint distributions, downstream classifier accuracy). For a real dataset $S$ and synthetic dataset $\tilde S$ generated by $G_\theta$, define the fidelity gap
$$\mathrm{Fid}(\theta; S) = \max_{1\le k\le K} \rho_k\!\big(T_k(S),\, T_k(\tilde S)\big).$$

Question. Does there exist a training mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ for time-series generative adversarial networks that is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private with meaningful parameters (say $\varepsilon = O(1)$ and $\delta = o(1/n)$), and such that for natural classes of networked time-series distributions $\mathcal{D}$ the expected fidelity gap $\mathbb{E}_{S\sim \mathcal{D}^n}[\mathrm{Fid}(\mathcal{A}(S); S)]$ converges to that of a comparable non-private GAN as $n \to \infty$?

Equivalently: can differentially private GAN mechanisms for time-series generation be improved enough to provide meaningful privacy guarantees without collapsing the fidelity of the generated data on standard fidelity metrics?
status_search_result: Subsequent work has proposed concrete improvements to DP-GAN training (e.g., taking more discriminator steps per generator step, clipping decay schedules, and DP fine-tuning from public pretraining), reporting substantial fidelity gains on tabular and image data and partial gains on time-series benchmarks. However, no work conclusively establishes that DP-GAN mechanisms can simultaneously achieve standard meaningful DP parameters and non-degraded fidelity on networked time-series tasks; recent surveys and empirical studies still report a substantial privacy–fidelity trade-off, so the question remains open.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: If differential privacy is not well aligned with GAN-generated networked time-series releases, what alternative privacy metrics should be explored for this form of synthetic data sharing?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the setting in which a data holder possesses a dataset of networked time series, i.e., a collection of multivariate sequences {X_i = (X_i^{(1)}, X_i^{(2)}, ..., X_i^{(T_i)})}_{i=1}^N indexed by entities in a network (each X_i^{(t)} ∈ R^d, possibly accompanied by static attributes A_i ∈ R^k). The holder wishes to release a synthetic dataset {Ŷ_j}_{j=1}^M produced by a generative adversarial network (GAN) trained on {X_i, A_i} so that downstream parties may perform analyses (e.g., distributional fidelity of marginals, autocorrelations, cross-series correlations, and rare-event statistics) without compromising the privacy of contributing entities.

Recall that a randomized release mechanism M satisfies (ε, δ)-differential privacy if for every pair of datasets D, D' differing in a single entity's record and every measurable set S of outputs, Pr[M(D) ∈ S] ≤ e^ε · Pr[M(D') ∈ S] + δ. Empirically, training GANs under (ε, δ)-DP with practically meaningful (ε, δ) typically degrades fidelity of long, high-dimensional networked time series substantially.

Problem. Propose and rigorously formalize a privacy metric P (a functional on pairs (training distribution, release mechanism)) suitable for evaluating GAN-based releases of networked time-series data, satisfying all of the following desiderata:
(a) P admits a precise mathematical definition with explicit adversarial threat model (specifying adversary knowledge, queries, and success criterion).
(b) P composes under repeated or sequential releases in a quantifiable way.
(c) P is post-processing robust: applying any data-independent function to the release does not decrease privacy as measured by P.
(d) P captures protection against the principal attacks relevant to time-series releases—membership inference, attribute inference of static attributes A_i, and trace/trajectory reconstruction of X_i—via provable reductions.
(e) P is empirically estimable from a trained GAN and a finite training set with computable confidence bounds.
(f) Under P, there exist non-trivial GAN training procedures that achieve a quantitatively meaningful privacy level while preserving utility (measured by a stated set of statistical functionals of the time series) strictly better than what is achievable under (ε, δ)-differential privacy at comparable utility.

Provide such a metric P, prove items (a)–(d), give an estimator with finite-sample guarantees for (e), and exhibit a training algorithm with a theorem establishing (f), or prove that no metric can simultaneously satisfy (a)–(f).
status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning alternative privacy notions for GAN-generated networked time series. Subsequent literature has proposed candidate metrics (e.g., membership-inference-based audits, attribute-inference resistance, plausible deniability, Rényi DP, f-DP, and similarity-based heuristics), but no single metric has been established as a definitive replacement for differential privacy with the stated combination of properties for time-series GANs. The general problem remains open.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: How can practitioners perform what-if analysis by modeling changes in an underlying networking system and then generating synthetic data for the modified system, especially when larger interventions invalidate the conditional distributions learned from the original data and may therefore require explicit physical-system modeling or simulation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a networked system that produces multivariate time series data, where each trace records the temporal behavior of agents (e.g., flows, users, devices) interacting through shared infrastructure. Suppose a generative model G (such as a GAN) has been trained on observed traces drawn from a joint distribution P(X, C), where X denotes the time series and C denotes auxiliary system parameters or conditions (e.g., topology, link capacities, traffic mix, protocol settings). Standard conditional generation can produce samples X ~ G(· | C) for values of C represented in the training data.

Now suppose a practitioner wishes to perform "what-if" analysis: predict and synthesize plausible time series for a modified system specified by a new condition C' that represents an intervention (for example, changing routing, introducing a new protocol, scaling the user population, or altering link capacities). When the intervention is small, one might hope that the learned conditional distribution P(X | C) extrapolates to C'; however, when the intervention is large, the original conditional distributions become invalid because the underlying physical/networking dynamics are themselves altered.

Formulate and solve the following problem:

(a) Provide a principled framework that combines a learned generative model of agent-level or fine-grained behavior with an explicit mechanistic / physical-system simulator of the network so that, given an intervention C' outside the training distribution, the framework produces synthetic time series whose joint distribution faithfully approximates the true post-intervention distribution P*(X | do(C')).

(b) Specify identifiability conditions on the decomposition (which aspects of behavior are modeled by G versus by the simulator) under which the resulting hybrid generator is consistent as the amount of pre-intervention training data grows.

(c) Develop quantitative evaluation criteria — beyond marginal or conditional fidelity on observed C — for assessing the accuracy of synthetic data produced under counterfactual interventions C', and demonstrate the framework on a concrete networked time-series setting.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning how to combine GAN-based generative modeling with physical/network simulation to support out-of-distribution counterfactual ("what-if") synthesis of networked time series. No published work has been identified that provides a complete, principled solution; subsequent literature on hybrid simulator-ML generators and causal time-series GANs addresses related sub-problems but does not resolve the full question.

paper_title: Answering two open problems on Banks theorem for non-autonomous dynamical systems
context_brief: Finitely generated but non-periodic Banks-type example
original_question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system (X, f1,∞) on a metric space X without isolated points such that the system is finitely generated but not periodic, is topologically transitive, has every point periodic so that Per(f1,∞) = X, and has two invariant periodic points x and y with disjoint orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space without isolated points. A non-autonomous dynamical system (NADS) on $X$ is a pair $(X, f_{1,\infty})$, where $f_{1,\infty} = (f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of continuous self-maps $f_n : X \to X$. For $n \ge 1$ set $f_1^n = f_n \circ f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1$, and $f_1^0 = \mathrm{id}_X$. The orbit of $x \in X$ is $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) = \{f_1^n(x) : n \ge 0\}$. 

Definitions:
- The system $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ is finitely generated if there is a finite set $\{g_1,\dots,g_k\}$ of continuous self-maps of $X$ such that each $f_n$ belongs to $\{g_1,\dots,g_k\}$.
- It is periodic if the sequence $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is periodic, i.e. there exists $p \ge 1$ with $f_{n+p} = f_n$ for all $n \ge 1$.
- It is topologically transitive if for every pair of nonempty open sets $U, V \subseteq X$ there exists $n \ge 1$ with $f_1^n(U) \cap V \ne \emptyset$.
- A point $x \in X$ is periodic if there exists $m \ge 1$ with $f_1^m(x) = x$; the set of periodic points is $\mathrm{Per}(f_{1,\infty})$.
- A periodic point $x \in X$ is invariant if $f_n(x) = x$ for all $n \ge 1$.

Question: Does there exist a metric space $X$ without isolated points and a non-autonomous dynamical system $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ such that all of the following hold simultaneously?
(i) $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ is finitely generated but not periodic;
(ii) $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ is topologically transitive;
(iii) $\mathrm{Per}(f_{1,\infty}) = X$;
(iv) there exist two invariant periodic points $x, y \in X$ with $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) \cap \mathrm{orb}(y, f_{1,\infty}) = \emptyset$.
status_search_result: The question has been answered positively: an explicit construction on a symbolic space $\Sigma$ with a finitely generated but non-periodic sequence $g_{1,\infty}$ has been exhibited that satisfies all four conditions, providing the desired example.

This gives a positive answer to Open Problem 6.", "claim": "An explicit example is constructed that is finitely generated but not periodic and satisfies the transitivity, dense periodic points, and disjoint invariant orbits conditions, resolving the question positively."}]

paper_title: ANSWERING TWO OPEN PROBLEMS ON BANKS THEOREM FOR NON-AUTONOMOUS DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS
context_brief: Finitely generated but non-periodic Banks-type example
original_question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system (X, f1,∞) on a metric space X without isolated points such that f1,∞ is topologically transitive, every point of X is periodic for the system, there exist two invariant periodic points x and y whose orbits orb(x, f1,∞) and orb(y, f1,∞) are disjoint, and the sequence of maps is finitely generated but not periodic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space without isolated points. A non-autonomous dynamical system (NADS) on $X$ is a pair $(X, f_{1,\infty})$, where $f_{1,\infty} = (f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of continuous self-maps $f_n: X \to X$. For $n \ge 1$ define $f_1^n = f_n \circ f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1$, with $f_1^0 = \mathrm{id}_X$. The orbit of $x \in X$ is $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) = \{f_1^n(x) : n \ge 0\}$. A point $x$ is periodic if there exists $p \ge 1$ with $f_1^{kp}(x) = x$ for all $k \ge 0$, and it is invariant periodic if additionally each $f_n$ permutes its orbit. The system is topologically transitive if for every pair of nonempty open sets $U,V \subset X$ there exists $n \ge 1$ with $f_1^n(U) \cap V \ne \emptyset$. The sequence $f_{1,\infty}$ is said to be finitely generated if there exists a finite set $\mathcal{F} = \{g_1,\dots,g_k\}$ of continuous maps on $X$ such that every $f_n \in \mathcal{F}$, and it is called periodic if in addition the sequence $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ itself is eventually periodic in $n$.

Question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ on a metric space $X$ without isolated points such that
(1) $f_{1,\infty}$ is topologically transitive,
(2) every point of $X$ is periodic for the system (i.e. $\mathrm{Per}(f_{1,\infty}) = X$),
(3) there exist two invariant periodic points $x, y \in X$ with $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) \cap \mathrm{orb}(y, f_{1,\infty}) = \emptyset$, and
(4) the generating sequence $f_{1,\infty}$ is finitely generated but not periodic?

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Can one prove local input-to-state stability by using non-coercive Lyapunov functions, and can one obtain such local results when the non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function is formulated in implication form rather than dissipative form? In other words, develop non-coercive Lyapunov criteria for LISS and for implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions in infinite-dimensional systems.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be a Banach space (the state space) with norm $\|\cdot\|_X$, let $U$ be a normed space of input values, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_+\to U$ equipped with a norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{U}}$. Consider a (generally nonlinear, infinite-dimensional) control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$, where $\phi(t,x,u)\in X$ denotes the state at time $t\ge 0$ starting from $x\in X$ under input $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and $\phi$ satisfies the standard axioms of a control system (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity).

Comparison-function classes. $\mathcal{K}$ is the set of continuous strictly increasing functions $\alpha:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ with $\alpha(0)=0$; $\mathcal{K}_\infty$ consists of unbounded $\mathcal{K}$-functions; $\mathcal{KL}$ is the set of functions $\beta(\cdot,\cdot)$ that are $\mathcal{K}$ in the first argument and decreasing to $0$ in the second.

Local input-to-state stability (LISS). $\Sigma$ is called LISS if there exist $r>0$, $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$, and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that for all $x\in X$ with $\|x\|_X\le r$ and all $u\in\mathcal{U}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le r$,
$$\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X\le \beta(\|x\|_X,t)+\gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}),\qquad t\ge 0.$$

Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions. A continuous functional $V:D\to\mathbb{R}_+$, defined on an open neighborhood $D\subset X$ of $0$, is called a non-coercive Lyapunov function if there exist $\psi_2\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$0\le V(x)\le \psi_2(\|x\|_X)\qquad\text{for all }x\in D,$$
(no lower bound $\psi_1(\|x\|_X)\le V(x)$ is required; coercive Lyapunov functions are those that additionally satisfy such a lower bound).

Two forms of the infinitesimal decay condition (with Dini derivative $\dot V_u(x):=\limsup_{t\to 0^+}\tfrac{1}{t}(V(\phi(t,x,u))-V(x))$):
- Dissipative form: there exist $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that $\dot V_u(x)\le -\alpha(\|x\|_X)+\sigma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}})$.
- Implication form: there exist $\rho,\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that $\|x\|_X\ge \rho(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}})\ \Rightarrow\ \dot V_u(x)\le -\alpha(\|x\|_X)$.

Problem. Develop non-coercive Lyapunov criteria for LISS of infinite-dimensional control systems. Specifically:

(a) Prove that the existence of a non-coercive Lyapunov function $V$ on a neighborhood $D$ of $0$ satisfying the dissipative-form decay only locally (for $\|x\|_X,\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}$ small) implies that $\Sigma$ is LISS.

(b) Establish an analogous LISS criterion when the non-coercive Lyapunov function is given in implication form.

(c) In the global case, prove that the existence of a non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function in implication form implies that $\Sigma$ is ISS.

Identify natural regularity/admissibility hypotheses on $\Sigma$ (e.g., the BRS, CEP, or robust-equilibrium properties used in infinite-dimensional ISS theory) under which the implications above hold, or exhibit counterexamples showing that without such hypotheses they fail.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has made progress. The 2019/2020 paper "Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems" (Jacob–Mironchenko–Partington–Wirth, SIAM J. Control Optim.) develops global non-coercive ISS results. A more recent preprint (arXiv:2510.14057, 2025) explicitly presents methods for constructing non-coercive LISS/iISS Lyapunov functions for time-varying semilinear evolution equations, addressing the local case. However, a fully general theory covering implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions and arbitrary infinite-dimensional control systems does not appear to be completely settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Establish converse input-to-state stability Lyapunov theorems for broad classes of infinite-dimensional systems beyond the currently covered cases, specifically for general nonlinear systems and for general linear boundary control systems. The goal is to know when ISS necessarily implies the existence of an appropriate ISS Lyapunov function in these settings.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider control systems of the form
  ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + f(x(t), u(t)),    x(t) ∈ X,  u ∈ U_c,
where X is a Banach space (the state space), U_c is a space of admissible input functions u: [0, ∞) → U taking values in a Banach space U (typically L^∞ or piecewise continuous functions), and the dynamics are given either by

(a) a general nonlinear evolution equation, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on X and f: X × U → X (or, more generally, into an extrapolation space) is a nonlinear term ensuring well-posedness of mild solutions, or

(b) a general linear boundary control system, written abstractly as
  ẋ(t) = 𝔄 x(t),    𝔅 x(t) = u(t),
where 𝔄: D(𝔄) ⊂ X → X is a closed linear operator, 𝔅: D(𝔄) → U is a boundary operator, and (𝔄, 𝔅) generates a well-posed boundary control system in the sense of Salamon–Weiss.

Definitions. Let 𝒦 = { γ: ℝ_{≥0} → ℝ_{≥0} : continuous, strictly increasing, γ(0)=0 }, 𝒦_∞ the subclass of unbounded such functions, and 𝒦𝓛 the class of functions β(r,t) that are 𝒦 in r and decay to 0 in t. The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ 𝒦𝓛 and γ ∈ 𝒦_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t; x_0, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{[0,t]})    for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous function V: X → ℝ_{≥0} is called an ISS Lyapunov function if there exist ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ 𝒦_∞, α ∈ 𝒦_∞, and χ ∈ 𝒦 such that
  ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖)    for all x ∈ X,
and along solutions
  ‖x‖ ≥ χ(‖u‖)   ⟹   V̇(x, u) ≤ −α(‖x‖),
where V̇ is the appropriate (Dini or Lie) derivative along the system.

Problem. Prove (or disprove) the following converse ISS Lyapunov theorems:

(1) For the general nonlinear class (a): if the system is ISS, then there exists a (coercive, possibly Lipschitz continuous) ISS Lyapunov function V: X → ℝ_{≥0}.

(2) For general linear boundary control systems (b): if the system is ISS (with respect to a suitable norm on the input space), then there exists an ISS Lyapunov function V on X.

Determine, in each case, the strongest regularity (continuity, local Lipschitz continuity, smoothness) and the structural form (coercive vs. non-coercive, quadratic when applicable) of the ISS Lyapunov function that can be guaranteed.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed: non-coercive converse Lyapunov theorems for ISS of infinite-dimensional systems have been established (Mironchenko–Wirth and follow-ups), and recent work proves coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded (including boundary) input operators, as well as quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for analytic linear systems. Counterexamples show that coercive quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions need not exist even for analytic semigroups with bounded inputs. However, fully general converse ISS Lyapunov theorems for arbitrary nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems and for the full class of linear boundary control systems remain unresolved, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Develop a satisfactory Lyapunov theory for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This includes deciding whether ISS always implies the existence of a coercive or non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function, whether heat equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions admit coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, whether some linear ISS systems admit only non-coercive but not coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, and whether admissibility of the input operator can be characterized in Lyapunov terms.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear infinite-dimensional control system of the form
  ẋ(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach space, A: D(A) ⊂ X → X generates a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on X, and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) linear input operator with values in the extrapolation space X_{-1}, U being a Banach space of input values. Inputs u are taken from L^∞(0,∞;U) (or another suitable input space).

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every initial state x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t; x₀, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)   for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called a non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function if there exist α ∈ K_∞, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, ρ ∈ K, and α_3 > 0 (or a positive definite α_3) such that
  ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖)   with ψ_1 only positive definite (not necessarily of class K_∞),
and the Dini derivative along trajectories satisfies V̇(x,u) ≤ −α_3(‖x‖) + ρ(‖u‖). It is called a coercive ISS Lyapunov function if additionally ψ_1 ∈ K_∞.

The operator B is called admissible (for (T(t))) if there exist t > 0 and c > 0 such that ∫₀^t T(t−s) B u(s) ds ∈ X with norm ≤ c‖u‖_{L^p(0,t;U)} for all u.

Address the following questions, providing proofs or counterexamples:
(a) Does ISS of the system always imply the existence of a (coercive or at least non-coercive) ISS Lyapunov function?
(b) Does the heat equation
  x_t = x_{xx} on (0,1), x(t,0) = u(t), x(t,1) = 0,
viewed as an ISS system in X = L^2(0,1) with Dirichlet boundary input, admit a coercive ISS Lyapunov function? More generally, do systems governed by analytic semigroups whose generators have unbounded spectrum admit coercive ISS Lyapunov functions?
(c) Do there exist linear ISS control systems with unbounded admissible input operators that admit non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions but no coercive ISS Lyapunov function?
(d) Can admissibility of the input operator B (relative to an exponentially stable semigroup) be characterized in terms of existence of an appropriate Lyapunov-type functional?
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on each sub-question but the program is not fully complete. Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions for linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators (including the Dirichlet heat equation) were constructed by Jacob, Mironchenko, Partington, Wirth (SICON, 2020). Recent work on quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for linear analytic systems (2023) and on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals via the regular-systems framework (MCSS, 2025), as well as generalized Lyapunov functionals (Automatica, 2024), give positive answers for several classes including the Dirichlet heat equation, but a complete general Lyapunov theory and a Lyapunov characterization of admissibility remain not fully settled.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: For time-delay systems viewed as infinite-dimensional control systems, determine whether forward completeness is equivalent to bounded reachability sets and whether the limit property LIM is equivalent to the uniform limit property ULIM. More generally, decide whether time-delay systems admit tighter ISS characterizations than those currently available from the general infinite-dimensional ISS superposition theorem.
self_contained_problem:
Consider time-delay control systems regarded as infinite-dimensional dynamical systems. Fix a finite delay r>0 and a state space X of functions on [-r,0] (e.g. C([-r,0];R^n) or L^∞([-r,0];R^n)), and consider systems of the form
    ẋ(t) = f(x_t, u(t)),    t ≥ 0,
where x_t(θ) := x(t+θ) for θ ∈ [-r,0], u: [0,∞) → R^m is a measurable essentially bounded input, and f satisfies standard regularity assumptions ensuring local existence and uniqueness of solutions.

Define the following properties:
  (FC) Forward completeness: for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u, the solution exists for all t ≥ 0.
  (BRS) Bounded reachability sets: for every T > 0 and every R > 0, the set {x_t : t ∈ [0,T], ‖x_0‖_X ≤ R, ‖u‖_∞ ≤ R} is bounded in X.
  (LIM) Limit property: there exists γ ∈ K_∞ such that for every x_0 ∈ X and every input u, liminf_{t→∞} ‖x(t)‖ ≤ γ(‖u‖_∞).
  (ULIM) Uniform limit property: there exists γ ∈ K_∞ such that for every ε > 0 and every R > 0 there is τ = τ(ε,R) with the property that for every ‖x_0‖_X ≤ R and every input u, there exists t ≤ τ with ‖x(t)‖ ≤ γ(‖u‖_∞) + ε.

Questions:
(a) For time-delay systems on a given state space X, is (FC) equivalent to (BRS)?
(b) For time-delay systems, is (LIM) equivalent to (ULIM)?
(c) More generally, do time-delay systems admit strictly tighter input-to-state stability (ISS) characterizations than those provided by the general infinite-dimensional ISS superposition theorem?
status_search_result: Subsequent research has partially resolved part (a). On the state space C([-r,0];R^n) of continuous functions, forward completeness has been shown NOT to imply boundedness of reachability sets, with explicit counterexamples (Chaillet, Pepe, Mironchenko, Wirth, 2023). On the state space L^∞([-r,0];R^n) of essentially bounded measurable functions, forward completeness DOES imply bounded reachability sets (Mironchenko, Chaillet, Pepe, Wirth, 2024, IEEE TAC). Parts (b) and (c) regarding LIM vs ULIM equivalence and the existence of tighter ISS characterizations for time-delay systems beyond the general superposition theorem remain, to our knowledge, open.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Develop superposition theorems for integral input-to-state stability in infinite-dimensional systems that play the role for iISS that Theorem 2.7 plays for ISS. In particular, find non-Lyapunov characterizations of infinite-dimensional iISS comparable to the known finite-dimensional ODE theory.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider an abstract control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$, where:
- $X$ is a Banach space (the state space) with norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ and zero element $0$;
- $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed vector space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$ (where $U$ is a Banach space of input values), closed under concatenation and time-shifts;
- $\phi:D_\phi\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times X\times\mathcal{U}\to X$ is a transition map satisfying the standard cocycle/causality axioms (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity in time on its maximal interval of existence).

Comparison function classes. $\mathcal{K}$ denotes continuous strictly increasing functions $\alpha:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $\alpha(0)=0$; $\mathcal{K}_\infty\subset\mathcal{K}$ are unbounded; $\mathcal{L}$ denotes continuous decreasing functions tending to $0$; $\mathcal{KL}=\{\beta:\beta(\cdot,t)\in\mathcal{K},\,\beta(r,\cdot)\in\mathcal{L}\}$.

Definition (iISS). $\Sigma$ is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if it is forward complete and there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\alpha,\gamma\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x\in X$, every $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and every $t\geq 0$,
$$\alpha(\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X)\;\leq\;\beta(\|x\|_X,t)\;+\;\int_0^t \gamma(\|u(s)\|_U)\,ds.$$

Background fact (ISS superposition theorem). For $\Sigma$ as above, input-to-state stability (ISS) is known to be equivalent to the conjunction of two strictly weaker properties: uniform local stability together with a suitable asymptotic gain / limit property (e.g., the bounded-input/uniform-limit property or the ULIM property), generalizing the Sontag–Wang superposition theorem from finite-dimensional ODEs to Banach-space systems. For finite-dimensional ODE systems, an analogous superposition-type non-Lyapunov characterization of iISS is known: iISS is equivalent to forward completeness combined with the global asymptotic stability of the zero-input system and a bounded-energy/converging-input bounded-state property.

Problem. Establish a superposition-type theorem for iISS in the infinite-dimensional setting. Specifically, identify a finite list of qualitative trajectory-based properties $(P_1),\dots,(P_k)$ — none of which involves the construction of a Lyapunov function — such that for every abstract control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$ on a Banach space $X$,
$$\Sigma\text{ is iISS}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (P_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge (P_k).$$
The characterization should reduce, in the special case $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ with ordinary differential equation dynamics, to the known finite-dimensional non-Lyapunov characterization of iISS, and should play the role for iISS that the ISS superposition theorem plays for ISS.
status_search_result: Superposition theorems for ISS and, more recently, for input-to-output stability (IOS) of infinite-dimensional systems have been established, and iISS has been characterized in various restricted settings (e.g., 1-D parabolic PDEs, time-varying systems, bilinear systems). However, a general non-Lyapunov superposition-style characterization of iISS for abstract control systems on Banach spaces, analogous to the ISS superposition theorem and matching the finite-dimensional ODE iISS theory, does not appear in the literature; recent surveys (2024) still discuss iISS characterizations as an active and partially developed research direction. Status appears open.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
context_brief: Limits of Lyapunov methods for iISS
original_question: Determine whether the existence of integral-input-to-state-stable infinite-dimensional systems that are not input-to-state stable would reveal genuine limitations of Lyapunov methods for systems with unbounded input operators, and if so, characterize how severe those limitations are. The issue is tied to the fact that ISS Lyapunov functions are automatically iISS Lyapunov functions.
self_contained_problem:
Consider control systems of the form
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x_0,
on a Banach space X, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator from a Banach space U of input values; admissible inputs u belong to L^∞(0,∞;U). Let β denote the class of KL-functions and let K, K_∞, P denote the standard comparison-function classes.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL, θ ∈ K_∞ and μ ∈ K such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + θ( ∫_0^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds )  for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called an ISS-Lyapunov function if it satisfies coercive bounds ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖) with ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, and an appropriate dissipation inequality of ISS type along trajectories; an iISS-Lyapunov function satisfies analogous bounds with an iISS dissipation inequality. Every ISS-Lyapunov function is automatically an iISS-Lyapunov function.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional control system of the above form, with an unbounded input operator B, that is integral input-to-state stable but not input-to-state stable? If such a system exists, quantify in what precise sense its existence reveals limitations of the Lyapunov-function approach to verifying ISS for systems with unbounded input operators, and characterize how severe these limitations are (e.g., whether iISS-Lyapunov functions can fail to detect the absence of ISS, and to what extent the Lyapunov method remains a complete tool for ISS in this setting).
status_search_result: Recent literature (2024–2025) on ISS/iISS for infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators continues to develop coercive and noncoercive ISS-Lyapunov methods, generalized ISS-Lyapunov functionals, and iISS-Lyapunov constructions for parabolic/hyperbolic PDEs with boundary disturbances. None of the surveyed works exhibits an iISS but not ISS infinite-dimensional system with unbounded B, nor rules it out; the question of whether such systems exist (and what limitations of the Lyapunov method this would entail) is still treated as an open problem in current surveys and tutorials.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Substantially extend the theory of interconnections of infinite-dimensional integral-input-to-state-stable systems, whose current state is much less complete than the corresponding ISS interconnection theory. This includes sharper small-gain results and a more systematic coupling theory for iISS subsystems.
self_contained_problem:
Consider control systems on Banach spaces of the form
  ẋ = A x + f(x, u),
where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X, u is an input from a function space U, and the resulting evolution is well-posed.

Such a system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist a class-KL function β and class-K functions α, γ such that for every initial state x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u, the solution x(·) satisfies
  α(‖x(t)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + ∫₀ᵗ γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds   for all t ≥ 0.

Now consider a feedback interconnection of two (or finitely many) such infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems
  ẋ_i = A_i x_i + f_i(x_1, …, x_n, u),   i = 1, …, n,
in which the "inputs" of subsystem i include the states x_j of the other subsystems plus an external input u.

Develop a substantial theory for such interconnections of infinite-dimensional iISS systems. In particular:

(a) Formulate sharp small-gain conditions on the iISS gain functions γ_{ij} (governing the influence of x_j on x_i) that guarantee iISS of the overall interconnected system on the product space X_1 × … × X_n.

(b) Provide a systematic coupling theory for infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems, including Lyapunov-based and trajectory-based criteria, that parallels and substantially extends the existing interconnection theory available for finite-dimensional iISS systems and for infinite-dimensional ISS systems.

The task is to establish such small-gain theorems and coupling criteria with the same level of completeness already achieved for ISS interconnections in the infinite-dimensional setting.
status_search_result: Several partial results exist: iISS small-gain theorems for two interconnected distributed-parameter systems and constructions of iISS Lyapunov functions for interconnected parabolic PDEs have been established, and recent works extend ISS small-gain theorems to infinite networks of heterogeneous infinite-dimensional systems. However, a complete and systematic coupling theory for infinite-dimensional iISS systems comparable to the ISS case is not yet available, so the broader program remains open.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Analyze the strong iISS concept in infinite-dimensional systems, extending the finite-dimensional ODE notion and the brief discussion given in this survey. The goal is to determine its properties, scope, and role in infinite-dimensional stability theory.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Consider an infinite-dimensional control system

  ẋ(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ X,  u ∈ U_c,

where X is a Banach state space, U_c is a space of admissible input functions u : [0,∞) → U taking values in a normed input space U (for instance L^∞_loc([0,∞); U)), and F generates a well-posed semiflow φ(t, x, u) with φ(0, x, u) = x. Denote by K the class of continuous, strictly increasing functions α : [0,∞) → [0,∞) with α(0) = 0; by K_∞ the subclass of unbounded such functions; and by KL the class of continuous β : [0,∞)² → [0,∞) such that β(·, t) ∈ K for each t and β(r, t) ↓ 0 as t → ∞.

Recall:
• The system is input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every x ∈ X and admissible u,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0.
• The system is integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and α, γ ∈ K_∞ such that
  α(‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + ∫_0^t γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds  for all t ≥ 0.
• Following the finite-dimensional definition, call the system strongly iISS if it is iISS and additionally ISS with respect to small inputs, i.e. there exist β ∈ KL, γ ∈ K, and a constant R > 0 such that for all admissible u with ‖u‖_∞ ≤ R,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0, x ∈ X.

Problem. Develop a theory of strong iISS for such infinite-dimensional control systems. In particular:
(a) Establish equivalent Lyapunov-function characterizations of strong iISS (e.g. the existence of a smooth iISS-Lyapunov function whose dissipation rate is positive definite, together with a small-input ISS condition).
(b) Determine the precise relationship of strong iISS to ISS, iISS, and to the existence of asymptotic gains, including whether strong iISS is strictly stronger than iISS and strictly weaker than ISS in the infinite-dimensional setting.
(c) Prove or disprove that strong iISS is preserved under cascade interconnection of infinite-dimensional systems and analyze its behaviour under feedback and small-gain interconnections.
(d) Identify nontrivial classes of infinite-dimensional systems (e.g. linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators, semilinear evolution equations, bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces) for which strong iISS can be verified, and provide checkable sufficient conditions in these classes.
status_search_result: Subsequent research has begun to develop strong iISS / strong ISS notions in infinite dimensions. Works on characterizations of ISS and iISS for infinite-dimensional and non-autonomous systems (e.g. Mironchenko-Wirth and follow-ups, and the 2022 characterization of integral ISS for time-varying systems of infinite dimension) have produced partial results, including Lyapunov-type characterizations and preservation under cascades, but a full systematic theory matching the finite-dimensional strong iISS framework does not yet appear complete in the literature.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Create general ISS methods for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional PDEs, not only for linear or semilinear equations of the form ẋ = Ax + f(x,u) with a bounded nonlinear part. In particular, extend ISS analysis to important fully nonlinear PDE classes such as porous medium and Navier–Stokes type equations, where nonlinear semigroup methods may be needed.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider control systems of the form
    x'(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  t > 0,  x(0) = x_0,
where the state x(t) takes values in a Banach space X, the input u belongs to the space U_c := L^∞(R_+, U) of essentially bounded measurable functions with values in a normed space U, and F generates (for each fixed input) a possibly nonlinear evolution. A typical existing framework treats the semilinear case
    x'(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t)),
where A generates a strongly continuous (linear) semigroup on X and f satisfies suitable Lipschitz/boundedness conditions.

A system Σ with state space X and input space U_c is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every initial state x_0 ∈ X, every admissible input u ∈ U_c, and all t ≥ 0,
    ‖x(t; x_0, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)}),
where K denotes continuous strictly increasing functions [0,∞) → [0,∞) vanishing at 0, and KL denotes functions β(r,t) that are class-K in r and decrease to 0 as t → ∞.

The theory of nonlinear semigroups (m-accretive operators, Crandall–Liggett generation, mild solutions in the sense of Bénilan–Crandall–Pazy) provides a unified well-posedness framework for fully nonlinear evolution equations including the porous medium equation
    ∂_t ρ = Δ(ρ^m) + b(ρ, u),  m > 1,
on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d with appropriate boundary conditions and distributed/boundary input u, and the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
    ∂_t v + (v · ∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + g(v, u),  div v = 0,
on a domain Ω with boundary conditions and an input u entering through forcing or boundary data.

Problem. Develop a general theory of input-to-state stability for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional control systems generated by (perturbed) nonlinear semigroups on Banach spaces. Specifically:

(a) Formulate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the nonlinear generator F (e.g., dissipativity/accretivity estimates, Lyapunov-type inequalities, or coercivity of an associated functional) and of the input dependence, that guarantee ISS of the resulting evolution with respect to inputs u ∈ L^∞(R_+, U).

(b) Apply the resulting framework to establish ISS (or appropriate variants such as integral ISS or strong ISS) for the porous medium equation and for the Navier–Stokes equations under physically meaningful classes of distributed and/or boundary disturbances.
status_search_result: A general ISS theory covering fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems via nonlinear semigroups, and applicable to the porous medium and Navier–Stokes equations under disturbances, does not appear to be established. Available literature focuses on linear or semilinear ISS results, or on stability of specific PDEs without an ISS-style robustness framework. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: Which broad and mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds can be described explicitly? Here an affine Poisson manifold means a finite-dimensional manifold equipped with an affine atlas and a Poisson bi-vector P whose Schouten self-bracket [[P,P]] vanishes.
self_contained_problem: An affine Poisson manifold is a pair $(M, P)$ where $M$ is a finite-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with an affine atlas (i.e. a maximal atlas whose chart transition maps are affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^{\dim M}$), and $P \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ is a bi-vector field on $M$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P, P]\!] = 0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Equivalently, the bracket $\{f, g\} := P(df, dg)$ on $C^\infty(M)$ is a Poisson bracket.\n\nProblem. Identify and explicitly describe broad, mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds $(M, P)$. That is, exhibit families of such pairs (for instance, characterized by the form of $P$ in affine coordinates, by symmetry, by the structure of the symplectic foliation, or by other geometric/algebraic properties) which are sufficiently large and natural to serve as a useful supply of examples, and give explicit normal forms or classifications within each class.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research question asking for a description of broad classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds. No comprehensive classification or solution appears in the literature; it remains an open-ended descriptive problem.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
context_brief: Stability and asymptotics of graph cocycles
original_question: For a graph cocycle γ=Σ_a c_a·γ_a on n vertices, are combinatorial statistics of the constituent graphs—such as diameter distributions and vertex-valency distributions—stable across the full cohomology class [γ]=[γ+d(λ)] after arbitrary coboundary changes by graphs λ on n−1 vertices? Relatedly, what is the large-n and asymptotic behavior of the dimension of graph cohomology, especially near the bi-grading ray (n, 2n−2) that is relevant for Poisson-bracket symmetries, and is there a generating function for those dimensions?
self_contained_problem:
Let G(n,k) denote the Kontsevich graph complex of equivalence classes (under sign-respecting graph automorphisms) of finite connected oriented graphs on n vertices and k edges, equipped with the standard differential d that inserts a new vertex and sums over ways of expanding an existing vertex (so coboundaries d(λ) of graphs λ on n−1 vertices land in graphs on n vertices). A graph cocycle is a finite formal linear combination γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a (with γ_a distinct equivalence classes of graphs on n vertices) satisfying d(γ) = 0, considered modulo the equivalence relation [γ] = [γ + d(λ)].

(a) Stability of combinatorial statistics. Fix n large. For a cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a on n vertices, define the multiset-valued statistics
  • Diam(γ) = the multiset of graph diameters of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|;
  • Val(γ) = the multiset of vertex-valency distributions of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|.
Determine whether Diam(γ) and Val(γ) (or natural normalizations thereof) are invariants of the cohomology class [γ], i.e. whether they are preserved under all coboundary modifications γ ↦ γ + d(λ) by graph cochains λ on n−1 vertices. If not invariants, identify which features of these statistics are well-defined on cohomology classes once n is sufficiently large.

(b) Asymptotics and generating function. Let H^{n,k} denote the cohomology of this graph complex in bi-grading (n vertices, k edges). Determine the large-n asymptotic behavior of dim H^{n,k}, with emphasis on the ray k = 2n − 2 (the bi-grading relevant to symmetries of Poisson brackets). In particular, determine whether there exists a generating function F(x,y) = Σ_{n,k} dim H^{n,k} x^n y^k (or its restriction along k = 2n − 2) admitting a closed form or functional equation, and describe the growth rate of dim H^{n, 2n−2} as n → ∞.
status_search_result: The dimensions of Kontsevich's graph cohomology remain an active subject of computational and theoretical research. Recent work (e.g., 11-loop computations posted in 2025) extends known dimensions but no closed-form generating function or asymptotic formula along the ray (n, 2n−2) is established. The cohomological-class invariance of combinatorial statistics such as diameter and valency distributions does not appear to be settled in the literature. The problems thus appear open.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: For the bi-grading ray (N, 2N), beginning at which N′>7 do nontrivial cocycles ω in the graph-complex kernel ker d exist, and beginning at which larger N′′ are those cocycles orientable to nonzero Kontsevich graphs built from wedges? Can one give explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P) using known cocycles γ and new cocycles ω on that ray?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Kontsevich's graph complex of finite undirected graphs on N vertices and 2N edges (for N ≥ 1), graded by the number of vertices and edges, equipped with the vertex-expansion differential d. A cocycle ω is an element of ker d. Along the bi-grading ray (#V, #E) = (N, 2N), the well-known wheel cocycles γ_{2ℓ+1} (the tetrahedron γ_3 at N=4, the pentagon-wheel γ_5 at N=6, the heptagon-wheel γ_7 at N=8, ...) are known to exist. For an undirected graph cocycle ω, let O→r(ω)(P) denote Kontsevich's orientation morphism producing, when no obstructions occur, an oriented graph cocycle built from wedges ←•→ which encodes an infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ = O→r(ω)(P) of any Poisson structure P on an affine manifold.

Solve the following:
(a) Determine the smallest integer N′ > 7 such that there exists a nontrivial cocycle ω ∈ ker d in the graph complex on the ray (N′, 2N′) that is not in the linear span of the previously known wheel cocycles.
(b) Determine the smallest integer N″ ≥ N′ such that some such new cocycle ω on the ray (N″, 2N″) is orientable, i.e. encounters no obstruction in passing through O→r(·) to a nonzero oriented Kontsevich graph cocycle built from wedges.
(c) Provide explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form
   Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P),  m ≠ 0,
where γ is a known wheel cocycle and ω is a new cocycle constructed in part (b).
status_search_result: Web sources confirm that on the ray (N, 2N) the known wheel cocycles γ_3, γ_5, γ_7 exist at N = 4, 6, 8, but no published computation appears to identify a new nontrivial cocycle at N′ > 7 nor establish its orientability or produce explicit composite Poisson-bracket symmetries of the stated form. The problem is presented as an explicit open problem in the relevant literature with no resolution found.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: Do there exist universal infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of Poisson structures that are nonlinear, proper, valid for all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds, and not produced from graph cocycles through Kontsevich’s orientation morphism O→r?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold, i.e. an affine space equipped with a Poisson bivector $P \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!] = 0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. An infinitesimal symmetry of the Poisson structure is a bivector-valued functional $Q(P) \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$, polynomial-differential in the components of $P$, such that the linearized Jacobi identity holds:
$$[\![P, Q(P)]\!] = 0.$$
Such a symmetry $Q$ is called:
- universal if a single universal differential-polynomial expression in $P$ defines $Q(P)$ simultaneously for every affine Poisson manifold of every finite dimension;
- proper if it is not of the form $[\![P, X(P)]\!]$ for any vector field $X(P)$ that is itself a universal differential-polynomial in $P$ (i.e. it is nontrivial in the relevant Poisson cohomology);
- nonlinear if its expression involves at least two copies of $P$ (so that it is not linear in $P$).

Kontsevich's orientation morphism $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}$ is a linear map from the (unoriented) graph complex to the space of universal differential-polynomial bivectors on affine Poisson manifolds: to each cocycle $\gamma$ in the Kontsevich graph complex it associates a universal infinitesimal symmetry $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ of $P$, obtained by summing over all admissible orientations of $\gamma$ with two outgoing edges at a chosen vertex and decorating each oriented edge with a copy of $P$.

Question. Do there exist nonlinear, proper, universal infinitesimal symmetries $Q(P)$ of Poisson structures (universal with respect to all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds) that do not arise as $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)$ for any cocycle $\gamma$ in the Kontsevich graph complex (modulo trivial symmetries)?

No source found claims to have produced or ruled out such non-graph universal symmetries, so the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: What are the Liouville-integrability and possible super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems Ṗ = Q(P) that arise from known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $M$ be a smooth (or formal) manifold and let $P=P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i\wedge\partial_j$ be a Poisson bi-vector on $M$, i.e. a smooth section of $\Lambda^2 TM$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!]=0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. A Kontsevich graph cocycle is a finite linear combination $\gamma=\sum c_\alpha \Gamma_\alpha$ of oriented graphs $\Gamma_\alpha$ on $n$ internal (aerial) vertices and two ground (sink) vertices, with two outgoing edges from each internal vertex, such that the universal bi-vector $Q_\gamma(P)$ obtained by inserting copies of $P$ at the internal vertices and contracting along the edge orientations satisfies the infinitesimal-symmetry equation
$$[\![P,Q_\gamma(P)]\!]=0\qquad\text{for every Poisson bi-vector }P.$$
Such a $\gamma$ thus determines a flow $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ on the variety of Poisson structures, where the right-hand side is a polynomial differential expression in the components $P^{ij}$ and their partial derivatives. Concrete examples include the tetrahedral flow $\dot P = Q_{\gamma_3}(P)$ and the higher graph cocycles $\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots$ producing nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems for the components $P^{ij}(x,t)$.

Recall that an evolutionary PDE system is called Liouville-integrable if it admits an infinite hierarchy of independent commuting symmetries (equivalently, an infinite family of Poisson-commuting conserved functionals in involution with respect to a compatible Hamiltonian structure), and super-integrable if it admits, in addition, further independent (not necessarily commuting) integrals beyond what Liouville integrability requires.

Problem. Determine the Liouville-integrability and, when applicable, the super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ associated with the known Kontsevich graph symmetries $\gamma$ of Poisson bi-vectors (in particular $\gamma_3$, $\gamma_5$, $\gamma_7$, and the linear combinations of graph cocycles producing nontrivial Poisson cohomology classes). Specifically:
(a) Exhibit, or prove the nonexistence of, an infinite hierarchy of commuting symmetries of $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$.
(b) Construct a (bi-)Hamiltonian formulation, recursion operator, or Lax representation, or prove that none exists.
(c) Decide whether any such system is super-integrable in the sense above.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
context_brief: Preservation of Nambu-type brackets on R^3
original_question: Consider the two-parameter family of Poisson brackets on R^3 defined by {f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)), where a is a smooth function and ρ is a density in the chosen coordinates. Is this class preserved by any Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ=Q(P), and for a given symmetry does there exist an induced evolutionary system ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) whose pushforward under τ:(a,ρ)↦{·,·}_{a,ρ} equals Q(P([a],ρ))?
self_contained_problem:
On $\mathbb{R}^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,z)$, consider the two-parameter family of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets
$$\{f,g\}_{a,\rho}(x,y,z) \;=\; \rho(x,y,z)\,\det\!\Big(\tfrac{\partial(a,f,g)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\Big),$$
where $a\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a Casimir function and $\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a density (the bracket is Poisson, i.e. skew-symmetric and Jacobi-satisfying, for every choice of $a,\rho$). Let $P=(P^{ij})$ denote the associated Poisson bi-vector and let
$$\dot P^{ij} \;=\; Q^{ij}_{P\alpha\beta}([a],\rho)$$
be a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry of $P$, i.e.\ a bi-vector flow built from a non-trivial cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex which preserves the Jacobi identity to first order.

Define the linear differential operator
$$\tau:(a,\rho)\longmapsto \{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}.$$

(i) Determine whether the class $\{\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho} : a,\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)\,\}$ is preserved under every Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry $\dot P=Q(P)$.

(ii) For a given Kontsevich symmetry $Q$, decide whether there exists an evolutionary system in the jet space with fibre variables $a,\rho$,
$$\dot a \;=\; A([a],[\rho]),\qquad \dot\rho \;=\; R([a],[\rho]),$$
whose pushforward under the tangent map $\tau_*$ equals $Q(P([a],\rho))$, i.e.
$$\tau_*\!\big(A([a],[\rho]),R([a],[\rho])\big) \;=\; Q\big(P([a],\rho)\big).$$
Describe such $(A,R)$ explicitly when they exist.
category_tag: Kontsevich graph flows on Nambu–Poisson brackets
status_search_result: Subsequent work has established that on $\mathbb{R}^3$ the class of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}$ is preserved by the known Kontsevich graph flows (tetrahedral and pentagon-wheel), with explicit evolutionary systems for $(a,\rho)$ realizing the symmetry; the corresponding deformations are trivial in second Poisson cohomology. The general statement for arbitrary Kontsevich symmetries and in higher dimensions remains under active investigation, with dimension-specific obstructions (e.g. invisible graphs) appearing in $d\geq 4$. Thus the problem is partially solved for the originally posed setting on $\mathbb{R}^3$.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how large is the family of trivialising vector fields X=X(γ) associated with graph cocycles γ∈ker d? Is the vector space of these vector fields locally complete enough to approximate arbitrary vector fields on the manifold, so that the exponentials of the trivialising fields could effectively imitate a smooth structure on the affine Poisson manifold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ be an affine Poisson manifold of dimension $r$, that is, a smooth manifold equipped with a Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ whose components in some affine atlas are polynomial (in particular, take the standard affine setting in which $P$ is given globally by polynomial coefficients). Consider the Kontsevich graph complex of unoriented finite graphs with a wedge-ordering on edges, equipped with the differential $d$ obtained by vertex-expansion. To each cocycle $\gamma\in\ker d$ one associates, via the Kontsevich orientation morphism applied to $(\gamma,P)$, a vector field $X(\gamma)=X(\gamma,P)\in\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ — called a trivialising vector field — with the property that the bivector flow $\dot P=[\![P,X(\gamma)]\!]$ realises the infinitesimal Poisson-cohomology-trivial deformation produced by $\gamma$.
\medskip

Question. Describe the size of the family
$$\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)=\{\,X(\gamma,P): \gamma\in\ker d\,\}\subset\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}}).$$
More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Is the linear span of $\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ locally complete in $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$, in the sense that for every point $x\in M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, every smooth vector field on a neighbourhood of $x$ can be approximated (in the $C^\infty$ topology) by elements of this span?
\item Equivalently, do the time-one flows $\exp(tX(\gamma,P))$, as $\gamma$ ranges over $\ker d$ and $t$ over $\mathbb{R}$, generate a (pseudo)group rich enough to imitate the full diffeomorphism action on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ preserving $P$?
\end{enumerate}
Determine, for a given $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, whether such local completeness holds, and if not, characterise the closure of $\mathrm{span}\,\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ inside $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$.
category_tag: Kontsevich graph cocycles and Poisson geometry
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning the size and local completeness of the family of trivialising vector fields produced by Kontsevich graph cocycles on affine Poisson manifolds. No published resolution was located; the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: How does the graph complex act on the space of deformation-quantisation star-products, especially under gauge transformations ⋆⇄⋆′, when the leading Poisson bi-vector in a Kontsevich star-product ⋆ = × + ħ{·,·}_P + o(ħ) is shifted by a graph-generated symmetry Q(P)=O→r(γ)(P) to P+εQ(P)+o(ε)? Can this action be described explicitly and illustrated by examples?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $P$ be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth manifold $M$, and let
$$\star \;=\; \times \;+\; \hbar\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_P \;+\; o(\hbar)$$
be a Kontsevich formal deformation-quantisation star-product on $C^\infty(M)[[\hbar]]$ whose leading deformation term is the Poisson bracket associated with $P$. Two such star-products $\star$ and $\star'$ are called gauge-equivalent if there exists a formal differential operator $T = \mathrm{id} + \hbar T_1 + \hbar^2 T_2 + \cdots$ such that
$$T(f \star g) \;=\; T(f) \star' T(g) \qquad \text{for all } f,g \in C^\infty(M)[[\hbar]].$$

Let $\mathsf{GC}$ denote Kontsevich's graph complex of (un)oriented graphs with the vertex-expansion differential $[\bullet\!-\!\bullet,\,\cdot\,]$. For each cocycle $\gamma \in \ker[\bullet\!-\!\bullet,\,\cdot\,]$, the orient-and-realise map produces a multivector field $Q(P) := \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ that is a symmetry of the Poisson structure, in the sense that $P + \varepsilon\,Q(P) + o(\varepsilon)$ is again Poisson modulo $\varepsilon^2$.

Problem. Describe explicitly the induced action of the graph complex $\mathsf{GC}$ on the set of Kontsevich star-products. Specifically:

1. Given a graph cocycle $\gamma$ and a star-product $\star$ as above, define and compute an infinitesimal deformation $\star \mapsto \star + \varepsilon\,\delta_\gamma(\star) + o(\varepsilon)$ whose leading-order Poisson bi-vector is shifted from $\hbar P$ to $\hbar P + \varepsilon\,Q(\hbar P) + o(\varepsilon)$.

2. Determine how this action interacts with gauge equivalence $\star \rightleftarrows \star'$: in particular, decide whether gauge-equivalent star-products are sent to gauge-equivalent star-products, and identify the induced action on gauge-equivalence classes.

3. Illustrate the construction with explicit examples (e.g. using small graph cocycles such as the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ or the pentagon-wheel $\gamma_5$) on concrete Poisson manifolds.
category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and deformation quantization
status_search_result: The problem of explicitly describing the action of Kontsevich's graph complex on star-products and on their gauge equivalence classes appears to remain open. Related developments include software (gcaops) computing the graph-complex action on Poisson structures, and theses/papers describing the action on Poisson structures and their formal deformations, but a complete explicit description at the level of star-products including gauge-transformation behaviour, with worked examples, has not been established as a finished theory.

paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
original_question: Do universal infinitesimal symmetries Ṗ=Q(P) of classical Poisson structures survive under Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, where the classical master equation [[P,P]]=0 is replaced by iħΔP + 1/2[[P,P]] = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth (affine) manifold, so that the classical master equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ holds, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten bracket on multi-vectors. A universal infinitesimal symmetry of the class of Poisson structures is a map $P\mapsto Q(P)$, built from $P$ by a universal (e.g. Kontsevich-graph) formula in the partial derivatives of the components of $P$, such that the flow $\dot P=Q(P)$ preserves the equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$, i.e. $[\![Q(P),P]\!]=0$ whenever $[\![P,P]\!]=0$.

In the Batalin–Vilkovisky framework, the classical master equation is replaced by the quantum master equation
$$i\hbar\,\Delta P + \tfrac12\,[\![P,P]\!] = 0,$$
where $\Delta$ is the BV Laplacian acting on the relevant space of (formal) multi-vectors / functionals, and $P$ is now allowed to depend formally on $\hbar$.

Question: Does every universal infinitesimal symmetry $\dot P=Q(P)$ of the classical equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ (in particular, those produced by the Kontsevich graph construction) persist under Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, in the sense that the flow $\dot P=Q(P)$ — possibly after a universal $\hbar$-deformation $Q(P)\mapsto Q_\hbar(P)$ — preserves the quantum master equation $i\hbar\,\Delta P + \tfrac12\,[\![P,P]\!]=0$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the Kontsevich-graph symmetry literature. A 2025 follow-up listing of open problems on Kontsevich graphs acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets still discusses BV-quantisation persistence among unresolved questions, and no published resolution of the persistence under BV quantisation of universal Kontsevich-graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors appears in the literature.

paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
context_brief: Periodic boundary conditions in snapshot models
original_question: In temporal-network epidemic models that compute the epidemic threshold from a repeated sequence of adjacency-matrix snapshots A_1, ..., A_T, one often imposes a periodic boundary condition A(T+t) = A_t so that the observed snapshot sequence repeats indefinitely. This repetition can create time-respecting transmission paths that did not exist in the original finite temporal network. Does imposing that periodic boundary condition change the epidemic threshold that is estimated for the original temporal contact network, and if so, how?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time temporal network on a fixed set of $N$ nodes given by a finite sequence of adjacency-matrix snapshots $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_T$, where $A_t \in \{0,1\}^{N\times N}$ records the contacts active during time step $t$. On this temporal network, run a discrete-time Markovian SIS spreading process with per-contact transmission probability $\lambda$ and per-step recovery probability $\mu$, and define the epidemic threshold $\lambda_c$ as the smallest $\lambda$ for which the disease-free state is unstable.

A standard analytic approach computes $\lambda_c$ by extending the snapshot sequence periodically, i.e., imposing the periodic boundary condition
$$A_{t+T} \equiv A_t \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{Z},$$
so that the network is treated as an infinitely repeated cycle of the original $T$ snapshots, and then analyzing the spectral radius of the product $\prod_{t=1}^{T}\bigl[(1-\mu)I + \lambda A_t\bigr]$ (or an analogous transmission operator).

Repeating the snapshot sequence can create time-respecting paths $(i_0, t_0) \to (i_1, t_1) \to \cdots$ (with $t_0 < t_1 < \cdots$ and $A_{t_k}(i_{k-1}, i_k) = 1$) that do not exist within the single original window $\{1,\dots,T\}$.

Question: Does imposing the periodic boundary condition $A_{t+T} \equiv A_t$ change the epidemic threshold of the original finite temporal contact network $(A_1,\dots,A_T)$ compared to the threshold one would obtain without periodic repetition? If so, characterize quantitatively how the threshold depends on $T$ and on the structure of the snapshots, and identify conditions (e.g., a minimum period length) under which the periodic-boundary threshold faithfully recovers the threshold of the non-repeated temporal network.
status_search_result: Available reviews and follow-up work on temporal-network epidemic thresholds reiterate that the periodic-boundary assumption used by Valdano et al. may introduce additional time-respecting paths not present in the original finite temporal network, and explicitly state that whether this changes the estimated epidemic threshold remains unresolved. Numerical heuristics for an "optimal minimum period length" have been explored, but no general analytical resolution was found in the search.

paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
original_question: Temporal contact patterns may be periodic because of seasonal or other recurring changes in behavior and social interaction. What effect do such periodic contact patterns have on disease spreading and epidemic thresholds in temporal networks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a temporal network model in which the contact structure is described by a time-indexed sequence of graphs $\{G_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}$ on a fixed vertex set $V$ of $n$ nodes, where each $G_t = (V, E_t)$ specifies which pairs of nodes are in contact at discrete time $t$. Assume the sequence is periodic with period $T \geq 1$, i.e. $G_{t+T} = G_t$ for all $t \geq 0$. On this temporal network, run a susceptible–infected–susceptible (SIS) (or SIR) Markovian spreading process: at each time step $t$, an infected node infects each susceptible neighbor in $G_t$ independently with probability $\beta \in (0,1]$, and each infected node recovers independently with probability $\mu \in (0,1]$. Define the epidemic threshold as the critical ratio $(\beta/\mu)_c$ above which the expected number of infected nodes does not vanish in the long-time limit (equivalently, the spectral threshold characterizing the stability of the disease-free state under the periodic time-inhomogeneous dynamics).

Problem. Determine the effect of the periodicity $T$ and the structure of the periodic sequence $\{G_t\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ on the epidemic threshold $(\beta/\mu)_c$ and on the qualitative behavior of disease spread. In particular:

(a) Derive an analytical expression (or sharp bounds) for $(\beta/\mu)_c$ as a function of $T$ and of the sequence of adjacency matrices $A_0, A_1, \dots, A_{T-1}$, for example in terms of the spectral radius of the product $\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\big((1-\mu) I + \beta A_t\big)$ or an analogous operator capturing one full period.

(b) Identify how the threshold compares with that of (i) the time-aggregated static network with adjacency $\bar A = \tfrac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_t$, and (ii) a randomly shuffled (non-periodic) version of the same sequence, and characterize regimes in which periodicity raises or lowers the threshold.

(c) Determine whether resonance phenomena can occur between the period $T$ of the contact pattern and the intrinsic time scale $1/\mu$ of the recovery process, and quantify their impact on outbreak size and on the prevalence in the endemic state.
status_search_result: Recent reviews and research on epidemic spreading on temporal networks (including the 2019/2021 review on epidemic thresholds and the 2021 Royal Society Interface review on concurrency measures) note that periodic/seasonal contact patterns have not been explicitly analyzed for their effect on epidemic thresholds in temporal networks, although standard temporal network models can in principle be extended to periodic settings. Analytical thresholds exist for some time-varying models (e.g., Valdano et al., Phys. Rev. X 2015), but a systematic theory specifically addressing periodic/seasonal contact structure and its impact on the threshold remains undeveloped.

paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
original_question: When one uses a closed temporal-network model for analytic or computational tractability even though the real population interacts with individuals outside the modeled network, can those external interactions be incorporated statistically in a way that still yields useful epidemic-threshold calculations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a population modeled by a temporal contact network: a vertex set $V$ together with a time-indexed family of edge sets $\{E(t)\}_{t \in T}$, encoding which pairs of individuals are in contact at each time. On this network, run a stochastic compartmental epidemic process (e.g., SIS or SIR) with infection rate $\beta$ along active edges and recovery rate $\mu$. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of $\beta/\mu$ separating extinction of the infection from a sustained outbreak.

For analytical or computational tractability, one often restricts attention to a closed temporal-network model, in which only contacts among the vertices of $V$ are represented, even though in reality individuals in $V$ also interact with individuals outside $V$. Model these unmodeled external contacts statistically: for instance, augment each vertex $v \in V$ with an independent inhomogeneous external infection process of rate $\lambda_v(t)$ (or, equivalently, attach a random time-varying boundary force of infection drawn from a prescribed distribution, possibly correlated across vertices and time).

The problem is the following: design such a statistical augmentation and a corresponding analytic framework so that one can compute (or rigorously bound) the epidemic threshold of the closed temporal-network model with external forcing, in a way that yields predictions which usefully approximate the threshold of the true open system. Concretely, identify classes of temporal networks and classes of external-interaction statistical models for which the epidemic threshold can be derived in closed form or via a tractable spectral / mean-field calculation, and quantify the error introduced by replacing the open system with the closed-plus-external-forcing surrogate.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the temporal-networks epidemic-threshold literature. Searches return the original review and related works on threshold computations for closed temporal-network models (spectral, contact-based, switching, modular formulations), but no work that systematically incorporates statistical models of external (off-network) interactions into a tractable threshold calculation. The question therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
context_brief: Statistical network models and community detection
original_question: Most epidemic-threshold work on temporal networks assumes that the network is deterministic and fully observed, but many practical settings require uncertainty quantification, prediction of future interactions, and inference of latent community structure. How can results on epidemic thresholds for temporal networks be connected to statistical network models and community-detection methods so that threshold analysis remains usable when the network is only partially known or must be modeled probabilistically?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a temporal network on a finite vertex set $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$, represented as a sequence of (possibly weighted) adjacency matrices $\{A_t\}_{t=1}^{T}$, where $A_t(i,j)$ encodes the strength or presence of an interaction between vertices $i$ and $j$ at discrete time $t$. On such a network run a Markovian SIS epidemic process: at each time step, an infected vertex $i$ infects a neighbor $j$ along edge $(i,j)$ at rate $\beta A_t(i,j)$, and each infected vertex recovers independently at rate $\delta>0$. The epidemic threshold $\tau^* = \tau^*(\{A_t\}, \delta)$ is the critical value of $\beta/\delta$ separating the regime where the expected time to extinction is $O(\log n)$ from the regime where it is $\exp(\Omega(n))$.

Now suppose the network is not deterministically observed but is generated from a statistical network model with latent community structure. Specifically, let $z:V\to\{1,\dots,K\}$ assign each vertex to one of $K$ communities, and let $\{A_t\}$ be drawn from a dynamic stochastic block model with community-pair interaction rates $B_t \in [0,1]^{K\times K}$, so that conditional on $z$ the entries $A_t(i,j)$ are independent Bernoulli$(B_t(z_i,z_j))$ random variables. Assume only a partial observation of $\{A_t\}$ is available (for instance edges revealed up to time $T_0<T$, or a subsample of edges).

Develop a framework producing:

(a) a definition of the epidemic threshold $\tau^*$ in this probabilistic, partially observed setting, together with a rigorous estimator $\hat\tau$ of $\tau^*$ computable from the observed portion of $\{A_t\}$ and from community labels inferred by a community-detection procedure;

(b) finite-sample concentration or consistency guarantees of the form $\hat\tau \to \tau^*$ (in probability, as $n\to\infty$ or $T\to\infty$) under stated identifiability conditions on the dynamic stochastic block model;

(c) valid uncertainty quantification (e.g.\ confidence intervals or posterior credible sets) for $\tau^*$ that incorporate both the randomness of the network model and errors arising from imperfect community recovery and from prediction of future interactions $\{A_t\}_{t>T_0}$.

The problem is to construct such a framework and to prove that it yields consistent estimation and asymptotically valid uncertainty quantification of the epidemic threshold under explicit, minimal assumptions on the dynamic stochastic block model.

No published work appears to provide a unified framework giving consistent estimation and uncertainty quantification of epidemic thresholds on partially observed temporal networks generated from dynamic stochastic block models, so the problem appears to remain open.
