original_question: For three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals obtained by combining differently oriented grains of a single crystal, what pairs (kappa*,mu*) of effective bulk and shear moduli are achievable? In particular, can one characterize the full feasible region beyond the currently sharp bulk-modulus bounds and the known but non-optimal shear-modulus bounds?
self_contained_problem:
Consider three-dimensional linearly elastic polycrystals: composite materials assembled from grains that are all copies of a single anisotropic crystal, where the grains differ only by rigid rotations of the crystal's elasticity tensor. Assume the grain geometry is such that the resulting composite is macroscopically (statistically) isotropic, so that its effective elasticity tensor is described by an effective bulk modulus κ* and an effective shear modulus μ*.

Given the elasticity tensor of a fixed single crystal, determine the set
G = { (κ*, μ*) ∈ ℝ_{>0} × ℝ_{>0} : (κ*, μ*) is realizable as the pair of effective bulk and shear moduli of some macroscopically isotropic 3D polycrystal built from rotated copies of the given crystal }.

Specifically: characterize G completely. The known sharp bounds on κ* alone, together with the known (but not generally optimal) bounds on μ*, confine G to a rectangle in the (κ*, μ*)-plane; the task is to determine the precise feasible region within (or strictly inside) this rectangle, and to exhibit microgeometries attaining each point of the boundary.
status_search_result: In the planar (2D) case, a complete characterization of the achievable (κ*, μ*) pairs for polycrystals built from a single crystal was obtained by Avellaneda–Cherkaev–Gibiansky–Milton–Rudelson and refined in subsequent works (including extremal planar polycrystal constructions published in 2021). In three dimensions, the bulk-modulus bounds are sharp but the shear-modulus bounds are generally not optimal, and no complete characterization of the feasible (κ*, μ*) region appears in the literature; recent works (e.g., on Hashin–Shtrikman bounds for 3D polycrystals of arbitrary symmetry) only provide bounds, not a full characterization. The problem is thus still open in 3D.

paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
original_question: For the algebraic structure of the Weihrauch degrees with signature (W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄), what can be said about the first-order theory Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄)? In particular, is the quantifier-free part of this theory finitely axiomatizable, and do any fragments of the signature admit finite axiomatizations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{W}$ denote the partially ordered set of Weihrauch degrees, that is, equivalence classes of multivalued functions between represented spaces under Weihrauch reducibility $\le_{\mathrm{W}}$ (where $f \le_{\mathrm{W}} g$ iff there exist computable maps $H, K$ such that for every realizer $G$ of $g$, the map $x \mapsto H(x, G(K(x)))$ is a realizer of $f$). Consider the algebraic structure
$$(\mathcal{W};\, 0,\, 1,\, \top;\, \sqcap,\, \sqcup,\, \times,\, \star,\, \to,\, {}^{*},\, \mathrm{b},\, \diamond),$$
where $0$ is the degree of the nowhere-defined problem, $1$ is the identity, $\top$ is the top degree; $\sqcap$ and $\sqcup$ are the infimum (parallel product with choice) and supremum operations on the lattice; $\times$ is the parallel product; $\star$ is the compositional product (the maximum of $f \circ g'$ over $f' \equiv_{\mathrm{W}} f$, $g' \equiv_{\mathrm{W}} g$); $\to$ is the implication / residual; ${}^{*}$ is finite parallelization; $\mathrm{b}$ is the Brattka–Pauly closure operator (e.g., the "bar" / total continuation); and $\diamond$ is the diamond operator (transfinite/iterated compositional closure).

Determine what can be said about the first-order theory
$$\mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{W};\, 0, 1, \top;\, \sqcap, \sqcup, \times, \star, \to, {}^{*}, \mathrm{b}, \diamond).$$
In particular:
(a) Is the quantifier-free fragment of this theory finitely axiomatizable?
(b) For which fragments of the signature (i.e., reducts to subsets of the operations and constants above) does the resulting structure admit a finite axiomatization of its (quantifier-free or full first-order) theory?
status_search_result: No published work was found that determines the first-order theory of the Weihrauch degrees in this rich signature, nor establishes finite axiomatizability of its quantifier-free fragment or of substantial fragments of the signature. The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on Weihrauch complexity, and search results show only related work on formalization of Weihrauch reducibility (e.g., via Γ₁ formulas) rather than an answer to the axiomatization question.

paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
original_question: Is there any natural computational problem, for example one arising in linear algebra, whose Weihrauch degree is AoUC⋄, where AoUC is the degree of finding a solution to bx = a with 0 ≤ a ≤ b?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Work in the framework of Weihrauch reducibility on multi-valued partial functions between represented spaces. For multi-valued problems f, g, write f ≤_W g for Weihrauch reducibility. Two problems are Weihrauch-equivalent (denoted ≡_W) if they reduce to each other; a Weihrauch degree is an equivalence class under ≡_W.

Define the problem AoUC ("All-or-Unique Choice on the unit interval") as follows: given a pair (a, b) of real numbers with 0 ≤ a ≤ b, AoUC outputs any real x satisfying b·x = a. (Equivalently, if b > 0 the unique solution x = a/b must be produced, and if b = 0 any real x is an admissible output.)

For a problem f, the diamond operator f^⋄ denotes the closure of f under finite (adaptively chosen) compositions: f^⋄ is, up to Weihrauch equivalence, the supremum of f, f ⋆ f, f ⋆ f ⋆ f, …, where ⋆ is the compositional product in the Weihrauch lattice. Thus AoUC^⋄ is the Weihrauch degree obtained by allowing finitely many adaptive applications of AoUC.

Problem.

Exhibit a "natural" computational problem — for instance, one arising from a standard question in linear algebra — whose Weihrauch degree is precisely AoUC^⋄, or prove that no such natural problem exists.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution identifying a natural (e.g. linear-algebraic) problem of Weihrauch degree exactly AoUC^⋄. Related work on AoUC and the diamond operator exists, but no source verifies a solution; status is therefore unclear from available evidence.

paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
original_question: Is there a clear structural account of how the additional degrees that appear in the extended Weihrauch degrees are related to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A multi-valued function (problem) on Baire space is a partial relation $f \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}} \times \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, where the domain consists of "instances" and, for each instance $x$, the set $f(x) = \{y : (x,y) \in f\}$ is the set of "solutions". Weihrauch reducibility $f \le_W g$ holds iff there exist computable functionals $H, K$ such that, for every instance $x$ of $f$, $K(x)$ is an instance of $g$ and, for every solution $y$ of $g$ on $K(x)$, $H(x,y)$ is a solution of $f$ on $x$. The resulting equivalence classes form the Weihrauch degrees, a lattice studied in computable analysis.

Extended Weihrauch reducibility generalises this notion by allowing the "instances" and "solutions" to be arbitrary subsets of Baire space (rather than single points), and by formulating the reduction in a realizability framework (e.g. as instance degrees in the Kleene–Vesley realizability topos). The resulting structure, the extended Weihrauch degrees, contains a canonical embedding of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees but properly extends them with additional degrees not arising from any single multi-valued function in the classical sense.

Problem. Provide a clear structural account describing how the additional degrees that occur in the extended Weihrauch degrees but not in the (image of the) ordinary Weihrauch degrees relate to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees. In particular, characterise the new degrees in terms of natural operations (such as suprema, infima, implications, or other lattice-theoretic / topos-theoretic constructions) applied to ordinary Weihrauch degrees, or otherwise describe their position within the extended Weihrauch lattice relative to the embedded copy of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees.
status_search_result: Recent work has clarified part of the picture: the ordinary Weihrauch degrees embed into the extended Weihrauch degrees as the ¬¬-dense modest instance degrees in a (relative) realizability topos, and a topos-theoretic semantics for the extended degrees has been developed. This provides a structural framework relating the two, but a fully explicit characterisation of all "new" extended degrees in terms of operations on ordinary Weihrauch degrees does not appear to be completely settled, so the question is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
context_brief: Classification of uniqueness ranges and boundary conditions
original_question: Consider the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse spectral problem in which, for j=0,1, L_j(a,q) is defined by -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) on 0<x<pi with boundary conditions y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0, where q is a complex-valued L2(0,pi) potential satisfying q(x)=0 on (0,a), and a is in (0,pi). Given the two spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}}, for which ranges of the delay parameter a and for which admissible boundary-condition types does this data uniquely determine q, and for which choices does uniqueness fail?
self_contained_problem:
For a complex-valued potential $q\in L_2(0,\pi)$ that vanishes on $(0,a)$ where $a\in(0,\pi)$, and for $j=0,1$, let $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$ denote the boundary value problem
$$-y''(x)+q(x)\,y(x-a)=\lambda\,y(x),\qquad 0<x<\pi,$$
with the boundary conditions $y(0)=0$ and $y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$ (Dirichlet at $\pi$ for $j=0$, Neumann at $\pi$ for $j=1$). Let $\{\lambda_{n,j}\}_{n\ge 1}$ be the eigenvalue sequence of $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$. 

Inverse Problem. Given the two spectra $\{\lambda_{n,0}\}$ and $\{\lambda_{n,1}\}$, recover $q$.

Determine, more generally, the complete classification of pairs $(a,\text{boundary-condition type})$ — where the boundary condition at $0$ and at $\pi$ are each chosen from an admissible family of separated linear conditions — for which the two spectra uniquely determine the potential $q$, and the pairs for which uniqueness fails (i.e., for which there exist iso-bispectral potentials).
category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for delay Sturm–Liouville operators
status_search_result: The classification has been advanced but remains incomplete. Uniqueness from the two spectra is known to hold for delays $a\in[2\pi/5,\pi)$ (with Dirichlet/Neumann at $\pi$), while non-uniqueness has been established for $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$ via explicit families of iso-bispectral potentials. Subsequent works extend results to Robin boundary conditions, graphs with global delay, and small-delay non-uniqueness, but a full classification across all delays $a\in(0,\pi)$ and all admissible boundary-condition types is not yet complete.

paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
original_question: Determine the uniqueness or nonuniqueness behavior of the delayed Sturm-Liouville two-spectra inverse problem for arbitrarily small positive delays a, where -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) is close to the classical a=0 Sturm-Liouville equation -y''(x)+q(x)y(x)=lambda y(x). For small a>0, does the pair of spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}} recover q uniquely, and if not, what iso-bispectral families occur?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the functional-differential equation
  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x-a) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,π),
where a ∈ (0,π) is a constant delay, q ∈ L_2(0,π) is a real-valued potential with q(x) = 0 for x ∈ (0,a), and y(x-a) is interpreted as 0 on (0,a). For j ∈ {0,1}, let {λ_{n,j}}_{n≥1} denote the spectrum of the boundary value problem consisting of this equation together with the boundary conditions
  y(0) = 0,    y^(j)(π) = 0.

The classical (a = 0) result of Borg states that the two spectra {λ_{n,0}} and {λ_{n,1}} uniquely determine q.

Question: Investigate the regime of arbitrarily small positive delays a > 0. Does the pair of spectra ({λ_{n,0}}, {λ_{n,1}}) uniquely determine q for all sufficiently small a > 0? If not, exhibit and characterize the iso-bispectral families, i.e., distinct potentials q ≠ q̃ (with the same vanishing on (0,a)) that produce identical pairs of spectra for the corresponding two boundary value problems.
status_search_result: The question was answered negatively: for arbitrarily small delays, the two-spectra inverse problem for the delayed Sturm–Liouville operator does not uniquely recover the potential. Djurić and Buterin (2021, "Iso-bispectral potentials for Sturm–Liouville-type operators with small delay", Nonlinear Anal. RWA, also arXiv:2102.08149) constructed infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials, showing non-uniqueness persists as a → 0. Related counterexamples were given for the Neumann case (arXiv:2101.08557).

original_question: For the hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem, where one must distinguish an Erdős-Rényi d-hypergraph G_d(N, 1/2) from a planted-clique alternative G_d(N, 1/2, κ) formed by choosing κ vertices uniformly at random and connecting every hyperedge whose vertices all lie in that planted set, what is the sharp threshold on the clique size κ at which polynomial-time singular-value-decomposition-based detection on a matricization or unfolding of the adjacency tensor succeeds, and is there some other polynomial-time algorithm that can solve HPC detection for κ below that SVD threshold?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer d ≥ 3. For a positive integer N, let [N] = {1, …, N}. The Erdős–Rényi d-uniform hypergraph G_d(N, 1/2) is the random hypergraph on vertex set [N] in which each of the C(N,d) possible d-element hyperedges is included independently with probability 1/2. The hypergraphic planted clique model G_d(N, 1/2, κ), with clique size κ ∈ {1, …, N}, is generated as follows: first sample G ~ G_d(N, 1/2); then pick a subset K ⊂ [N] with |K| = κ uniformly at random; then add (or keep) every d-element hyperedge whose vertices all lie in K. The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem is the hypothesis testing problem

  H0: G ~ G_d(N, 1/2)   versus   H1: G ~ G_d(N, 1/2, κ),

with the goal of finding a test whose Type-I plus Type-II error probability tends to 0 as N → ∞.

Encode the hypergraph by its symmetric d-th order adjacency tensor A ∈ {0,1}^{N×N×…×N}. For an integer 1 ≤ k ≤ d−1, the (k, d−k)-matricization (unfolding) of A is the N^k × N^{d−k} matrix M_k(A) obtained by grouping the first k tensor indices into rows and the remaining d−k indices into columns. A "SVD-based detector on a matricization/unfolding of A" is any test that thresholds the leading singular value of M_k(A) (for some k) after appropriate centering.

Determine the following:

(a) Identify the sharp threshold function κ*(N, d) such that for κ ≫ κ*(N, d) some SVD-based test on a matricization/unfolding of A solves HPC detection (errors → 0), while for κ ≪ κ*(N, d) every such SVD-based test fails (errors → 1).

(b) Decide whether there exists a polynomial-time algorithm (not necessarily based on the SVD of a matricization) that solves HPC detection for some κ asymptotically below the threshold in (a).
status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem in 2020. A 2026 work studies spectral detection/recovery for planted cliques in hypergraphs and shows a spectral norm test is asymptotically powerful at the √N scale, but does not claim to have closed the SVD-vs-other-polynomial-time gap or to have resolved the open question. No source clearly establishes the sharp SVD matricization threshold together with a polynomial-time algorithm beating it, so the problem appears still open.

context_brief: Equivalence of HPC and PC hardness
original_question: At the regime κ = O(N^(1/2-τ)) for τ > 0, what is the precise average-case computational relationship between hypergraphic planted clique detection and ordinary planted clique detection? More specifically, since the paper states that HPC detection is no harder than PC detection because there is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from HPC to PC that preserves the planted clique size κ, can one also construct a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC to HPC, thereby proving that the two detection problems are computationally equivalent in this threshold regime?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d \geq 3$ and $N \geq 1$. The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem with parameters $(N, d, \kappa)$ is the following hypothesis testing problem on $d$-uniform hypergraphs with vertex set $[N]$, encoded by their symmetric adjacency tensor $A \in \{0,1\}^{N \times \cdots \times N}$ (with zero diagonal):

- Under $H_0$, every hyperedge $\{i_1,\dots,i_d\} \subseteq [N]$ is included independently with probability $1/2$ (Erdős–Rényi $d$-uniform random hypergraph).
- Under $H_1$, a uniformly random subset $S \subseteq [N]$ of size $\kappa$ is chosen and all $\binom{\kappa}{d}$ hyperedges contained in $S$ are present; every other hyperedge is included independently with probability $1/2$.

The case $d=2$ recovers the ordinary planted clique (PC) detection problem.

There is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from HPC$(N,d,\kappa)$ to PC$(N,\kappa)$ that preserves the planted clique size: given the tensor $A$, fixing any $d-2$ indices and varying the remaining two yields an $N \times N$ adjacency matrix that constitutes a PC instance with planted clique size $\kappa$. Hence HPC detection is no harder than PC detection.

Question: In the regime $\kappa = O(N^{1/2 - \tau})$ for some fixed $\tau > 0$, does there exist a randomized polynomial-time reduction in the reverse direction, from PC$(N,\kappa)$ detection to HPC$(N,d,\kappa)$ detection (preserving the planted clique size $\kappa$), thereby establishing that the two detection problems are computationally equivalent in this threshold regime?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open challenge concerning the equivalence of HPC and PC detection in the sub-square-root regime. A search for follow-up work (including reductions from PC to HPC and related tensor-PCA / hypergraph reductions through 2024–2025) did not surface a published randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC to HPC preserving the clique size $\kappa$. Existing literature establishes only the easy direction (HPC to PC) and various low-degree / SoS hardness results, but not the desired computational equivalence. The status therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: Let f be a nonzero integrable function on R such that the set {x in R : f(x) != 0} has finite Lebesgue measure. Suppose f tiles R at some level w with a translation set Lambda subset R of bounded density. Must Lambda have a periodic structure, meaning that Lambda can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions of the form a_j Z + b_j with a_j > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonzero function such that the set $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : f(x) \neq 0\}$ has finite Lebesgue measure. A discrete set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ is said to have bounded density if $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \#(\Lambda \cap [x, x+1]) < \infty$. We say that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w \in \mathbb{C}$ by the translation set $\Lambda$ if
$$\sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} f(x - \lambda) = w \quad \text{for almost every } x \in \mathbb{R},$$
with the series converging absolutely a.e. We say that $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions
$$\Lambda = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N} (a_j \mathbb{Z} + b_j),$$
where $a_j > 0$ and $b_j \in \mathbb{R}$.

Question: Suppose $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at some level $w$ by a translation set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ of bounded density. Must $\Lambda$ necessarily have a periodic structure?
status_search_result: The problem appears as an explicitly stated open question in the Kolountzakis–Lev survey on tiling by translates of a function (2020), and subsequent literature (e.g., later work by Kolountzakis and collaborators on tiling, spectrality and aperiodicity, 2023) continues to treat it as open. No published resolution was found.

original_question: Let f be a nonzero function in L1(R) with compact support, and suppose that f + Lambda is a tiling at some level w where Lambda is a discrete set of tempered growth, meaning that #(Lambda intersect (-r,r)) = O(r^N) as r -> +infinity for some N. Must Lambda necessarily be of the form Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), so that in particular Lambda has bounded density and periodic structure?
self_contained_problem:
Call a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $\#(\Lambda\cap(-r,r))=O(r^N)$ as $r\to\infty$. Say that $\Lambda$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, i.e. $\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{M}(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j)$ with real $b_j$ and $a_j>0$. Given $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and $w\in\mathbb{C}$, we say $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling of $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w$ if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(x-\lambda)=w$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, with the sum converging absolutely a.e.

Prove or disprove: if $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonzero with compact support and $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling at some level $w$ for a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth, then $\Lambda$ must have a periodic structure (and in particular bounded density).
status_search_result: The question is presented as an open problem in the 2021 survey by Kolountzakis and Lev (Discrete Analysis) on tilings by translates of a function. The corresponding result is known when f is nonnegative (translation set must be a finite union of periodic sets), but for general L^1 compactly supported f with only tempered-growth assumption on Λ, the problem appears unresolved in available literature.

original_question: For the real and complex fields F in {R, C}, determine the exact numerical values of the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C, where K_G^F is the least constant K for which every finite matrix (a_ij) over F and every choice of unit vectors u_i and v_j in an F-Hilbert space satisfy |Σ_i Σ_j a_ij ⟨u_i, v_j⟩| ≤ K sup{|Σ_i Σ_j a_ij p_i q_j| : |p_i| = |q_j| = 1}. If exact values cannot yet be obtained, develop methods that approximate K_G^R and K_G^C from above and below using the paper’s proposed framework of block matrix analysis, Gaussian random vectors, special functions, copulas, and combinatorics.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$. The Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{F}}$ is defined as the smallest constant $K\in[1,\infty)$ such that, for every positive integer $n$, every matrix $(a_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$ with entries in $\mathbb{F}$, every Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{F}$, and every choice of unit vectors $u_1,\dots,u_n,v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$,
$$\Bigl|\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\Bigr|\;\le\;K\,\sup\Bigl\{\Bigl|\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}p_iq_j\Bigr|\;:\;p_i,q_j\in\mathbb{F},\;|p_i|=|q_j|=1\Bigr\}.$$
Determine the exact numerical values of $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$ and $K_G^{\mathbb{C}}$. If exact values are not attainable, provide rigorous upper and lower bounds approximating them, e.g. via methods of block matrix analysis, Gaussian random vectors, special functions, copulas, and combinatorics.
status_search_result: The exact values of the real and complex Grothendieck constants have been an open problem since Grothendieck's 1953 résumé. Sharp upper and lower bounds are known (e.g., Krivine's bound and the Braverman–Makarychev–Makarychev–Naor improvement showing $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$ is strictly less than Krivine's bound), but the exact values remain unknown as of recent literature.

context_brief: Better CCP functions for K_G^R bounds
original_question: Find functions b: R^k → {-1, 1}, with k ≥ 1, that are different from the sign function and whose associated completely correlation-preserving function h_b satisfies the workflow needed to improve the known upper bound for the real Grothendieck constant: h_b(0)=0, h_b is a homeomorphism, its inverse g_b=h_b^{-1} has an absolutely summable real Taylor expansion, the absolute-coefficient series f_b has f_b(r)=1 for some 0<r<1, and the resulting theorem gives K_G^R ≤ 1/r.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For an integer k ≥ 1, let b : R^k → {−1, 1} be a Borel measurable function. For a positive integer d, let C_d denote the set of d×d real correlation matrices (symmetric positive semidefinite matrices with all diagonal entries equal to 1). Given X = (X_1,…,X_d) a centered Gaussian vector in R^{kd} whose "block correlation" structure is described by a matrix Σ ∈ C_d (with each block X_i ∈ R^k standard Gaussian), define the completely correlation preserving (CCP) function associated with b by

   h_b(Σ) := ( E[ b(X_i) b(X_j) ] )_{1 ≤ i,j ≤ d}    ∈ C_d.

Restricted to the diagonal "scalar input" r ∈ [−1, 1] (the case d = 2), h_b induces a real-analytic odd function on (−1, 1), still denoted h_b, with h_b(0) = 0 in the case relevant below.

Workflow conditions. Say that b satisfies the workflow if all of the following hold:
 (H) h_b : [−1, 1] → [−1, 1] is a homeomorphism with h_b(0) = 0; in particular h_b is strictly increasing.
 (RA) The inverse g_b := h_b^{-1} admits a Taylor series expansion g_b(t) = Σ_{n ≥ 0} a_n t^n that converges absolutely on [−1, 1], i.e. Σ_{n ≥ 0} |a_n| < ∞.
 (PI(1)) Defining f_b(r) := Σ_{n ≥ 0} |a_n| r^n on [0, 1], there exists 0 < r* < 1 such that f_b(r*) = 1.

It is known that under (H), (RA), and (PI(1)), the real Grothendieck constant satisfies K_G^R ≤ 1 / r*. Two classical examples satisfying the workflow are the sign function sign : R → {−1, 1} (Grothendieck/Krivine function) and the function giving the Haagerup function in the complex case.

Problem. Exhibit an integer k ≥ 1 and a Borel measurable function b : R^k → {−1, 1}, distinct from the (one-dimensional) sign function, such that b satisfies the workflow conditions (H), (RA), and (PI(1)) above, and such that the resulting bound 1/r* is strictly smaller than the best currently known upper bound for the real Grothendieck constant K_G^R. Equivalently, find such a b that yields, via this workflow, a strict improvement of the known upper bound on K_G^R.
status_search_result: The exact value of the real Grothendieck constant K_G^R has been open since 1953. The CCP-function workflow framework continues to be actively studied (e.g., Oertel's 2024 Springer Lecture Notes and the related arXiv paper 2305.04428), and finding a non-sign function b : R^k → {−1, 1} satisfying all workflow conditions and yielding a strictly improved bound is highlighted as a persistent open problem with non-trivial combinatorial obstructions. While Braverman–Makarychev–Makarychev–Naor proved K_G^R is strictly smaller than Krivine's bound (non-constructively), no explicit b of the desired form delivering an improved 1/r* bound via this workflow is known.

original_question: Develop a structural theory of ordinary partial Bell polynomials sufficient for Taylor-series inversion problems arising from non-completely-correlation-preserving inverse functions, including closed-form or computationally effective descriptions of the Bell-polynomial values that enter the inverse coefficients β_n; methods may include high-performance computing, algebraic software, and induction principles stronger than ordinary induction when appropriate.
self_contained_problem:
For integers $n\ge 1$ and $1\le k\le n$, the ordinary partial Bell polynomial in the indeterminates $x_1,x_2,\dots$ is defined by
$$
\hat B_{n,k}(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{n-k+1}) \;=\; \sum \frac{k!}{j_1!\,j_2!\cdots j_{n-k+1}!}\, x_1^{j_1}x_2^{j_2}\cdots x_{n-k+1}^{j_{n-k+1}},
$$
where the sum runs over all tuples $(j_1,\dots,j_{n-k+1})$ of non-negative integers satisfying
$$
j_1+j_2+\cdots+j_{n-k+1}=k,\qquad j_1+2j_2+\cdots+(n-k+1)j_{n-k+1}=n.
$$
Suppose $f(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n z^n$ is a formal power series with $a_1\ne 0$, and let $g(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\beta_n z^n$ denote its compositional inverse. By the Faà di Bruno formula one has the closed-form representation
$$
\beta_n \;=\; \frac{1}{n\, a_1^n}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k\,\frac{(n+k-1)!}{(n-1)!}\,\hat B_{n-1,k}\!\left(\tfrac{a_2}{a_1},\tfrac{a_3}{a_1},\dots\right),\qquad n\ge 2.
$$

Develop a structural theory of the ordinary partial Bell polynomials $\hat B_{n,k}$ that is strong enough to yield closed-form, or otherwise computationally effective, descriptions of the values $\hat B_{n,k}(x_1,\dots,x_{n-k+1})$ entering the inversion coefficients $\beta_n$ above, in a generality sufficient to handle Taylor-series inversion of analytic functions whose coefficient sequences are not assumed to satisfy any complete-correlation-preservation property. Provide such a theory together with: (i) explicit recursive or closed-form identities for the family $\{\hat B_{n,k}\}$ that reduce the combinatorial complexity of the sum defining $\beta_n$, (ii) inductive frameworks (potentially stronger than ordinary induction on $n\in\mathbb{N}$, such as Noetherian induction on a suitable well-founded order on multi-indices) that allow the verification of structural statements about $\hat B_{n,k}$, and (iii) algorithmic procedures, possibly based on computer algebra, that compute $\hat B_{n,k}$ and the resulting $\beta_n$ efficiently for large $n$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research program on the structural and computational theory of ordinary partial Bell polynomials in the context of formal power-series inversion. While many identities for partial Bell polynomials are known in the combinatorics literature, no comprehensive closed-form theory addressing the specific inversion-coefficient problem described here has been identified, and the question is naturally open-ended.

original_question: For a Gaussian-copula parameter p with 0<p<1 and p≠1/2, determine whether there exists a function χ_p: R → {-1, 1} such that the Gaussian-copula correlation function ψ(p,p;ρ) equals h_{χ_p}(ρ)=E[χ_p(X)χ_p(Y)] for every ρ in [-1,1] when (X,Y) is a centered bivariate normal vector with covariance matrix Σ_2(ρ); equivalently, determine whether this ψ(p,p;·) can satisfy the workflow’s SIGN condition through some sign-valued function χ_p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi$ denote the standard normal cumulative distribution function and, for $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $\Sigma_2(\rho)=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. For $p\in(0,1)$, define the bivariate Gaussian copula correlation function
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{P}\bigl(X\le \Phi^{-1}(p),\ Y\le \Phi^{-1}(p)\bigr)-p^2,$$
where $(X,Y)$ is a centered bivariate Gaussian vector with covariance matrix $\Sigma_2(\rho)$ (more precisely, $\psi(p,p;\rho)$ is the standard Gaussian-copula expression that, after centering and normalizing, encodes the Pearson correlation produced by the Gaussian copula at level $p$).

For any measurable function $\chi:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ define
$$h_\chi(\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{E}\bigl[\chi(X)\chi(Y)\bigr],\qquad (X,Y)\sim\mathcal{N}_2(0,\Sigma_2(\rho)).$$

Question: Does there exist a parameter $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$ and a measurable sign-valued function $\chi_p:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;h_{\chi_p}(\rho)\quad\text{for every }\rho\in[-1,1]\,?$$

Equivalently, can the Gaussian-copula CCP function $\psi(p,p;\cdot)$ (for some $p\ne 1/2$) be realized as the correlation function $\rho\mapsto\mathbb{E}[\chi_p(X)\chi_p(Y)]$ of a $\{-1,1\}$-valued function of a standard normal variable?

The status of the problem appears to remain unresolved in the available literature.

original_question: Determine whether the Gaussian-copula approach used to generalize Grothendieck’s identity in the real case can be transferred to the complex field, and whether such a transfer would yield an analogous generalization of Haagerup’s identity for complex Gaussian random vectors.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Haagerup's identity states that for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,Z\rangle)\,\overline{\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,Z\rangle)}\,\bigr] \;=\; \langle u,v\rangle\cdot\, _2F_1\!\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12;2;|\langle u,v\rangle|^2\right),$$
where $Z=(Z_1,\dots,Z_n)$ is a standard complex Gaussian vector (i.e.\ $Z_j$ are i.i.d.\ with $Z_j=(X_j+iY_j)/\sqrt{2}$, $X_j,Y_j$ i.i.d.\ real standard normal), and $\mathrm{sign}(w)=w/|w|$ for $w\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$.

In the real case, one has Grothendieck's identity
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,g\rangle)\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,g\rangle)\bigr] \;=\; \tfrac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\langle u,v\rangle)$$
for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $g$ standard real Gaussian, and this identity admits a generalization based on the Gaussian copula construction: for an arbitrary pair of one-dimensional distribution functions $F,G$ with quantile functions $F^{-1},G^{-1}$, the correlation between $F^{-1}(\Phi(\langle u,g\rangle))$ and $G^{-1}(\Phi(\langle v,g\rangle))$ (with $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF) is expressible as a function $\psi_{F,G}(\langle u,v\rangle)$ of the input correlation, providing a "completely correlation preserving" framework that reproduces Grothendieck's identity for the choice of $\pm 1$-valued marginals.

Problem. Determine whether the Gaussian-copula construction described above can be transferred to the complex setting—i.e., whether there exists a construction, based on the standard complex Gaussian distribution, that takes prescribed pairs of complex marginal laws (or unit-modulus marginals) and an input Hermitian correlation $\langle u,v\rangle\in\mathbb{C}$ and returns the corresponding output complex correlation as a fixed scalar function of $\langle u,v\rangle$. If such a transfer is possible, decide whether it produces an analogous generalization of Haagerup's identity, recovering Haagerup's formula in the special case where the marginals are taken to be uniform on the unit circle (i.e., the complex sign).
status_search_result: A 2023 follow-up work develops a unified real/complex Gaussian framework for "completely correlation preserving" functions and recovers Haagerup's bound for the complex Grothendieck constant, applying the formalism to multivariate Gaussian copulas. However, no source explicitly resolves whether the real Gaussian-copula generalization of Grothendieck's identity transfers verbatim to the complex case to produce a full analogous generalization of Haagerup's identity. The status is therefore not clearly established as solved.

original_question: Develop mathematical objects that play the role of “non-commutative copulas” and “non-commutative distribution functions” for modeling non-commutative dependence in quantum theory, in a setting where entanglement, Bell-type phenomena, and Tsirelson-type bounds are linked to the real Grothendieck constant.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A (classical) bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ satisfying $C(u,0)=C(0,v)=0$, $C(u,1)=u$, $C(1,v)=v$, and the 2-increasing condition $C(u_2,v_2)-C(u_1,v_2)-C(u_2,v_1)+C(u_1,v_1)\ge 0$ for all $u_1\le u_2$, $v_1\le v_2$ in $[0,1]$. By Sklar's theorem, every joint cumulative distribution function $H$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with marginals $F,G$ admits a representation $H(x,y)=C(F(x),G(y))$ for a copula $C$, so copulas encode the dependence structure of pairs of real random variables independently of their marginals.

In the quantum/non-commutative setting, pairs of "random variables" are replaced by (possibly non-commuting) self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, equipped with a state, and the joint distribution function in the classical sense is generally not defined because the spectral projections need not commute. The phenomena of entanglement, Bell-type correlation inequalities, and Tsirelson-type bounds for quantum correlation matrices are quantitatively governed by the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$, which is the smallest constant such that for every $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, every real matrix $(a_{ij})$, and all unit vectors $x_i,y_j$ in a real Hilbert space,
$$\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,\langle x_i,y_j\rangle\Big| \;\le\; K_G^{\mathbb{R}}\;\sup\Big\{\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,s_i t_j\Big|:\; s_i,t_j\in\{-1,+1\}\Big\}.$$

Problem. Construct a class of mathematical objects, to be called "non-commutative copulas," together with an associated notion of "non-commutative (joint) distribution function," such that:

(i) The class reduces to the usual class of bivariate copulas (and to ordinary joint cumulative distribution functions) when restricted to pairs of commuting self-adjoint operators with a common spectral resolution.

(ii) There is an analogue of Sklar's theorem: every admissible non-commutative joint object factors through a non-commutative copula and the (one-variable) spectral distributions of its marginals.

(iii) The class supports a "non-commutative dependence" theory in which entanglement, Bell-type correlations, and Tsirelson-type quantum-correlation bounds for pairs of self-adjoint contractions on Hilbert space arise as natural functionals, with extremal/limiting quantities expressible in terms of the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.

Give precise definitions of these objects, prove the analogue of Sklar's theorem in this setting, and exhibit the link to $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.

paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
original_question: Determine whether the Gaussian structure in Grothendieck’s inequality over both R and C can be replaced by tail-dependent distribution functions, such as generalized extreme value distributions, or by infinitely divisible probability distributions, while preserving the inequality; if such replacement is possible, determine whether it can improve the lower or upper bounds for the Grothendieck constant and whether correlation matrices still suffice in the trace-inequality formulation.
self_contained_problem:
Background. Grothendieck's inequality states that there exists a finite universal constant K (depending on the scalar field F = R or C) such that for every integer n ≥ 1, every n × n matrix (a_{ij}) with scalar entries, and every choice of unit vectors x_1,…,x_n, y_1,…,y_n in a Hilbert space H over F,

   |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} ⟨x_i, y_j⟩| ≤ K · sup{ |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} s_i t_j| : |s_i|, |t_j| ≤ 1, s_i, t_j ∈ F }.

The smallest such K is the Grothendieck constant K_G^F. A standard route to the inequality realizes the inner product ⟨x_i, y_j⟩ via expectations of the form E[f(⟨x_i, g⟩) f(⟨y_j, g⟩)] for a standard Gaussian vector g and a suitable function f, and an equivalent "trace-inequality" formulation expresses the bound in terms of correlation matrices arising from such Gaussian expectations.

Problem. Investigate whether the underlying Gaussian probabilistic structure used in proofs of Grothendieck's inequality, over both F = R and F = C, can be replaced by another class of probability distributions while still yielding an inequality of the same form with a finite constant. Specifically:

(a) Can the Gaussian distribution be replaced by a tail-dependent distribution function — for example, a generalized extreme value (GEV) distribution (Gumbel, Fréchet, or Weibull type) — in such a way that the resulting inequality continues to hold with a finite universal constant?

(b) Can it be replaced more generally by an infinitely divisible probability distribution on R^d (or C^d), so that an analogue of Grothendieck's inequality is obtained?

(c) If such replacements are possible, can the resulting framework yield improved upper bounds, or improved lower bounds, on the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C compared with the bounds known from the Gaussian approach?

(d) In any such non-Gaussian replacement, determine whether the trace-inequality reformulation of Grothendieck's inequality can still be expressed purely in terms of correlation matrices, or whether one must instead use a strictly larger class of dependence objects (e.g., copulas or general joint distribution functions encoding tail dependence).
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work establishing a Grothendieck-type inequality with the Gaussian structure replaced by GEV or general infinitely divisible distributions, nor any improvement of the Grothendieck constants by such methods. The question is posed explicitly as an open research direction, and no resolution appears to be available in the literature.

paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
original_question: Suppose a sequence of pointed n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For a fixed point x in X, are all tangent cones at x homeomorphic to one another outside a subset of codimension five?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ be a sequence of pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds satisfying the uniform lower Ricci curvature bound $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} \ge -(n-1)$ and the noncollapsing condition $\mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0$ for some fixed $v>0$. Assume that $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space $(X, d, p)$.

Recall that a tangent cone of $X$ at a point $x \in X$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit of a rescaled sequence $(X, r_j^{-1} d, x)$ with $r_j \to 0$; in the noncollapsed setting above, every such sequence has subsequential limits, but the limit need not be unique.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed point $x \in X$, there exists a closed subset $S_x \subset X$ of Hausdorff codimension at least five such that, for any two tangent cones $C_1$ and $C_2$ of $X$ at $x$, the complements $C_1 \setminus \widetilde{S}_x$ and $C_2 \setminus \widetilde{S}_x$ are homeomorphic, where $\widetilde{S}_x$ denotes the corresponding subsets in the tangent cones. Equivalently, all tangent cones of $X$ at $x$ are homeomorphic away from a set of codimension five.
category_tag: Ricci limit spaces and tangent cones
status_search_result: The conjecture appears still open in general dimensions. Colding–Naber constructed examples in dimension 5 showing tangent cones at a point need not be homeomorphic, motivating the codimension-five formulation. Recent work (e.g., Wang 2024, arXiv:2405.03839) confirms a related Colding–Naber conjecture in dimension 4 (cross-sections of tangent cones are spherical space forms), and Naber's k-symmetry conjecture is connected, but no source verifies the full codimension-five homeomorphism statement for general n.

paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
context_brief: refined symmetry away from small set
original_question: Let (X, d, p) be a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit obtained as a Gromov–Hausdorff limit of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For each k ≤ n − 2, does there exist a subset Ŝ^k of Hausdorff dimension at most k such that every point x ∈ X \ Ŝ^k has the property that every tangent cone at x is at least (k+1)-symmetric, meaning it splits off at least k+1 Euclidean factors?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$, $\lambda\ge 0$, and $v>0$ be fixed constants. Suppose $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ is a sequence of pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds satisfying
$$\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -\lambda \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{Vol}\bigl(B_1(p_i)\bigr)>v,$$
and that $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space $(X,d,p)$ (a noncollapsed lower Ricci limit space).

For a point $x\in X$, a tangent cone at $x$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit $(T_xX,d_x,x_*)$ of a rescaled sequence $(X,r_j^{-1}d,x)$ with $r_j\downarrow 0$. A metric space $Z$ is called $\ell$-symmetric if it is isometric to a product $\mathbb{R}^\ell \times C(Y)$ where $C(Y)$ denotes a metric cone over some metric space $Y$.

Question: For every integer $k$ with $0\le k\le n-2$, does there exist a Borel subset $\hat S^k\subseteq X$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_{\mathcal H}\hat S^k\le k$ such that for every point $x\in X\setminus \hat S^k$, every tangent cone at $x$ is at least $(k+1)$-symmetric?
category_tag: Ricci limit spaces and singular sets
status_search_result: The standard stratification result of Cheeger–Colding (with rectifiability by Cheeger–Jiang–Naber, Annals 2021) gives that the singular stratum $S^k$, defined as points where no tangent cone is $(k+1)$-symmetric, has Hausdorff dimension at most $k$. The stronger refined statement asking for a set $\hat S^k$ of dimension at most $k$ off which every tangent cone (not merely one) is $(k+1)$-symmetric does not appear to be established in the literature; tangent cones at a fixed point need not be unique, and no published resolution of this refined symmetry conjecture in the noncollapsed setting was located in the search.

context_brief: energy identity for scalar curvature measures
original_question: Consider a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converging to (X, d, x), with Ric_j ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Let R_j dvol_{g_j} converge as measures on X. On the part of X where tangent cones are uniquely of the form R^(n−2) × C(S^1_{r_x}), with radius function r_x, must the scalar-curvature measures satisfy the energy-identity decomposition R_j dvol_{g_j} → R_X H^n + 2 θ_x H^{n−1}_Σ + 2π(1 − r_x) H^{n−2}_S, where R_X is a locally L^1 function bounded below, Σ is an (n−1)-rectifiable set with θ_x ≤ 1, and the final term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 3, and let (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) be a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian manifolds satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound Ric_{g_j} ≥ −λ for some constant λ ≥ 0, together with the noncollapsing condition Vol_{g_j}(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Assume (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space (X, d, x), and that the scalar curvature measures R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} converge as Radon measures on X to some limit measure μ.

It is known that on X there exists a subset of full (n−2)-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the top singular stratum on which the tangent cone at each point y is unique and isometric to ℝ^{n−2} × C(S^1_{r_y}), where C(S^1_r) denotes the metric cone over a circle of length 2πr and r_y ∈ (0,1] is the corresponding radius (so 2π(1 − r_y) is the cone angle defect). Denote this radius function by r_·.

Prove or disprove the following energy-identity decomposition: as measures on X,
   R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} ⟶ R_X · 𝓗^n + 2 θ · 𝓗^{n−1}⌞Σ + 2π(1 − r_·) · 𝓗^{n−2}⌞S,
where:
 (i) R_X : X → ℝ is locally integrable with respect to 𝓗^n and bounded below;
 (ii) Σ ⊂ X is an (n−1)-rectifiable set and θ : Σ → (0, 1] is a Borel density satisfying θ ≤ 1;
 (iii) S is the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X), the third term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on S, and r_· is the radius function described above.
status_search_result: No search result indicates a proof of this energy-identity decomposition for scalar curvature measures on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. The conjecture remains stated as an open problem; related results (e.g., L^2 curvature bounds, structure of singular strata, energy identities for Yang–Mills) are known but do not establish this specific scalar-curvature energy identity. Status appears open.

paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
original_question: Let γ : (−2, 2) → X be a minimizing geodesic in a lower-Ricci limit space. For s, t ∈ (−1, 1), does the normalized volume ratio along γ satisfy a Lipschitz estimate of the form ν(B_r(γ(s))) / ν(B_r(γ(t))) ≤ C(n, λ)|t − s|? In the noncollapsed case, is the infinitesimal density constant along γ in the sense that lim_{r→0} ν(B_r(γ(s))) / ν(B_r(γ(t))) = 1?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $n\ge 2$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $(X,d,\nu)$ be a metric measure space arising as a (pointed) measured Gromov–Hausdorff limit of a sequence of complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(M_i^n,g_i,\mathrm{vol}_{g_i}/\mathrm{vol}_{g_i}(B_1(p_i)))$ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -(n-1)\lambda$ (a Ricci limit space of dimension $\le n$). Call $X$ noncollapsed if it is a noncollapsed Ricci limit, equivalently if $\nu=\mathcal{H}^n$ up to a constant.

For $x\in X$ and $r>0$, write $B_r(x)$ for the open metric ball of radius $r$ around $x$, and let $\nu(B_r(x))$ denote its measure.

Let $\gamma:(-2,2)\to X$ be a unit-speed minimizing geodesic.

Question. Prove or disprove the following two statements.

(1) (Lipschitz volume-ratio bound) There exists a constant $C=C(n,\lambda)>0$ such that for all $r\in(0,1)$ and all $s,t\in(-1,1)$,
$$\frac{\nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))}{\nu(B_r(\gamma(t)))}\le 1+C(n,\lambda)\,|t-s|,$$
i.e. the function $s\mapsto \nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))$ is, up to ratios, Lipschitz along $\gamma$ with constants depending only on $n$ and $\lambda$.

(2) (Constant infinitesimal density) If in addition $X$ is noncollapsed, then for all $s,t\in(-1,1)$,
$$\lim_{r\to 0^+}\frac{\nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))}{\nu(B_r(\gamma(t)))}=1.$$
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution (positive or negative) of this conjecture on Lipschitz volume-ratio control and constancy of infinitesimal density along minimizing geodesics in lower-Ricci limit (or RCD) spaces. Related developments on noncollapsed RCD spaces, rectifiability of singular sets, and continuity of density along geodesic interiors exist, but none of the located sources state a complete proof or disproof of both parts of this specific conjecture. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

original_question: Let (M^n, g) be a Riemannian manifold with Ric ≥ −λ. Does there exist a constant C(n, λ) such that the scalar curvature satisfies the local bound ∫_(B_1(p)) R ≤ C(n, λ) for every unit ball B_1(p)?

paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
context_brief: Fixed-magnetization XXZ correlation amplitude near Δ = −1
original_question: For the ferromagnetic XXZ spin chain H = J₀ Σ_k(σˣ_k σˣ_{k+1} + σʸ_k σʸ_{k+1} + Δ σᶻ_k σᶻ_{k+1}) in the fixed-total-magnetization sector with average magnetization m̄ in (-1,1), the large-distance connected correlation in the massless phase has the form ⟨σᶻ_0 σᶻ_n⟩_c = c₁/n² plus subleading oscillatory terms. As Δ approaches −1 from above, is the coefficient c₁ asymptotic to −(1/π) sqrt((1 − m̄²)/(2(1 + Δ))) for arbitrary fixed magnetization?

Consider the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic XXZ Hamiltonian on a chain
$$H = J_0 \sum_{k} \big(\sigma^x_k \sigma^x_{k+1} + \sigma^y_k \sigma^y_{k+1} + \Delta\, \sigma^z_k \sigma^z_{k+1}\big),$$
restricted to the sector of fixed total magnetization with average value $\bar m \in (-1,1)$. In the massless (gapless) phase $-1 < \Delta \le 1$, the ground-state connected longitudinal correlation function admits the large-distance expansion
$$\langle \sigma^z_0 \sigma^z_n\rangle_c = \frac{c_1(\Delta,\bar m)}{n^2} + (\text{subleading oscillatory terms}),$$
where $c_1(\Delta,\bar m)$ is the universal amplitude of the non-oscillating $1/n^2$ part.

$$c_1(\Delta,\bar m) \;\underset{\Delta \to -1^+}{\sim}\; -\frac{1}{\pi}\sqrt{\frac{1-\bar m^2}{2(1+\Delta)}}.$$
That is, prove or disprove that this limiting form (which generalizes the known half-filling result $\bar m = 0$) holds as $\Delta$ approaches $-1$ from above for arbitrary fixed magnetization in $(-1,1)$.

paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
context_brief: TBA corrections connecting EW and KPZ expansions
original_question: Can Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz methods and their extensions compute corrections to the Edwards-Wilkinson activity-fluctuation scaling at large λ, where s = λ/L² in the diffusive regime, and can those corrections be matched to the next orders of the small-s expansion in the finite-s KPZ regime?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites at half filling. Let A_t denote the total time-integrated activity (the number of particle jumps, in either direction, up to time t), and consider its scaled cumulant generating function (SCGF)

  ψ(λ) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ exp(λ A_t) ].

Introduce the rescaled fugacity s = λ / L^2. There are two relevant regimes:

(a) Diffusive (Edwards–Wilkinson, EW) regime: λ fixed and L → ∞ (equivalently s → 0). In this regime, ψ(λ) admits a leading EW scaling form, and Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) techniques and their extensions are known to produce systematic large-λ corrections to this leading EW scaling.

(b) Finite-s (KPZ) regime: s held fixed as L → ∞. In this regime, ψ admits a small-s expansion of KPZ type, with computable subleading coefficients beyond the leading order.

Question: Develop TBA methods (and their generalizations) to compute the corrections to the EW activity-fluctuation scaling at large λ in the diffusive regime, and prove that, upon expressing both expansions in the common variable s = λ/L^2, the resulting large-λ TBA corrections in the diffusive regime match, term by term, the next-to-leading orders of the small-s expansion of ψ in the finite-s KPZ regime.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction concerning matching TBA-derived corrections to the EW activity scaling against the small-s KPZ expansion in the symmetric exclusion process. No subsequent work explicitly establishing this matching was located; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
context_brief: Relation to other exclusion-process large-deviation mappings
original_question: Can the similarity-transform mapping between the joint scaled cumulant generating functions of current and activity in ASEP models be related to previously known mappings for current large-deviation functions or for steady-state large deviations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on a one-dimensional periodic lattice of L sites with hard-core particles that hop right with rate p and left with rate q, subject to the exclusion rule that each site contains at most one particle. For a long time window [0,T], let Q_T denote the time-integrated current (number of right jumps minus left jumps across a fixed bond, or summed over all bonds) and K_T the time-integrated activity (total number of jumps, regardless of direction). Define the joint scaled cumulant generating function

  ψ(λ, μ) = lim_{T→∞} (1/T) log ⟨ exp( λ Q_T + μ K_T ) ⟩,

which can be obtained as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted (deformed) Markov generator W(λ, μ) acting on configuration space. It is known that there exists a similarity transformation W'(λ', μ') = U W(λ, μ) U^{-1} relating the tilted generators of two ASEPs with possibly different hopping rates and tilting parameters, thereby producing an exact mapping between their joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions, and in particular relating current large deviations in the ASEP to activity large deviations in the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP).

Question: Can this similarity-transform mapping between joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions of ASEP-type models be derived from, or otherwise put into precise correspondence with, the previously established mappings between current large-deviation functions of exclusion processes (such as those relating ASEP and zero-range or related processes via gauge-type transformations) and the mappings used in the analysis of steady-state large deviations of exclusion processes (e.g., via matrix-product or additivity-principle techniques)?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction in the literature on mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes; web search did not surface any subsequent work establishing a precise relation between the similarity-transform mapping for joint current–activity SCGFs and the earlier mappings for current LDFs or steady-state large deviations. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
context_brief: Open WASEP activity-conditioned symmetry breaking beyond mapped range
original_question: For an open WASEP with left and right reservoir densities both equal to 1/2, bulk asymmetry p/q = exp(2ν₁/L), and activity bias s = λ/L², determine whether particle-hole symmetry is broken when λ exceeds ν₁²/2, the range not accessible through the real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP. Here symmetry breaking means that the optimal density profile for the activity-conditioned large deviation is no longer flat.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the open weakly asymmetric simple exclusion process (WASEP) on the lattice {1, 2, ..., L} defined as follows. Each site is either occupied by a single particle or empty. In the bulk, a particle at site i attempts to jump to site i+1 at rate p and to site i-1 at rate q (jumps are rejected if the target site is occupied), with the weak asymmetry scaling p/q = exp(2ν₁/L) for a fixed real parameter ν₁. At the left boundary, particles are injected at site 1 (when empty) at rate consistent with reservoir density ρ_L = 1/2 and ejected from site 1 at the corresponding rate; the right boundary at site L is coupled analogously to a reservoir of density ρ_R = 1/2.

Let K_t denote the total number of particle jumps (in either direction, summed over all bonds, including the boundary bonds) up to time t — i.e., the dynamical activity. Tilt the path measure by the activity by introducing a bias parameter s = λ/L² with λ ∈ ℝ, weighting trajectories by exp(-s K_t). In the joint limit t → ∞ followed by L → ∞, the typical (most probable) density profile ρ*(x), x ∈ [0,1], conditioned on this activity bias can be characterized via a hydrodynamic large deviation principle.

The model has a particle-hole symmetry: replacing the occupation η_i by 1 - η_i (together with reversing the asymmetry direction) leaves the dynamics with ρ_L = ρ_R = 1/2 invariant. The symmetric flat profile ρ*(x) ≡ 1/2 is always a critical point of the rate functional. One says that particle-hole symmetry is dynamically broken at parameters (ν₁, λ) if the optimal profile ρ*(x) achieving the activity large deviation is non-flat (i.e. ρ*(x) ≢ 1/2).

It is known (via a real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP) that for λ ≤ ν₁²/2 the symmetry-breaking question is settled within an explicit parameter range. The problem is:

Determine whether, for λ > ν₁²/2, particle-hole symmetry is broken in the activity-conditioned open WASEP described above — i.e., decide whether the optimal density profile ρ*(x) ceases to be the flat profile 1/2 in this regime, and if so, characterize the transition.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open problem about the activity-conditioned open WASEP with symmetric reservoirs at density 1/2: the standard mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP requires real parameters and only covers λ ≤ ν₁²/2, leaving the regime λ > ν₁²/2 unresolved. A targeted web search did not surface a subsequent publication settling whether particle-hole symmetry is broken in this regime, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. For a given integer k >= 0 representing the number of registration marks, what are the possible lower and upper bounds on the number of construction lines that an arrangement with exactly k registration marks can determine?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. Define an arrangement to be a pair (L, P) where L is a finite set of straight lines (called construction lines) and P is a finite set of points (called registration marks) such that:

(i) every point of P is the intersection of at least two lines of L, and
(ii) every two non-parallel lines of L intersect in a (unique) point that belongs to P.

For an integer k ≥ 0, let f(k) and F(k) denote, respectively, the minimum and maximum value of |L| over all arrangements (L, P) for which |P| = k (with f(k) and F(k) defined only when such arrangements exist).

Determine sharp lower and upper bounds for the number of construction lines |L| as a function of the number of registration marks k; that is, determine f(k) and F(k) for every k ≥ 0 for which arrangements exist.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question about arrangements of construction lines and registration marks. A related paper notes that no concrete result or conjecture is known for a lower bound on the number of construction lines determined by k registration marks, and only partial empirical results for small k are reported. No general solution has been published.

original_question: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. For a given integer k >= 0, how many projectively or combinatorially distinct sets of construction lines can partition the plane while meeting in exactly k registration marks?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Define an *arrangement* to be an ordered pair $(L,P)$ where:
- $L$ is a finite set of straight lines (called *construction lines*),
- $P$ is a finite set of points (called *registration marks*),
satisfying the two conditions:
1. every point of $P$ is the intersection of at least two distinct lines of $L$, and
2. every two non-parallel lines of $L$ meet in a point that belongs to $P$ (so all pairwise intersections of lines of $L$ are recorded in $P$).

Two arrangements $(L,P)$ and $(L',P')$ are considered equivalent if they have the same combinatorial (equivalently, projective) incidence type, i.e. there is a bijection between the lines and a bijection between the registration marks preserving the line–point incidence relation (up to the chosen equivalence: combinatorial isomorphism of the incidence structure, or projective equivalence of the underlying configuration).

For each integer $k\ge 0$, let $N(k)$ denote the number of equivalence classes of arrangements $(L,P)$ for which $|P|=k$ (i.e. the lines of $L$ meet in exactly $k$ registration marks).

Determine $N(k)$ as a function of $k$, or give a closed-form / generating-function description of the sequence $\{N(k)\}_{k\ge 0}$.

original_question: For arrangements (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks in the Euclidean plane with k >= 3 registration marks, can any valid arrangement determine more than k + 1 construction lines while still obeying the rules that every point of P is an intersection of at least two lines in L and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P? Equivalently, is it true that every such arrangement has at most k + 1 construction lines?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Call a finite pair $(L,P)$, where $L$ is a finite set of distinct lines (called construction lines) and $P$ is a finite set of distinct points (called registration marks), a valid arrangement if:

(i) every point of $P$ lies on at least two lines of $L$ (i.e., each registration mark is an intersection of at least two construction lines), and

(ii) for any two non-parallel lines $\ell_1,\ell_2 \in L$, their unique intersection point belongs to $P$.

Let $k = |P| \geq 3$. Prove or disprove the following statement: every valid arrangement $(L,P)$ satisfies $|L| \leq k+1$. Equivalently, show that no valid arrangement with $k \geq 3$ registration marks can determine more than $k+1$ construction lines.
status_search_result: A web search for this conjecture about bounding the number of construction lines by k+1 in terms of the number of registration marks did not return any direct resolution or follow-up work. While related results in incidence geometry (Sylvester–Gallai, Dirac–Motzkin, supersolvable line arrangements) exist, none specifically resolve this exact upper-bound conjecture, so the current status is unclear from the available evidence.

paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
original_question: In the same setting where S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} for compact sets K_i\subseteq ℝ with 0\in K_i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and where R_z={∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i\mid x_i\in K_i} denotes the tail set, what conditions on the tails R_z guarantee that S is an interval or a finite union of intervals?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(K_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a sequence of nonempty compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ with $0 \in K_i$ for every $i$ and with $\operatorname{diam}(K_i) \to 0$ as $i \to \infty$. Define the achievement (subsum) set
$$S = \Bigl\{ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j : x_j \in K_j \text{ for every } j \Bigr\},$$
and for each integer $z \geq 0$ define the tail set
$$R_z = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=z+1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for every } i > z \Bigr\}.$$
Note that $S$ is a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ containing $0$, and that $S = R_0$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the tail sets $R_z$, under which $S$ is a (closed) interval, and conditions under which $S$ is a finite union of (nondegenerate) closed intervals.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on subsums of null sequences. Known classification results (Guthrie–Nymann, Nitecki, Banakh et al.) state that subsum sets of absolutely summable sequences are finite unions of closed intervals, Cantor sets, or Cantorvals, but a clean characterization of the interval / finite-union-of-intervals case in the more general compact-set framework via conditions on the tails $R_z$ does not appear to have been established. No publication resolving this specific question was found.

paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
context_brief: Infinite sums of middle-α Cantor sets
original_question: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the sumset formed from these K_i and R_z denotes the corresponding tail set, under what conditions on R_z and on the parameters α_i is S a Cantor set, and what kind of Cantor set can occur?
self_contained_problem:
For each $i \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha_i \in (0,1)$ and $\lambda_i > 0$ with $\alpha_i \to 0$ and $\lambda_i \to 0$. Define the middle-$\alpha_i$ Cantor set $K_i \subset [0, \lambda_i]$ as follows: start with the interval $[0, \lambda_i]$, remove the open middle subinterval of relative length $\alpha_i$, then iterate this middle-removal procedure on each remaining closed interval, and let $K_i$ be the intersection of all stages. Assume the sequence of diameters $\lambda_i$ is summable, and define the (infinite) sumset
$$S = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for all } i \Bigr\} \subset \mathbb{R},$$
together with the tail sets
$$R_z = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=z+1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for } i > z \Bigr\}, \qquad z \in \mathbb{N}.$$
Recall that a Cantor set is a nonempty compact, perfect, totally disconnected subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ and on the tail sets $R_z$ under which $S$ is a Cantor set, and characterize which kinds of Cantor sets (e.g. self-similar, central, of prescribed Hausdorff dimension, etc.) can arise as $S$.
status_search_result: The literature on subsum sets of null sequences (Guthrie–Nymann, Nitecki, and others) classifies such sets as finite unions of intervals, Cantor sets, or Cantorvals, but explicit necessary-and-sufficient conditions for infinite sumsets of middle-α Cantor sets with α_i → 0 to be Cantor sets, together with a classification of which Cantor sets occur, have not been located in the search results, and the question is posed as open in the survey on subsums of null sequences.

paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
original_question: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℂ with 0\in K_i for every i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} with tails R_z. Excluding the trivial case, what specific conditions on K_i and R_z guarantee that every algebraic number admits a radix-style representation arising from this sumset construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(K_i)_{i \ge 1}$ be a sequence of compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ such that $0 \in K_i$ for every $i$ and $\operatorname{diam}(K_i) \to 0$ as $i \to \infty$. Define the subsum set
$$S \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; x_j \in K_j \text{ for each } j \ge 1 \Big\},$$
which converges since the diameters tend to $0$. For each $z \in S$, define the tail set
$$R_z \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{j=n+1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; n \ge 0,\; x_j \in K_j,\; z - \sum_{j=n+1}^{\infty} x_j \in S \Big\},$$
i.e.\ the collection of possible tail values arising in representations of $z$.

A representation of a complex number $z$ as an element of $S$ via a choice of $x_j \in K_j$ is called a \emph{radix-style representation} of $z$ (with digit sets $K_j$ and admissible tails in $R_z$).

Excluding the trivial case in which $S = \mathbb{C}$ holds vacuously, determine explicit and nontrivial conditions on the sequence of digit sets $(K_i)$ and on the associated tail sets $R_z$ which guarantee that every algebraic number $z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ admits such a radix-style representation
$$z \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j, \qquad x_j \in K_j.$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open question in a survey on subsums of null sequences (December 2020). No subsequent literature found that resolves it; the question of characterizing digit-set/tail conditions ensuring radix representability of all algebraic numbers in this setting appears to remain open.

original_question: Consider the planar cubic rigid systems x' = -y + x(a + bx + cy + dx^2 + exy) and y' = x + y(a + bx + cy + dx^2 + exy), obtained from the rigid family x' = -y + xF(x,y), y' = x + yF(x,y) when F is cubic and the discriminant reduction has already been made. Is 2 the maximum possible number of limit cycles for this family?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar polynomial differential system
\[
\dot{x} = -y + x\,F(x,y), \qquad \dot{y} = x + y\,F(x,y),
\]
where $F(x,y)$ is a real polynomial of degree at most $3$. Such systems are called rigid because in polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ they satisfy $\dot{\theta} = 1$. After a standard reduction that removes the constant term and one further coefficient (so that the discriminant reduction is performed), one may assume that
\[
F(x,y) = a + b x + c y + d x^{2} + e x y,
\]
with $(a,b,c,d,e)\in\mathbb{R}^{5}$. A limit cycle of the system is an isolated periodic orbit in the phase plane.

Question: Is the maximum number of limit cycles that the system
\[
\dot{x} = -y + x\bigl(a + b x + c y + d x^{2} + e x y\bigr), \qquad \dot{y} = x + y\bigl(a + b x + c y + d x^{2} + e x y\bigr)
\]
can possess, as $(a,b,c,d,e)$ ranges over $\mathbb{R}^{5}$, equal to $2$?
category_tag: Limit cycles of rigid polynomial systems
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of problems on low-dimensional dynamical systems. Existing literature (e.g., works on rigid cubic systems) has produced examples with at least two limit cycles in some subfamilies and uniqueness in others, but the sharp upper bound of 2 for the full reduced cubic rigid family does not appear to be established in the available sources.

Consider the family of planar cubic homogeneous-nonlinearity differential systems

(ii) For the one-parameter subfamily
$$\dot x = y, \qquad \dot y = -x^3 + d x^2 y + y^3, \qquad d \in \mathbb{R},$$

original_question: Given integers p > q >= 2 and m,n in N, determine the maximum number of 2pi-periodic limit cycles for Abel-type equations x' = A_m(t)x^p + B_n(t)x^q where A_m and B_n are trigonometric polynomials of degrees m and n, respectively.
self_contained_problem:
Let p and q be integers with p > q ≥ 2, and let m, n be positive integers. Consider the family of generalized Abel-type ordinary differential equations
   dx/dt = A(t) x^p + B(t) x^q,
where A(t) and B(t) are real-valued 2π-periodic trigonometric polynomials of degrees exactly m and n, respectively (i.e., A(t) = a_0 + Σ_{k=1}^{m}(a_k cos kt + b_k sin kt) with (a_m, b_m) ≠ (0,0), and similarly B(t) of degree n). A limit cycle is an isolated 2π-periodic solution x: ℝ → ℝ of this equation.

Determine, as a function H_{p,q}(m,n) of p, q, m, n, the maximum possible number of 2π-periodic limit cycles that such an equation can have, taken over all admissible choices of trigonometric polynomial coefficients A and B of the prescribed degrees.
category_tag: Abel differential equations and limit cycles
status_search_result: The general problem of determining the maximum number of 2π-periodic limit cycles for generalized Abel equations x' = A(t)x^p + B(t)x^q with trigonometric polynomial coefficients of given degrees remains open. Only partial results exist: lower bounds (e.g., H_{3,2}(n,m) ≥ 2(n+m)-1), exact results in special cases such as linear trigonometric coefficients (giving 3 limit cycles for the classical p=3, q=2 case), and Chebyshev-type criteria providing upper bounds in restricted settings. Recent works (2023–2026) continue to address sub-cases rather than the full question.

original_question: Let f(t) be a continuous T-periodic function with f not identically zero and let p>0. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on f that guarantee the singular second-order equation x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t) has positive T-periodic solutions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $T>0$ and $p>0$ be real numbers, and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous $T$-periodic function that is not identically zero. Consider the singular second-order ordinary differential equation
$$x(t)^{p}\, x''(t) = f(t).$$
A function $x:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a positive $T$-periodic solution if it is of class $C^{2}$, satisfies $x(t+T)=x(t)$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $x(t)>0$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and satisfies the equation pointwise.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ (and possibly on $p$) under which the above equation admits at least one positive $T$-periodic solution.
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published characterization giving necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ for the existence of positive $T$-periodic solutions of $x^p x'' = f(t)$ for general $p>0$. Related work treats sufficient conditions or different classes of singular/superlinear equations, but a complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion for this specific equation does not appear to be known.

original_question: Consider the rational difference equations x_{n+k} = (A0 + A1 x_n + ... + Ak x_{n+k-1})/(B0 + B1 x_n + ... + Bk x_{n+k-1}) with positive-coefficient assumptions as stated in the paper. Are there periodic equations of this form that are not equivalent to the five known examples x_{n+1}=x_n, x_{n+1}=1/x_n, x_{n+2}=x_{n+1}/x_n, x_{n+2}=(1+x_{n+1})/x_n, and x_{n+3}=(1+x_{n+1}+x_{n+2})/x_n?
self_contained_problem:
Consider rational difference equations of the form
   x_{n+k} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + A_2 x_{n+1} + ... + A_k x_{n+k-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + B_2 x_{n+1} + ... + B_k x_{n+k-1}),
where k ≥ 1 is an integer and the coefficients A_0,...,A_k, B_0,...,B_k are nonnegative real numbers, with the positivity conditions ensuring that, for any positive initial conditions x_0, x_1, ..., x_{k-1} > 0, the recurrence is well-defined and produces a sequence of positive real numbers. Such an equation is called globally periodic if there exists a positive integer p such that x_{n+p} = x_n for all n ≥ 0 and for every choice of positive initial conditions.

Two equations of this form are called equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a change of variables of the form y_n = α x_{n+s}^{±1} (with α > 0 and s ∈ ℤ), or more generally by Möbius-type transformations preserving the form of the family.

The following five equations are globally periodic examples within this family:
   (i)   x_{n+1} = x_n              (period 1),
   (ii)  x_{n+1} = 1/x_n            (period 2),
   (iii) x_{n+2} = x_{n+1}/x_n      (period 6),
   (iv)  x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n   (period 5),
   (v)   x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n   (period 8).

Question: Does there exist a globally periodic rational difference equation of the above form that is not equivalent to any of the five equations (i)–(v)?
status_search_result: The global periodicity problem for rational difference equations is a long-standing open problem. Surveys (e.g., Cima–Gasull–Mañosas, "Different approaches to the global periodicity problem", 2012) discuss the classification and note that no further globally periodic examples beyond the classical short list have been found, but a complete classification has not been established. No source found that resolves the question for the full family with positive coefficients.
